9.s: atha tattvapravibhāgo vistarataḥ kathyate kramaprāptaḥ // 1
9.d: अथ तत्त्वप्रविभागो विस्तरतः कथ्यते क्रमप्राप्तः ॥ 1
9.m: Now the classification of principles, arriving in due order, is explained in detail. // 1b

9.s:
yānyuktāni purāṇyamūni vividhaibhadairyadeṣvanvitaṃ rūpaṃ bhāti paraṃ prakāśaniviḍaṃ devaḥ sa ekaḥ śivaḥ /
tatsvātantryarasātpunaḥ śivapadādbhede vibhāte paraṃ yadrūpaṃ bahudhānugāmi tadidaṃ tattvaṃ vibhoḥ śāsane // 2
9.d:
यान्युक्तानि पुराण्यमूनि विविधैभदैर्यदेष्वन्वितं रूपं भाति परं प्रकाशनिविडं देवः स एकः शिवः ।
तत्स्वातन्त्र्यरसात्पुनः शिवपदाद्भेदे विभाते परं यद्रूपं बहुधानुगामि तदिदं तत्त्वं विभोः शासने ॥ 2
9.m: Whatever these aforesaid worlds may be, that inherent, supreme form full of compact luminosity which shines within them is the one God, Śiva. / Furthermore, due to the aesthetic relish of His absolute autonomy, when difference from the state of Śiva shines forth, whatever supreme form runs through the many is a principle in the teaching of the All-pervading Lord. // 2

9.s:
tathāhi kālasadanādvīrabhadrapurāntagam /
dhṛtikāṭhinyagarimādyavabhāsāddharātmatā // 3
9.d:
तथाहि कालसदनाद्वीरभद्रपुरान्तगम् ।
धृतिकाठिन्यगरिमाद्यवभासाद्धरात्मता ॥ 3
9.m: To explain: from the abode of Kāla up to the world of Vīrabhadra, / the nature of the earth [principle] exists due to the appearance of support, hardness, heaviness, and the like. // 3

9.s:
evaṃ jalāditattveṣu vācyaṃ yāvatsadāśive /
svasminkārye'tha dharmaughe yadvāpi svasadṛgguṇe // 4
9.d:
एवं जलादितत्त्वेषु वाच्यं यावत्सदाशिवे ।
स्वस्मिन्कार्येऽथ धर्मौघे यद्वापि स्वसदृग्गुणे ॥ 4
9.m: In the same manner, [the common nature] is to be declared in the principles beginning with water up to Sadāśiva. / Whatever exists in its own effect, or in a collection of properties, or in an attribute similar to itself, // 4

9.s:
āste sāmānyakalpena tananādvyāptṛbhāvataḥ /
tattattvaṃ kramaśaḥ pṛthvīpradhānaṃ puṃśivādayaḥ // 5
9.d:
आस्ते सामान्यकल्पेन तननाद्व्याप्तृभावतः ।
तत्तत्त्वं क्रमशः पृथ्वीप्रधानं पुंशिवादयः ॥ 5
9.m: by way of a general universal, by virtue of extending and pervading, / that is a principle: in order, earth, Pradhāna, Puruṣa, Śiva, and so on. // 5

9.s:
dehānāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca na prasaṅgastato bhavet /
śrīmanmataṅgaśāstrādau taduktaṃ parameśinā // 6
9.d:
देहानां भुवनानां च न प्रसङ्गस्ततो भवेत् ।
श्रीमन्मतङ्गशास्त्रादौ तदुक्तं परमेशिना ॥ 6
9.m: Consequently, an endless proliferation of bodies and worlds does not occur; / that has been stated by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Mataṅga treatise and elsewhere. // 6

9.s:
tatraiṣāṃ darśyate dṛṣṭaḥ siddhayogīśvarīmate /
kāryakāraṇabhāvo yaḥ śivecchāparikalpitaḥ // 7
9.d:
तत्रैषां दर्श्यते दृष्टः सिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ।
कार्यकारणभावो यः शिवेच्छापरिकल्पितः ॥ 7
9.m: There, the relation of cause and effect observed among these in the doctrine of the Siddhayogīśvarī, / which is fashioned by Śiva's will, is shown: // 7

9.s:
vastutaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ karteśānaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ /
asvatantrasya kartṛtvaṃ nahi jātūpapadyate // 8
9.d:
वस्तुतः सर्वभावानां कर्तेशानः परः शिवः ।
अस्वतन्त्रस्य कर्तृत्वं नहि जातूपपद्यते ॥ 8
9.m: In reality, the supreme Śiva, Īśāna, is the agent of all entities; / for agency never belongs to what lacks autonomy. // 8

9.s:
svatantratā ca cinmātravapuṣaḥ parameśituḥ /
svatantraṃ ca jaḍaṃ ceti tadanyonyaṃ virudhyate // 9
9.d:
स्वतन्त्रता च चिन्मात्रवपुषः परमेशितुः ।
स्वतन्त्रं च जडं चेति तदन्योन्यं विरुध्यते ॥ 9
9.m: And autonomy belongs [only] to the Supreme Lord whose form is pure consciousness; / for 'autonomous' and 'insentient' are mutually contradictory. // 9

9.s:
jāḍyaṃ pramātṛtantratvaṃ svātmasiddhimapi prati /
na kartṛtvādṛte cānyat kāraṇatvaṃ hi labhyate // 10
9.d:
जाड्यं प्रमातृतन्त्रत्वं स्वात्मसिद्धिमपि प्रति ।
न कर्तृत्वादृते चान्यत् कारणत्वं हि लभ्यते ॥ 10
9.m: Insentience is dependence on a conscious subject even for the establishment of its own existence; / and causality is indeed never found apart from agency. // 10

9.s:
tasminsati hi tadbhāva ityapekṣaikajīvitam /
nirapekṣeṣu bhāveṣu svātmaniṣṭhatayā katham // 11
9.d:
तस्मिन्सति हि तद्भाव इत्यपेक्षैकजीवितम् ।
निरपेक्षेषु भावेषु स्वात्मनिष्ठतया कथम् ॥ 11
9.m: The notion 'when that exists, this arises' has its very life solely in mutual dependence; / how could it apply to independent entities that rest in themselves? // 11

9.s:
sa pūrvamatha paścātsa iti cetpūrvapaścimau /
svabhāve'natiriktau cetsama ityavaśiṣyate // 12
9.d:
स पूर्वमथ पश्चात्स इति चेत्पूर्वपश्चिमौ ।
स्वभावेऽनतिरिक्तौ चेत्सम इत्यवशिष्यते ॥ 12
9.m: If it is said, 'that is prior and then this is posterior,' / if the prior and posterior are not distinct from intrinsic nature, only identity remains. // 12

9.s:
bījamaṅkura ityasmin satattve hetutadvatoḥ /
ghaṭaḥ paṭaśceti bhavet kāryakāraṇatā na kim // 13
9.d:
बीजमङ्कुर इत्यस्मिन् सतत्त्वे हेतुतद्वतोः ।
घटः पटश्चेति भवेत् कार्यकारणता न किम् ॥ 13
9.m:
If the nature of cause and effect were [nothing more than] ‘seed’ and ‘sprout’,
why would there not be a relation of cause and effect [just as well] between ‘pot’ and ‘cloth’? // 13

9.s:
bījamaṅkurapatrāditayā pariṇameta cet /
atatsvabhāvavapuṣaḥ sa svabhāvo na yujyate // 14
9.d:
बीजमङ्कुरपत्रादितया परिणमेत चेत् ।
अतत्स्वभाववपुषः स स्वभावो न युज्यते ॥ 14
9.m:
If it is argued that the seed transforms as the sprout, leaf, and so on,
such a nature is not appropriate for that whose form is not of that nature. // 14

9.s:
sa tatsvabhāva iti cet tarhi bījāṅkurā nije /
tāvatyeva na viśrāntau tadanyātyantasaṃbhavāt // 15
9.d:
स तत्स्वभाव इति चेत् तर्हि बीजाङ्कुरा निजे ।
तावत्येव न विश्रान्तौ तदन्यात्यन्तसंभवात् ॥ 15
9.m:
If [it is replied that] it has that nature, then seed and sprout do not
rest entirely in themselves, since what is other than them completely exists [there]. // 15

9.s:
tataśca citrākāro'sau tāvānkaścitprasajyate /
astu cet na jaḍe'nyonyaviruddhākārasaṃbhavaḥ // 16
9.d:
ततश्च चित्राकारोऽसौ तावान्कश्चित्प्रसज्यते ।
अस्तु चेत् न जडेऽन्योन्यविरुद्धाकारसंभवः ॥ 16
9.m:
Consequently, this entity would absurdly have to possess such a manifold form.
If [they say], ‘Let it be so,’ no: mutually contradictory forms cannot exist in an insentient entity. // 16

9.s:
krameṇa citrākāro'stu jaḍaḥ kiṃ nu viruddhyate /
kramo'kramo vā bhāvasya na svarūpādhiko bhavet // 17
9.d:
क्रमेण चित्राकारोऽस्तु जडः किं नु विरुद्ध्यते ।
क्रमोऽक्रमो वा भावस्य न स्वरूपाधिको भवेत् ॥ 17
9.m:
If [they say], ‘Let the insentient [seed] have a manifold form in succession; what contradiction is there?’—
succession or non-succession cannot be something additional to the entity's own nature. // 17

9.s:
tathopalambhamātraṃ tau upalambhaśca kiṃ tathā /
upalabdhāpi vijñānasvabhāvo yo'sya so'pi hi // 18
9.d:
तथोपलम्भमात्रं तौ उपलम्भश्च किं तथा ।
उपलब्धापि विज्ञानस्वभावो योऽस्य सोऽपि हि ॥ 18
9.m:
Those two are merely perception appearing thus; and why should perception be thus?
Indeed, the perceiver whose nature is consciousness—he too [would be manifold], // 18

9.s:
kramopalambharūpatvāt krameṇopalabheta cet /
tasya tarhi kramaḥ ko'sau tadanyānupalambhataḥ // 19
9.d:
क्रमोपलम्भरूपत्वात् क्रमेणोपलभेत चेत् ।
तस्य तर्हि क्रमः कोऽसौ तदन्यानुपलम्भतः ॥ 19
9.m:
if he perceives in succession because his nature is the perception of succession.
Then what is that succession of his, since nothing other than that is perceived? // 19

9.s:
svabhāva iti cennāsau svarūpādadhiko bhavet /
svarūpānadhikasyāpi kramasya svasvabhāvataḥ // 20
9.d:
स्वभाव इति चेन्नासौ स्वरूपादधिको भवेत् ।
स्वरूपानधिकस्यापि क्रमस्य स्वस्वभावतः ॥ 20
9.m:
If [they say], ‘It is [its] intrinsic nature,’ no; it cannot be additional to its own nature.
If [it is replied that] succession, though not additional to its own nature, arises from its own nature, // 20

9.s:
svātantryādbhāsanaṃ syāccet kimanyadbrūmahe vayam /
itthaṃ śrīśiva evaikaḥ karteti paribhāṣyate // 21
9.d:
स्वातन्त्र्याद्भासनं स्याच्चेत् किमन्यद्ब्रूमहे वयम् ।
इत्थं श्रीशिव एवैकः कर्तेति परिभाष्यते ॥ 21
9.m:
and that it shines forth through absolute autonomy, then what else are we saying?
Thus, glorious Śiva alone is designated as the [sole] agent. // 21

9.s:
kartṛtvaṃ caitadetasya tathāmātrāvabhāsanam /
tathāvabhāsanaṃ cāsti kāryakāraṇabhāvagam // 22
9.d:
कर्तृत्वं चैतदेतस्य तथामात्रावभासनम् ।
तथावभासनं चास्ति कार्यकारणभावगम् ॥ 22
9.m:
And this agency of his is nothing other than shining forth in such a manner;
and such a shining forth occurs as the relation of cause and effect. // 22

9.s:
yathā hi ghaṭasāhityaṃ paṭasyāpyavabhāsate /
tathā ghaṭānantaratā kiṃ tu sā niyamojjhitā // 23
9.d:
यथा हि घटसाहित्यं पटस्याप्यवभासते ।
तथा घटानन्तरता किं तु सा नियमोज्झिता ॥ 23
9.m:
For just as the cloth's being together with the pot shines forth,
so does its succeeding the pot; but that [succession] is devoid of regular invariable rule. // 23

9.s:
ato yanniyamenaiva yasmādābhātyanantaram /
tattasya kāraṇaṃ brūmaḥ sati rūpānvaye'dhike // 24
9.d:
अतो यन्नियमेनैव यस्मादाभात्यनन्तरम् ।
तत्तस्य कारणं ब्रूमः सति रूपान्वयेऽधिके ॥ 24
9.m:
Therefore, when a thing invariably shines forth immediately after another,
we call that [first] thing its cause, when there is additionally an experiential continuity of form. // 24

9.s:
niyamaśca tathārūpabhāsanāmātrasārakaḥ /
bījādaṅkura ityevaṃ bhāsanaṃ nahi sarvadā // 25
9.d:
नियमश्च तथारूपभासनामात्रसारकः ।
बीजादङ्कुर इत्येवं भासनं नहि सर्वदा ॥ 25
9.m:
And the regular invariable rule has as its sole essence the mere shining forth of such a form;
for the shining forth as ‘the sprout is from the seed’ does not occur always, // 25

9.s:
yogīcchānantarodbhūtatathābhūtāṅkuro yataḥ /
iṣṭe tathāvidhākāre niyamo bhāsate yataḥ // 26
9.d:
योगीच्छानन्तरोद्भूततथाभूताङ्कुरो यतः ।
इष्टे तथाविधाकारे नियमो भासते यतः ॥ 26
9.m:
since such a sprout arises immediately after the will of a yogin;
for a regular invariable rule shines forth only when such a specific form is desired. // 26

9.s:
svapne ghaṭapaṭādīnāṃ hetutadvatsvabhāvatā /
bhāsate niyamenaiva bādhāśūnyena tāvati // 27
9.d:
स्वप्ने घटपटादीनां हेतुतद्वत्स्वभावता ।
भासते नियमेनैव बाधाशून्येन तावति ॥ 27
9.m:
In a dream, the causal nature of pot, cloth, and so forth
shines forth with regular invariable rule, free from contradiction in that realm. // 27

9.s:
tato yāvati yādrūpyānniyamo bādhavarjitaḥ /
bhāti tāvati tādrūpyāddṛḍhahetuphalātmatā // 28
9.d:
ततो यावति याद्रूप्यान्नियमो बाधवर्जितः ।
भाति तावति ताद्रूप्याद्दृढहेतुफलात्मता ॥ 28
9.m:
Therefore, to whatever extent and in whatever form a regular invariable rule devoid of sublation
shines forth, to that extent and in that form an unwavering relation of cause and effect exists. // 28

9.s:
tathābhūte ca niyame hetutadvattvakāriṇi /
vastutaścinmayasyaiva hetutā taddhi sarvagam // 29
9.d:
तथाभूते च नियमे हेतुतद्वत्त्वकारिणि ।
वस्तुतश्चिन्मयस्यैव हेतुता तद्धि सर्वगम् ॥ 29
9.m:
And when such an invariable rule establishes the status of cause and effect,
in reality the causal nature belongs only to that which consists of consciousness, for that pervades all. // 29

9.s:
ata eva ghaṭodbhūtau sāmagrī heturucyate /
sāmagrī ca samagrāṇāṃ yadyekaṃ neṣyate vapuḥ // 30
9.d:
अत एव घटोद्भूतौ सामग्री हेतुरुच्यते ।
सामग्री च समग्राणां यद्येकं नेष्यते वपुः ॥ 30
9.m:
Precisely for this reason, the totality of causal factors is called the cause in the production of a pot;
and if one does not accept that the totality of factors has a single form, // 30

9.s:
hetubhedānna bhedaḥ syāt phale taccāsamañjasam /
yadyasyānuvidhatte tāmanvayavyatirekitām // 31
9.d:
हेतुभेदान्न भेदः स्यात् फले तच्चासमञ्जसम् ।
यद्यस्यानुविधत्ते तामन्वयव्यतिरेकिताम् ॥ 31
9.m:
then diversity in the cause would not produce diversity in the effect, and that is absurd.
If [it is said that] whatever conforms to positive and negative concomitance with respect to a thing // 31

9.s:
tattasya hetu cetso'yaṃ kuṇṭhatarko na naḥ priyaḥ /
samagrāśca yathā daṇḍasūtracakrakarādayaḥ // 32
9.d:
तत्तस्य हेतु चेत्सोऽयं कुण्ठतर्को न नः प्रियः ।
समग्राश्च यथा दण्डसूत्रचक्रकरादयः ॥ 32
9.m:
is its cause, we do not favor this blunt reasoning.
And just as the complete collection—the stick, string, wheel, hands, and so on—[is the cause], // 32

9.s:
dūrāśca bhāvinaścetthaṃ hetutveneti manmahe /
yadi tatra bhavenmerurbhaviṣyanvāpi kaścana // 33
9.d:
दूराश्च भाविनश्चेत्थं हेतुत्वेनेति मन्महे ।
यदि तत्र भवेन्मेरुर्भविष्यन्वापि कश्चन ॥ 33
9.m:
we consider that distant and future things are causes in this manner as well.
If Mount Meru, or something that will exist in the future, were present there, // 33

9.s:
na jāyeta ghaṭo nūnaṃ tatpratyūhavyapohitaḥ /
yathā ca cakraṃ niyate deśe kāle ca hetutām // 34
9.d:
न जायेत घटो नूनं तत्प्रत्यूहव्यपोहितः ।
यथा च चक्रं नियते देशे काले च हेतुताम् ॥ 34
9.m:
the pot certainly would not be produced, being obstructed by that impediment.
And just as the wheel attains the status of cause in a determined space and time, // 34

9.s:
yāti karkisumervādyāstadvatsvasthāvadhi sthitāḥ /
tathā ca teṣāṃ hetunāṃ saṃyojanaviyojane // 35
9.d:
याति कर्किसुमेर्वाद्यास्तद्वत्स्वस्थावधि स्थिताः ।
तथा च तेषां हेतुनां संयोजनवियोजने ॥ 35
9.m:
so do Cancer, Mount Sumeru, and the like, situated within their own limits;
and likewise in the bringing together and separating of these causes // 24

9.s:
niyate śiva evaikaḥ svatantraḥ kartṛtāmiyāt /
kumbhakārasya yā saṃvit cakradaṇḍādiyojane // 36
9.d:
नियते शिव एवैकः स्वतन्त्रः कर्तृतामियात् ।
कुम्भकारस्य या संवित् चक्रदण्डादियोजने ॥ 36
9.m:
in a determined manner, autonomous Śiva alone attains agency.
The consciousness of the potter in bringing together the wheel, stick, and so forth // 36

9.s:
śiva eva hi sā yasmāt saṃvidaḥ kā viśiṣṭatā /
kaumbhakārī tu saṃvittiravacchedāvabhāsanāt // 37
9.d:
शिव एव हि सा यस्मात् संविदः का विशिष्टता ।
कौम्भकारी तु संवित्तिरवच्छेदावभासनात् ॥ 37
9.m:
is indeed Śiva alone, because what distinction is there in consciousness?
But the potter's consciousness, because it appears delimited, // 37

9.s:
bhinnakalpā yadi kṣepyā daṇḍacakrādimadhyataḥ /
tasmādekaikanirmāṇe śivo viśvaikavigrahaḥ // 38
9.d:
भिन्नकल्पा यदि क्षेप्या दण्डचक्रादिमध्यतः ।
तस्मादेकैकनिर्माणे शिवो विश्वैकविग्रहः ॥ 38
9.m:
is considered distinct, if it must be counted along with the stick, wheel, and so on.
Therefore, in the fashioning of each individual thing, Śiva, whose sole body is the universe, // 38

9.s:
karteti puṃsaḥ kartṛtvābhimāno'pi vibhoḥ kṛtiḥ /
ata eva tathābhānaparamārthatayā sthiteḥ // 39
9.d:
कर्तेति पुंसः कर्तृत्वाभिमानोऽपि विभोः कृतिः ।
अत एव तथाभानपरमार्थतया स्थितेः ॥ 39
9.m:
is the agent; even the bound soul's conceit of agency is the work of the all-pervading Lord.
For this very reason, since reality consists in shining forth in that manner, // 39

9.s:
kāryakāraṇabhāvasya loke śāstre ca citratā /
māyāto'vyaktakalayoriti rauravasaṃgrahe // 40
9.d:
कार्यकारणभावस्य लोके शास्त्रे च चित्रता ।
मायातोऽव्यक्तकलयोरिति रौरवसंग्रहे ॥ 40
9.m:
there is variety in the relation of cause and effect both in worldly experience and in scripture.
In the Rauravasaṃgraha [it is taught] that the unmanifest and Kalā [arise] from Māyā; // 40

9.s:
śrīpūrve tu kalātattvādavyaktamiti kathyate /
tata eva niśākhyānātkalībhūtādaliṅgakam // 41
9.d:
श्रीपूर्वे तु कलातत्त्वादव्यक्तमिति कथ्यते ।
तत एव निशाख्यानात्कलीभूतादलिङ्गकम् ॥ 41
9.m:
in the Śrīpūrva, however, it is stated that the unmanifest [arises] from the principle of Kalā.
Therefore, the explanation that ‘the markless [unmanifest] arises from the night [Māyā] that has become fractional’ // 41

9.s:
iti vyākhyāsmadukte'sminsati nyāye'tiniṣphalā /
loke ca gomayātkīṭāt saṃkalpātsvapnataḥ smṛteḥ // 42
9.d:
इति व्याख्यास्मदुक्तेऽस्मिन्सति न्यायेऽतिनिष्फला ।
लोके च गोमयात्कीटात् संकल्पात्स्वप्नतः स्मृतेः ॥ 42
9.m:
is completely pointless once this principle stated by us is accepted.
And in worldly experience, a scorpion [is born] from cow dung, from an insect, from conceptual imagination, from a dream, from memory, // 42

9.s:
yogīcchāto dravyamantraprabhāvādeśca vṛścikaḥ /
anya eva sa cet kāmaṃ kutaścitsvaviśeṣataḥ // 43
9.d:
योगीच्छातो द्रव्यमन्त्रप्रभावादेश्च वृश्चिकः ।
अन्य एव स चेत् कामं कुतश्चित्स्वविशेषतः ॥ 43
9.m:
from the will of a yogin, from the power of substances and mantras, and so forth.
If it is argued that it is entirely different due to some specific difference of its own, so be it, // 43

9.s:
sa tu sarvatra tulyastatparāmarśaikyamasti tu /
tata eva svarūpe'pi krame'pyanyādṛśī sthitiḥ // 44
9.d:
स तु सर्वत्र तुल्यस्तत्परामर्शैक्यमस्ति तु ।
तत एव स्वरूपेऽपि क्रमेऽप्यन्यादृशी स्थितिः ॥ 44
9.m:
yet it is equal everywhere, for there is unity in the reflective awareness of it.
Therefore, even with regard to essence and succession, a diverse condition // 44

9.s:
śāstreṣu yujyate citrāt tathābhāvasvabhāvataḥ /
puṃrāgavitkalākālamāyā jñānottare kramāt // 45
9.d:
शास्त्रेषु युज्यते चित्रात् तथाभावस्वभावतः ।
पुंरागवित्कलाकालमाया ज्ञानोत्तरे क्रमात् ॥ 45
9.m:
is appropriate in the scriptures, because of the manifold nature of reality shining thus.
In the Jñānottara, the order is Puruṣa, Rāga, Vidyā, Kalā, Kāla, and Māyā; // 45

9.s:
niyatirnāsti vairiñce kalordhve niyatiḥ śratā /
puṃrāgavittrayādūrdhvaṃ kalāniyatisaṃpuṭam // 46
9.d:
नियतिर्नास्ति वैरिञ्चे कलोर्ध्वे नियतिः श्रता ।
पुंरागवित्त्रयादूर्ध्वं कलानियतिसंपुटम् ॥ 46
9.m:
in the Vairiñca, Niyati is absent, [or rather] Niyati is taught above Kalā;
above the triad of Puruṣa, Rāga, and Vidyā is the pair of Kalā and Niyati, // 46

9.s:
kālo māyeti kathitaḥ kramaḥ kiraṇaśāstragaḥ /
pumānniyatyā kālaśca rāgavidyākalānvitaḥ // 47
9.d:
कालो मायेति कथितः क्रमः किरणशास्त्रगः ।
पुमान्नियत्या कालश्च रागविद्याकलान्वितः ॥ 47
9.m:
then Kāla and Māyā—this order is declared in the Kiraṇaśāstra;
Puruṣa, accompanied by Niyati, and Kāla endowed with Rāga, Vidyā, and Kalā— // 47

9.s:
ityeṣa krama uddiṣṭo mātaṅge pārameśvare /
kāryakāraṇabhāvīye tattve itthaṃ vyavasthite // 48
9.d:
इत्येष क्रम उद्दिष्टो मातङ्गे पारमेश्वरे ।
कार्यकारणभावीये तत्त्वे इत्थं व्यवस्थिते ॥ 48
9.m:
this is the order taught in the supreme lord's Mātaṅga.
The principle governing the relation of cause and effect being thus established, // 48

9.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre kathitāṃ vacmaḥ kāraṇakalpanām /
śivaḥ svatantradṛgrūpaḥ pañcaśaktisunirbharaḥ // 49
9.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे कथितां वच्मः कारणकल्पनाम् ।
शिवः स्वतन्त्रदृग्रूपः पञ्चशक्तिसुनिर्भरः ॥ 49
9.m:
we now explain the scheme of causes taught in the Śrīpūrva scripture.
Śiva, whose nature is autonomous perception, completely replete with the five powers, // 49

9.s:
svātantryabhāsitabhidā pañcadhā pravibhajyate /
cidānandeṣaṇājñānakriyāṇāṃ susphuṭatvataḥ // 50
9.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यभासितभिदा पञ्चधा प्रविभज्यते ।
चिदानन्देषणाज्ञानक्रियाणां सुस्फुटत्वतः ॥ 50
9.m:
is divided fivefold through the difference manifested by his absolute autonomy,
because consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge, and action are clearly evident. // 50

9.s:
śivaśaktisadeśānavidyākhyaṃ tattvapañcakam /
ekaikatrāpi tattve'smin sarvaśaktisunirbhare // 51
9.d:
शिवशक्तिसदेशानविद्याख्यं तत्त्वपञ्चकम् ।
एकैकत्रापि तत्त्वेऽस्मिन् सर्वशक्तिसुनिर्भरे ॥ 51
9.m:
These are the five principles named Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, and Vidyā.
Even in each single one of these principles, though completely replete with all powers, // 51

9.s:
tattatprādhānyayogena sa sa bhedo nirūpyate /
tathāhi svasvatantratvaparipūrṇatayā vibhuḥ // 52
9.d:
तत्तत्प्राधान्ययोगेन स स भेदो निरूप्यते ।
तथाहि स्वस्वतन्त्रत्वपरिपूर्णतया विभुः ॥ 52
9.m:
this or that distinction is determined by the predominance of this or that [power].
For the all-pervading Lord, through the perfection of his own absolute autonomy, // 52

9.s:
niḥsaṃkhyairbahubhī rūpairbhātyavacchedavarjanāt /
śāṃbhavāḥ śaktijā mantramaheśā mantranāyakāh // 53
9.d:
निःसंख्यैर्बहुभी रूपैर्भात्यवच्छेदवर्जनात् ।
शांभवाः शक्तिजा मन्त्रमहेशा मन्त्रनायकाह् ॥ 53
9.m:
shines forth in countless, manifold forms because he is devoid of delimitation:
the Śāmbhavas, those born of Śakti, the Mantramaheśas, the Mantranāyakas, // 53

9.s:
mantrā iti viśuddhāḥ syuramī pañca gaṇāḥ kramāt /
svasminsvasmin gaṇe bhāti yadyadrūpaṃ samanvayi // 54
9.d:
मन्त्रा इति विशुद्धाः स्युरमी पञ्च गणाः क्रमात् ।
स्वस्मिन्स्वस्मिन् गणे भाति यद्यद्रूपं समन्वयि ॥ 54
9.m:
and the Mantras—these five groups are pure in succession.
Whatever conforming form shines forth within its respective group, // 54

9.s:
tadeṣu tattvamityuktaṃ kālāgnyāderdharādivat /
tena yatprāhurākhyānasādṛśyena viḍambitāḥ // 55
9.d:
तदेषु तत्त्वमित्युक्तं कालाग्न्यादेर्धरादिवत् ।
तेन यत्प्राहुराख्यानसादृश्येन विडम्बिताः ॥ 55
9.m:
that is called a principle among these, just as the earth and so forth [comprehend] Kālāgni and the rest.
Therefore, as for what those say who, deceived by a superficial similarity of names, // 55

9.s:
gurūpāsāṃ vinaivāttapustakābhīṣṭadṛṣṭayaḥ /
brahmā nivṛttyadhipatiḥ pṛthaktattvaṃ na gaṇyate // 56
9.d:
गुरूपासां विनैवात्तपुस्तकाभीष्टदृष्टयः ।
ब्रह्मा निवृत्त्यधिपतिः पृथक्तत्त्वं न गण्यते ॥ 56
9.m:
have formed their favorite views from books without serving a guru:
‘Brahmā, the ruler of Nivṛtti, is not counted as a separate principle; // 56

9.s:
sadāśivādyāstu pṛthag gaṇyanta iti ko nayaḥ /
brahmaviṣṇuhareśānasuśivānāśritātmani // 57
9.d:
सदाशिवाद्यास्तु पृथग् गण्यन्त इति को नयः ।
ब्रह्मविष्णुहरेशानसुशिवानाश्रितात्मनि ॥ 57
9.m:
what principle is it, then, that Sadāśiva and the others are counted separately?
In the hexad called "causes," consisting of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, Īśāna, Suśiva, and the Unattached, // 57

9.s:
ṣaṭke kāraṇasaṃjñe'rdhajaratīyamiyaṃ kutaḥ /
iti tanmūlato dhvastaṃ gaṇitaṃ nahi kāraṇam // 58
9.d:
षट्के कारणसंज्ञेऽर्धजरतीयमियं कुतः ।
इति तन्मूलतो ध्वस्तं गणितं नहि कारणम् ॥ 58
9.m:
whence this half-an-old-woman fallacy?’—
that [objection] is refuted at its very root, for a cause is not [as such] counted [as a distinct principle]. // 58

9.s:
yathā pṛthivyadhipatirnṛpastattvāntaraṃ nahi /
tathā tattatkaleśānaḥ pṛthak tattvāntaraṃ katham // 59
9.d:
यथा पृथिव्यधिपतिर्नृपस्तत्त्वान्तरं नहि ।
तथा तत्तत्कलेशानः पृथक् तत्त्वान्तरं कथम् ॥ 59
9.m:
Just as a king, though the ruler of the earth, is not a separate principle,
how could the lord of a particular Kalā be a separate principle? // 59

9.s:
tadevaṃ pañcakamidaṃ śuddho'dhvā paribhāṣyate /
tatra sākṣācchivecchaiva kartryābhāsitabhedikā // 60
9.d:
तदेवं पञ्चकमिदं शुद्धोऽध्वा परिभाष्यते ।
तत्र साक्षाच्छिवेच्छैव कर्त्र्याभासितभेदिका ॥ 60
9.m: Thus, this pentad is defined as the pure path; / therein, it is directly the will of Śiva that acts, bringing about differentiation through manifestation.

9.s:
īśvarecchāvaśakṣubdhabhogalolikacidgaṇān /
saṃvibhaktumaghoreśaḥ sṛjatīha sitetaram // 61
9.d:
ईश्वरेच्छावशक्षुब्धभोगलोलिकचिद्गणान् ।
संविभक्तुमघोरेशः सृजतीह सितेतरम् ॥ 61
9.m: In order to divide the hosts of consciousness, agitated by the will of the Lord and greedy for enjoyment, / Aghoreśa creates here what is other than white (the impure path).

9.s:
aṇūnāṃ lolikā nāma niṣkarmā yābhilāṣitā /
apūrṇaṃmanyatājñānaṃ malaṃ sāvacchidojjhitā // 62
9.d:
अणूनां लोलिका नाम निष्कर्मा याभिलाषिता ।
अपूर्णंमन्यताज्ञानं मलं सावच्छिदोज्झिता ॥ 62
9.m: The greed of bound souls is that desire which is devoid of karma; / when devoid of particular delimitation, it is the ignorance of conceiving oneself incomplete, which is mala.

9.s:
yogyatāmātramevaitadbhāvyavacchedasaṃgrahe /
malastenāsya na pṛthaktattvabhāvo'sti rāgavat // 63
9.d:
योग्यतामात्रमेवैतद्भाव्यवच्छेदसंग्रहे ।
मलस्तेनास्य न पृथक्तत्त्वभावोऽस्ति रागवत् ॥ 63
9.m: This is mere capacity with respect to apprehending future delimitation; / hence, like attachment, mala has no existence as a separate reality from this.

9.s:
niravacchedakarmāṃśamātrāvacchedatastu sā /
rāgaḥ puṃsi dhiyo dharmaḥ karmabhedavicitratā // 64
9.d:
निरवच्छेदकर्मांशमात्रावच्छेदतस्तु सा ।
रागः पुंसि धियो धर्मः कर्मभेदविचित्रता ॥ 64
9.m: Through delimitation to mere portions of karma that lack delimitation, however, it becomes / attachment in the soul, an attribute of the intellect, manifesting the diversity of differentiated karmas.

9.s:
apūrṇamanyatā ceyaṃ tathārūpāvabhāsanam /
svatantrasya śivasyecchā ghaṭarūpo yathā ghaṭaḥ // 65
9.d:
अपूर्णमन्यता चेयं तथारूपावभासनम् ।
स्वतन्त्रस्य शिवस्येच्छा घटरूपो यथा घटः ॥ 65
9.m: And this conceiving oneself incomplete is the shining forth in such a form; / it is the will of autonomous Śiva, just as a pot has the form of a pot.

9.s:
svātmapracchādanecchaiva vastubhūtastathā malaḥ /
yathaivāvyatiriktasya dharāderbhāvitātmatā // 66
9.d:
स्वात्मप्रच्छादनेच्छैव वस्तुभूतस्तथा मलः ।
यथैवाव्यतिरिक्तस्य धरादेर्भावितात्मता ॥ 66
9.m: The will to conceal one's own nature is itself mala existing as an entity, / just as the external state of earth and other [elements] is non-different [from consciousness].

9.s:
tathaivāsyeti śāstreṣu vyatiriktaḥ sthito malaḥ /
vyatiriktaḥ svatantrastu na ko'pi śakaṭādivat // 67
9.d:
तथैवास्येति शास्त्रेषु व्यतिरिक्तः स्थितो मलः ।
व्यतिरिक्तः स्वतन्त्रस्तु न कोऽपि शकटादिवत् ॥ 67
9.m: Thus in the scriptures mala is established as distinct only in this sense; / but it is not distinct as something autonomous, like a cart or the like.

9.s:
tatsadvitīyā sāśuddhiḥ śivamuktāṇugā na kim /
malasya roddhrī kāpyasti śaktiḥ sa cāpyamuktagā // 68
9.d:
तत्सद्वितीया साशुद्धिः शिवमुक्ताणुगा न किम् ।
मलस्य रोद्ध्री काप्यस्ति शक्तिः स चाप्यमुक्तगा ॥ 68
9.m: [Opponent:] Why would that impurity not attach to the liberated souls and Śiva, since it has a counterpart? / [Or] there is some blocking power of mala, and that resides only in the unliberated.

9.s:
iti nyāyojjhito vādaḥ śraddhāmātraikakalpitaḥ /
roddhrī śaktirjaḍasyāsau svayaṃ naiva pravartate // 69
9.d:
इति न्यायोज्झितो वादः श्रद्धामात्रैककल्पितः ।
रोद्ध्री शक्तिर्जडस्यासौ स्वयं नैव प्रवर्तते ॥ 69
9.m: [Reply:] This doctrine is devoid of logic, imagined solely through mere faith: / for that blocking power, being insentient, certainly cannot operate of its own accord.

9.s:
svayaṃ pravṛttau viśvaṃ syāttathā ceśanikā pramā /
malasya roddhrīṃ tāṃ śaktimīśaścetsaṃyunakti tat // 70
9.d:
स्वयं प्रवृत्तौ विश्वं स्यात्तथा चेशनिका प्रमा ।
मलस्य रोद्ध्रीं तां शक्तिमीशश्चेत्संयुनक्ति तत् ॥ 70
9.m: If it operated of its own accord, the whole universe would do so, and valid knowledge would reside in an inert master. / If the Lord connects that power which blocks mala,

9.s:
kīdṛśaṃ pratyaṇumiti praśne nāstyuttaraṃ vacaḥ /
malaścāvaraṇaṃ tacca nāvāryasya viśeṣakam // 71
9.d:
कीदृशं प्रत्यणुमिति प्रश्ने नास्त्युत्तरं वचः ।
मलश्चावरणं तच्च नावार्यस्य विशेषकम् ॥ 71
9.m: then to the question, 'In what manner with respect to each bound soul?', there is no answering word. / Moreover, mala is a veil, and that does not differentiate the veiled entity.

9.s:
upalambhaṃ vihantyetadghaṭasyeva paṭāvṛtiḥ /
malenāvṛtarūpāṇāmaṇūnāṃ yatsatattvakam // 72
9.d:
उपलम्भं विहन्त्येतद्घटस्येव पटावृतिः ।
मलेनावृतरूपाणामणूनां यत्सतत्त्वकम् ॥ 72
9.m: It obstructs perception, like the covering of a pot with a cloth. / As for the real nature of bound souls whose form is veiled by mala,

9.s:
śiva eva ca tatpaśyettasyaivāsau malo bhavet /
vibhorjñānakriyāmātrasārasyāṇugaṇasya ca // 73
9.d:
शिव एव च तत्पश्येत्तस्यैवासौ मलो भवेत् ।
विभोर्ज्ञानक्रियामात्रसारस्याणुगणस्य च ॥ 73
9.m: Śiva alone would see that, and that mala would belong only to him! / Furthermore, for the host of bound souls, whose essence consists solely of the pervasive Lord's knowledge and action,

9.s:
tadabhāvo malo rūpadhvaṃsāyaiva prakalpate /
dharmāddharmiṇi yo bhedaḥ samavāyena caikatā // 74
9.d:
तदभावो मलो रूपध्वंसायैव प्रकल्पते ।
धर्माद्धर्मिणि यो भेदः समवायेन चैकता ॥ 74
9.m: the absence thereof [called] mala would effect the destruction of their very nature! / The difference between property and bearer of property, and their oneness through inherence,

9.s:
na tadbhavadbhiruditaṃ kaṇabhojanaśiṣyavat /
nāmūrtena na mūrtena prāvarītuṃ ca śakyate // 75
9.d:
न तद्भवद्भिरुदितं कणभोजनशिष्यवत् ।
नामूर्तेन न मूर्तेन प्रावरीतुं च शक्यते ॥ 75
9.m: was not asserted by you, unlike the disciples of Kaṇāda. / Nor can [consciousness] be veiled by something formless or by something with form;

9.s:
jñānaṃ cākṣuṣaraśmīnāṃ tathābhāve saratyapi /
sa eva ca malo mūrtaḥ kiṃ jñānena na vedyate // 76
9.d:
ज्ञानं चाक्षुषरश्मीनां तथाभावे सरत्यपि ।
स एव च मलो मूर्तः किं ज्ञानेन न वेद्यते ॥ 76
9.m: for knowledge extends even as the rays of the eyes undergo such a state. / And if that mala has form, why is it not perceived by knowledge?

9.s:
sarvageṇa tataḥ sarvaḥ sarvajñatvaṃ na kiṃ bhajet /
yaśca dhvāntātprakāśasyāvṛtistatpratighātibhiḥ // 77
9.d:
सर्वगेण ततः सर्वः सर्वज्ञत्वं न किं भजेत् ।
यश्च ध्वान्तात्प्रकाशस्यावृतिस्तत्प्रतिघातिभिः ॥ 77
9.m: Then, through the all-pervading [knowledge], why would everyone not attain omniscience? / And as for the veiling of light by darkness through its counteracting agents,

9.s:
mūrtānāṃ pratighastejo'ṇūnāṃ nāmūrta īdṛśam /
na ca cetanamātmānamasvatantro malaḥ kṣamaḥ // 78
9.d:
मूर्तानां प्रतिघस्तेजोऽणूनां नामूर्त ईदृशम् ।
न च चेतनमात्मानमस्वतन्त्रो मलः क्षमः ॥ 78
9.m: the resistance among entities with form belongs to light particles; there is no such [resistance] in what is formless. / Nor is a non-autonomous mala capable of veiling the conscious self.

9.s:
āvarītuṃ na cācyaṃ ca madyāvṛtinidarśanam /
uktaṃ bhavadbhirevetthaṃ jaḍaḥ kartā nahi svayam // 79
9.d:
आवरीतुं न चाच्यं च मद्यावृतिनिदर्शनम् ।
उक्तं भवद्भिरेवेत्थं जडः कर्ता नहि स्वयम् ॥ 79
9.m: Nor should the example of veiling by liquor be cited [to that effect]; / for you yourselves have stated thus: an inert entity is never an agent by itself.

9.s:
svatantrasyeśvarasyaitāḥ śaktayaḥ prerikāḥ kila /
ataḥ karmavipākajñaprabhuśaktibaleritam // 80
9.d:
स्वतन्त्रस्येश्वरस्यैताः शक्तयः प्रेरिकाः किल ।
अतः कर्मविपाकज्ञप्रभुशक्तिबलेरितम् ॥ 80
9.m: These powers of the autonomous Lord are indeed the impelling agents. / Therefore, impelled by the force of the powers of the Master who knows the fruition of karma,

9.s:
madyaṃ sūte madaṃ duḥkhasukhamohaphalātmakam /
na ceśapreritaḥ puṃso mala āvṛṇuyādyataḥ // 81
9.d:
मद्यं सूते मदं दुःखसुखमोहफलात्मकम् ।
न चेशप्रेरितः पुंसो मल आवृणुयाद्यतः ॥ 81
9.m: liquor produces intoxication consisting of the fruits of pain, pleasure, and delusion. / Nor could mala veil the soul when impelled by the Lord, because,

9.s:
nirmale puṃsi neśasya prerakatvaṃ tathocitam /
tulye nirmalabhāve ca prerayeyurna te katham // 82
9.d:
निर्मले पुंसि नेशस्य प्रेरकत्वं तथोचितम् ।
तुल्ये निर्मलभावे च प्रेरयेयुर्न ते कथम् ॥ 82
9.m: in a spotless soul, the Lord's impelling is not appropriate in that manner. / And when souls are equal in their spotless state, why would [his powers] not impel [all of them]?

9.s:
tamīśaṃ prati yuktaṃ yad bhūyasāṃ syātsadharmatā /
tena svarūpasvātantryamātraṃ malavijṛmbhitam // 83
9.d:
तमीशं प्रति युक्तं यद् भूयसां स्यात्सधर्मता ।
तेन स्वरूपस्वातन्त्र्यमात्रं मलविजृम्भितम् ॥ 83
9.m: Toward that Lord, it is proper that the majority would share the same nature. / Therefore, [mala] is simply the flourishing of the autonomous nature of the Self;

9.s:
nirṇītaṃ vitataṃ caitanmayānyatretyalaṃ punaḥ /
malo'bhilāṣaścājñānamavidyā lolikāprathā // 84
9.d:
निर्णीतं विततं चैतन्मयान्यत्रेत्यलं पुनः ।
मलोऽभिलाषश्चाज्ञानमविद्या लोलिकाप्रथा ॥ 84
9.m: this has been determined and expounded by me elsewhere, so enough of repetition! / Mala is desire, ignorance, nescience, the expansion of greed,

9.s:
bhavadoṣo'nuplavaśca glāniḥ śoṣo vimūḍhatā /
ahaṃmamātmatātaṅko māyāśaktirathāvṛtiḥ // 85
9.d:
भवदोषोऽनुप्लवश्च ग्लानिः शोषो विमूढता ।
अहंममात्मतातङ्को मायाशक्तिरथावृतिः ॥ 85
9.m: the defect of existence, the raft, languor, desiccation, utter bewilderment, / the anguish of 'I' and 'mine', the power of Māyā, and the veil;

9.s:
doṣabījaṃ paśutvaṃ ca saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam /
ityādyanvarthasaṃjñābhistatra tatraiṣa bhaṇyate // 86
9.d:
दोषबीजं पशुत्वं च संसाराङ्कुरकारणम् ।
इत्याद्यन्वर्थसंज्ञाभिस्तत्र तत्रैष भण्यते ॥ 86
9.m: it is called the seed of defects, bondage, the cause of the sprout of transmigratory existence, / and so on, by various meaningful designations in various contexts.

9.s:
asmin sati bhavati bhavo duṣṭo bhedātmaneti bhavadoṣaḥ /
mañcavadasmin duḥkhasroto'ṇūn vahati yatplavastena // 87
9.d:
अस्मिन् सति भवति भवो दुष्टो भेदात्मनेति भवदोषः ।
मञ्चवदस्मिन् दुःखस्रोतोऽणून् वहति यत्प्लवस्तेन ॥ 87
9.m: When this exists, existence becomes corrupted through duality; hence it is 'the defect of existence'. / Because like a raft it carries bound souls across the stream of suffering in this [world], it is a 'raft'.

9.s:
śeṣāstu sugamarūpāḥ śabdāstatrārthamūhayeducitam /
saṃsārakāraṇaṃ karma saṃsārāṅkura ucyate // 88
9.d:
शेषास्तु सुगमरूपाः शब्दास्तत्रार्थमूहयेदुचितम् ।
संसारकारणं कर्म संसाराङ्कुर उच्यते ॥ 88
9.m: The remaining words are easy to understand; one should infer the appropriate meaning there. / Karma, the cause of transmigratory existence, is called 'the sprout of transmigratory existence',

9.s:
caturdaśavidhaṃ bhūtavaiciatryaṃ karmajaṃ yataḥ /
ata eva sāṃkhyayogapāñcarātrādiśāsane // 89
9.d:
चतुर्दशविधं भूतवैचिअत्र्यं कर्मजं यतः ।
अत एव सांख्ययोगपाञ्चरात्रादिशासने ॥ 89
9.m: since the fourteen-fold diversity of beings arises from karma. / For this very reason, in the teachings of Sāṃkhya, Yoga, Pāñcarātra, and others,

9.s:
ahaṃmameti saṃtyāgo naiṣkarmyāyopadiśyate /
niṣkarmā hi sthite mūlamale'pyajñānanāmani // 90
9.d:
अहंममेति संत्यागो नैष्कर्म्यायोपदिश्यते ।
निष्कर्मा हि स्थिते मूलमलेऽप्यज्ञाननामनि ॥ 90
9.m: renunciation of 'I' and 'mine' is taught for the attainment of state free from karma. / For when one is devoid of karma, even though the root mala named ignorance remains,

9.s:
vaicitryakāraṇābhāvānnordhva sarati nāpyadhaḥ /
kevalaṃ pārimityena śivābhedamasaṃspṛśan // 91
9.d:
वैचित्र्यकारणाभावान्नोर्ध्व सरति नाप्यधः ।
केवलं पारिमित्येन शिवाभेदमसंस्पृशन् ॥ 91
9.m: due to the absence of the cause of diversity, one moves neither upward nor downward; / solely through limitation, without touching non-duality with Śiva,

9.s:
vijñānakevalī proktaḥ śuddhacinmātrasaṃsthitaḥ /
sa punaḥ śāṃbhavecchātaḥ śivābhedaṃ parāmṛśan // 92
9.d:
विज्ञानकेवली प्रोक्तः शुद्धचिन्मात्रसंस्थितः ।
स पुनः शांभवेच्छातः शिवाभेदं परामृशन् ॥ 92
9.m: one established in pure consciousness alone is called a vijñānakevalī. / He again, through the will of Śambhu, contemplating non-duality with Śiva,

9.s:
kramānmantreśatannetṛrūpo yāti śivātmatām /
nanu kāraṇametasya karmaṇaścenmalaḥ katham // 93
9.d:
क्रमान्मन्त्रेशतन्नेतृरूपो याति शिवात्मताम् ।
ननु कारणमेतस्य कर्मणश्चेन्मलः कथम् ॥ 93
9.m: gradually attains the nature of Śiva in the form of the lords of mantras and their masters. / [Objection:] If mala is the cause of this karma, how is it

9.s:
sa vijñānākalasyāpi na sūte karmasaṃtatim /
maivaṃ sa hi malo jñānākale didhvaṃsiṣuḥ katham // 94
9.d:
स विज्ञानाकलस्यापि न सूते कर्मसंततिम् ।
मैवं स हि मलो ज्ञानाकले दिध्वंसिषुः कथम् ॥ 94
9.m: that it does not generate a continuum of karma even for the vijñānākala? / [Reply:] Not so; for how could that mala, about to perish in a vijñānākala,

9.s:
hetuḥ syāddhvaṃsamānatvaṃ svātantryādeva codbhavet /
didhvaṃsiṣudhvaṃsamānadhvastākhyāsu tisṛṣvatha // 95
9.d:
हेतुः स्याद्ध्वंसमानत्वं स्वातन्त्र्यादेव चोद्भवेत् ।
दिध्वंसिषुध्वंसमानध्वस्ताख्यासु तिसृष्वथ ॥ 95
9.m: be a cause? The state of perishing arises from absolute autonomy alone. / Then, in the three states called 'desiring to perish', 'perishing', and 'perished',

9.s:
daśāsvantaḥ kṛtāvasthāntarāsu svakramasthiteḥ /
vijñānākalamantreśatadīśāditvakalpanā // 96
9.d:
दशास्वन्तः कृतावस्थान्तरासु स्वक्रमस्थितेः ।
विज्ञानाकलमन्त्रेशतदीशादित्वकल्पना ॥ 96
9.m: which contain intermediary states within them, in the order of their respective progression, / the designation of vijñānākala, lord of mantras, master thereof, etc., is posited.

9.s:
tataśca supte turye ca vakṣyate bahubhedatā /
ataḥ pradhvaṃsanaunmukhyakhilībhūtasvaśaktikaḥ // 97
9.d:
ततश्च सुप्ते तुर्ये च वक्ष्यते बहुभेदता ।
अतः प्रध्वंसनौन्मुख्यखिलीभूतस्वशक्तिकः ॥ 97
9.m: And hence, in deep sleep and the fourth state, manifold varieties will be described. / Therefore, how can mala, whose inherent power is incapacitated by readiness for destruction,

9.s:
karmaṇo hetutāmetu malaḥ kathamivocyatām /
kiṃ ca karmāpi na malādyataḥ karma kriyātmakam // 98
9.d:
कर्मणो हेतुतामेतु मलः कथमिवोच्यताम् ।
किं च कर्मापि न मलाद्यतः कर्म क्रियात्मकम् ॥ 98
9.m: be the cause of karma? Tell us! / Moreover, karma does not arise from mala, because karma is of the nature of action,

9.s:
kriyā ca kartṛtārūpāt svātantryānna punarmalāt /
yā tvasya karmaṇaścitraphaladatvena karmatā // 99
9.d:
क्रिया च कर्तृतारूपात् स्वातन्त्र्यान्न पुनर्मलात् ।
या त्वस्य कर्मणश्चित्रफलदत्वेन कर्मता ॥ 99
9.m: and action arises from absolute autonomy which is the nature of agency, not from mala. / But as for that character of karma, as granting manifold fruits,

9.s:
prasiddhā sā na saṃkocaṃ vinātmani malaśca saḥ /
vicitraṃ hi phalaṃ bhinnaṃ bhogyatvenābhimanyate // 100
9.d:
प्रसिद्धा सा न संकोचं विनात्मनि मलश्च सः ।
विचित्रं हि फलं भिन्नं भोग्यत्वेनाभिमन्यते ॥ 100
9.m: which is well known—that does not occur without contraction in the self, and that is mala. / For a manifold and differentiated fruit is conceived as an object of enjoyment

9.s:
bhoktaryātmani teneyaṃ bhedarūpā vyavasthitiḥ /
iti svakāryaprasave sahakāritvamāśrayan // 101
9.d:
भोक्तर्यात्मनि तेनेयं भेदरूपा व्यवस्थितिः ।
इति स्वकार्यप्रसवे सहकारित्वमाश्रयन् ॥ 101
9.m: by the enjoying self; hence this arrangement consisting of difference [ensues]. / Thus, resorting to co-operation in bringing forth its own effect,

9.s:
sāmarthyavyañjakatvena karmaṇaḥ kāraṇaṃ malaḥ /
nanvevaṃ karmasadbhāvānmalasyāpi sthiteḥ katham // 102
9.d:
सामर्थ्यव्यञ्जकत्वेन कर्मणः कारणं मलः ।
नन्वेवं कर्मसद्भावान्मलस्यापि स्थितेः कथम् ॥ 102
9.m: mala is the cause of karma by manifesting its capability. / [Objection:] Surely, in this way, since karma exists, and because mala also remains,

9.s:
vijñānākalatā tasya saṃkoco hyasti tādṛśaḥ /
maivamadhvastasaṃkoco'pyasau bhāvanayā dṛḍham // 103
9.d:
विज्ञानाकलता तस्य संकोचो ह्यस्ति तादृशः ।
मैवमध्वस्तसंकोचोऽप्यसौ भावनया दृढम् ॥ 103
9.m: how can there be the state of being a vijñānākala for him? For there is such contraction. / [Reply:] Not so; although his contraction is not destroyed, firmly through contemplation

9.s:
nāhaṃ karteti manvānaḥ karmasaṃskāramujjhati /
phaliṣyatīdaṃ karmeti yā dṛḍhā vṛttirātmani // 104
9.d:
नाहं कर्तेति मन्वानः कर्मसंस्कारमुज्झति ।
फलिष्यतीदं कर्मेति या दृढा वृत्तिरात्मनि ॥ 104
9.m: thinking 'I am not the agent', he casts off the latent impression of karma. / That firm conviction within the self that 'this karma will bear fruit'

9.s:
sa saṃskāraḥ phalāyeha na tu smaraṇakāraṇam /
apradhvaste'pi saṃkoce nāhaṃ karteti bhāvanāt // 105
9.d:
स संस्कारः फलायेह न तु स्मरणकारणम् ।
अप्रध्वस्तेऽपि संकोचे नाहं कर्तेति भावनात् ॥ 105
9.m: is the latent impression leading to fruit here, not the cause of memory; / [and it ceases] because of the contemplation 'I am not the agent', even though contraction is not yet destroyed.

9.s:
na phalaṃ kṣīvamūḍhādeḥ prāyaścitte'tha vā kṛte /
yanmayādya tapastaptaṃ tadasmai syāditi sphuṭam // 106
9.d:
न फलं क्षीवमूढादेः प्रायश्चित्तेऽथ वा कृते ।
यन्मयाद्य तपस्तप्तं तदस्मै स्यादिति स्फुटम् ॥ 106
9.m: There is no fruit for one intoxicated, bewildered, and the like, or when an expiation has been performed, / [or when one thinks:] 'Whatever austerity I have practiced today, clearly let it belong to him.'

9.s:
abhisaṃdhimataḥ karma na phaledabhisandhitaḥ /
tathābhisaṃdhānākhyāṃ tu mānase karma saṃskriyām // 107
9.d:
अभिसंधिमतः कर्म न फलेदभिसन्धितः ।
तथाभिसंधानाख्यां तु मानसे कर्म संस्क्रियाम् ॥ 107
9.m: The action of one who has an intention would not bear fruit according to that intention; / but producing in the mind a mental trace called 'intention'

9.s:
phaloparaktāṃ vidadhatkalpate phalasampade /
yastu tatrāpi dārḍhyena phalasaṃskāramujjhati // 108
9.d:
फलोपरक्तां विदधत्कल्पते फलसम्पदे ।
यस्तु तत्रापि दार्ढ्येन फलसंस्कारमुज्झति ॥ 108
9.m: colored by the fruit, an action becomes capable of yielding the fruit. / But whoever, even in that state, firmly casts off the trace of the fruit,

9.s:
sa tatphalatyāgakṛtaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ phalamaśnute /
anayā paripāṭyā yaḥ samastāṃ karmasaṃtatim // 109
9.d:
स तत्फलत्यागकृतं विशिष्टं फलमश्नुते ।
अनया परिपाट्या यः समस्तां कर्मसंततिम् ॥ 109
9.m: attains an exceptional fruit produced by the abandonment of that fruit. / Whoever, by this succession, completely abandons the entire continuum of karma

9.s:
anahaṃyutayā projjhet sasaṃkoco'pi so'kalaḥ /
nanvitthaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcidātmīyamabhisaṃdhitaḥ // 110
9.d:
अनहंयुतया प्रोज्झेत् ससंकोचोऽपि सोऽकलः ।
नन्वित्थं दुष्कृतं किंचिदात्मीयमभिसंधितः ॥ 110
9.m: through the state of non-egoity, is free of parts (akala) even while contraction remains. / Now, [someone might object:] 'In this way, some misdeed of one's own might belong to another through intention.'

9.s:
parasmai syānna vijñātaṃ bhavatā tāttvikaṃ vacaḥ /
tasya bhoktustathā cetsyādabhisaṃdhiryathātmani // 111
9.d:
परस्मै स्यान्न विज्ञातं भवता तात्त्विकं वचः ।
तस्य भोक्तुस्तथा चेत्स्यादभिसंधिर्यथात्मनि ॥ 111
9.m: [We reply:] You have not understood the genuine teaching. / If there should be an intention in that experiencer [directing it] to another just as towards oneself,

9.s:
tadavaśyaṃ parasyāpi satastadduṣkṛtaṃ bhavet /
parābhisaṃdhisaṃvittau svābhisaṃdhirdṛḍhībhavet // 112
9.d:
तदवश्यं परस्यापि सतस्तद्दुष्कृतं भवेत् ।
पराभिसंधिसंवित्तौ स्वाभिसंधिर्दृढीभवेत् ॥ 112
9.m: then inevitably that misdeed would belong to the other as well, since [the intention] is actual. / When the intention regarding the other is conscious, one's own intention would become firm.

9.s:
abhisaṃdhānavirahe tvasya no phalayogitā /
na me duṣkṛtamityeṣā rūḍhistasyāphalāya sā // 113
9.d:
अभिसंधानविरहे त्वस्य नो फलयोगिता ।
न मे दुष्कृतमित्येषा रूढिस्तस्याफलाय सा ॥ 113
9.m: However, in the absence of intention, there is no connection to the fruit for him. / The deeply rooted conviction 'This is not my misdeed' results in its fruitlessness.

9.s:
parābhisandhivicchede svātmanānabhisaṃhitau /
dvayorapi phalaṃ na syānnāśahetuvyavasthiteḥ // 114
9.d:
पराभिसन्धिविच्छेदे स्वात्मनानभिसंहितौ ।
द्वयोरपि फलं न स्यान्नाशहेतुव्यवस्थितेः ॥ 114
9.m: When the intention towards another is broken, and there is no intention regarding oneself, / there would be no fruit for either of the two, because the cause of destruction is established.

9.s:
sukhahetau sukhe cāsya sāmānyādabhisaṃdhitaḥ /
nirviśeṣādapi nyāyyā dharmādiphalabhoktṛtā // 115
9.d:
सुखहेतौ सुखे चास्य सामान्यादभिसंधितः ।
निर्विशेषादपि न्याय्या धर्मादिफलभोक्तृता ॥ 115
9.m: Regarding the cause of pleasure and pleasure itself, because of this [agent's] general intention, / it is appropriate that he is the experiencer of the fruits of righteousness (dharma) and the like, even without distinction.

9.s:
duḥkhaṃ me duḥkhaheturvā stādityeṣa punarna tu /
sāmānyo'pyabhisaṃdhiḥ syāttadadharmasya nāgamaḥ // 116
9.d:
दुःखं मे दुःखहेतुर्वा स्तादित्येष पुनर्न तु ।
सामान्योऽप्यभिसंधिः स्यात्तदधर्मस्य नागमः ॥ 116
9.m: However, the thought 'May suffering or the cause of suffering be mine' / would never be even a general intention; therefore, unrighteousness (adharma) does not accrue [to him].

9.s:
prakṛtaṃ brūmahe jñānākalasyoktacarasya yat /
anahaṃyutayā sarvā vilīnāḥ karmasaṃskriyāḥ // 117
9.d:
प्रकृतं ब्रूमहे ज्ञानाकलस्योक्तचरस्य यत् ।
अनहंयुतया सर्वा विलीनाः कर्मसंस्क्रियाः ॥ 117
9.m: We state the present topic: that for the knower free of instruments mentioned before, / all impressions of karma have dissolved through the state of non-egoity.

9.s:
tasmādasya na karmāsti kasyāpi sahakāritām /
malaḥ karotu tenāyaṃ dhvaṃsamānatvamaśnute // 118
9.d:
तस्मादस्य न कर्मास्ति कस्यापि सहकारिताम् ।
मलः करोतु तेनायं ध्वंसमानत्वमश्नुते ॥ 118
9.m: Therefore, he has no karma; towards what could impurity provide assistance? / Because of that, he attains the state of being dissolved.

9.s:
apadhvastamalastvantaḥśivāveśavaśīkṛtaḥ /
ahaṃbhāvaparo'pyeti na karmādhīnavṛttitām // 119
9.d:
अपध्वस्तमलस्त्वन्तःशिवावेशवशीकृतः ।
अहंभावपरोऽप्येति न कर्माधीनवृत्तिताम् ॥ 119
9.m: However, one whose impurity is destroyed, being subjugated by the internal absorption in Śiva, / does not enter into a state dependent on karma even though he is devoted to the sense of 'I'.

9.s:
uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca tadetatparameśinā /
malamajñānamicchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam // 120
9.d:
उक्तं श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे च तदेतत्परमेशिना ।
मलमज्ञानमिच्छन्ति संसाराङ्कुरकारणम् ॥ 120
9.m: And this very thing has been taught by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra (Mālinīvijayottara): / 'They consider impurity to be ignorance, the cause of the sprout of transmigratory existence (saṃsāra).'

9.s:
dharmādharmātmakaṃ karma sukhaduḥkhādilakṣaṇam /
lakṣayetsukhaduḥkhādi svaṃ kārya hetubhāvataḥ // 121
9.d:
धर्माधर्मात्मकं कर्म सुखदुःखादिलक्षणम् ।
लक्षयेत्सुखदुःखादि स्वं कार्य हेतुभावतः ॥ 121
9.m: Karma consists of righteousness and unrighteousness, characterized by pleasure, pain, and the like; / it indicates its own effect—pleasure, pain, and the like—by virtue of being their cause.

9.s:
nahi hetuḥ kadāpyāste vinā kārya nijaṃ kvacit /
hetutā yogyataivāsau phalānantaryabhāvitā // 122
9.d:
नहि हेतुः कदाप्यास्ते विना कार्य निजं क्वचित् ।
हेतुता योग्यतैवासौ फलानन्तर्यभाविता ॥ 122
9.m: For a cause never exists anywhere without its own effect; / causality is simply this capacity that becomes actualized immediately prior to the fruit.

9.s:
pūrvakasya tu hetutvaṃ pāramparyeṇa kiṃ ca tat /
lakṣyate sukhaduḥkhādyaiḥ samāne dṛṣṭakāraṇe // 123
9.d:
पूर्वकस्य तु हेतुत्वं पारम्पर्येण किं च तत् ।
लक्ष्यते सुखदुःखाद्यैः समाने दृष्टकारणे ॥ 123
9.m: Moreover, the causality of what is prior, operating indirectly, / is indicated by pleasure, pain, and the like, even when an observed cause is identical,

9.s:
citrairhetvantaraṃ kiṃcittacca karmeha darśanāt /
svāṅge prasādaraukṣyādi jāyamānaṃ svakarmaṇā // 124
9.d:
चित्रैर्हेत्वन्तरं किंचित्तच्च कर्मेह दर्शनात् ।
स्वाङ्गे प्रसादरौक्ष्यादि जायमानं स्वकर्मणा ॥ 124
9.m: through varied effects, as some other cause; and in this world, from observation, that is karma. / One sees tranquility, roughness, and the like arising in one's own body due to one's own karma;

9.s:
dṛṣṭamityanyadehasthaṃ kāraṇaṃ karma kalpyāte /
ihāpyanyānyadehasthe sphuṭaṃ karmaphale yataḥ // 125
9.d:
दृष्टमित्यन्यदेहस्थं कारणं कर्म कल्प्याते ।
इहाप्यन्यान्यदेहस्थे स्फुटं कर्मफले यतः ॥ 125
9.m: therefore, karma is postulated as a cause residing in another body, / because even in this life, karma and fruit manifestly reside in different bodies.

9.s:
kṛṣikarma madhau bhogaḥ śaradyanyā ca sā tanuḥ /
anusaṃdhāturekasya saṃbhavastu yatastataḥ // 126
9.d:
कृषिकर्म मधौ भोगः शरद्यन्या च सा तनुः ।
अनुसंधातुरेकस्य संभवस्तु यतस्ततः ॥ 126
9.m: The work of agriculture takes place in spring, the enjoyment in autumn, and that body is different; / but because the existence of a single synthesizer is possible, therefore,

9.s:
tasyaiva tatphalaṃ citraṃ karma yasya purātanam /
kṣīvo'pi rājā sūdaṃ cedādiśetprātarīdṛśam // 127
9.d:
तस्यैव तत्फलं चित्रं कर्म यस्य पुरातनम् ।
क्षीवोऽपि राजा सूदं चेदादिशेत्प्रातरीदृशम् ॥ 127
9.m: that variegated fruit belongs to him alone whose prior karma it is. / If even an intoxicated king should instruct the cook: 'Serve such food tomorrow morning,'

9.s:
bhojayetyanusaṃdhānādvinā prāpnoti tatphalam /
itthaṃ janmāntaropāttakarmāpyadyānusaṃdhinā // 128
9.d:
भोजयेत्यनुसंधानाद्विना प्राप्नोति तत्फलम् ।
इत्थं जन्मान्तरोपात्तकर्माप्यद्यानुसंधिना ॥ 128
9.m: he receives that fruit without [subsequent] mindful synthesis. / In this way, one experiences the fruit even of karma acquired in another birth, without any present mindful synthesis;

9.s:
vinā bhuṅkte phalaṃ hetustatra prācyā hyakampatā /
ata eva kṛtaṃ karma karmaṇā tapasāpi vā // 129
9.d:
विना भुङ्क्ते फलं हेतुस्तत्र प्राच्या ह्यकम्पता ।
अत एव कृतं कर्म कर्मणा तपसापि वा ॥ 129
9.m: for the cause in that case is indeed the firmness of the earlier [action]. / For this very reason, an action that has been done may be arrested by an action, by austerity,

9.s:
jñānena vā nirudhyeta phalapākeṣvanunmukham /
ārabdhakāryaṃ dehe'smin yatpunaḥ karma tatkatham // 130
9.d:
ज्ञानेन वा निरुध्येत फलपाकेष्वनुन्मुखम् ।
आरब्धकार्यं देहेऽस्मिन् यत्पुनः कर्म तत्कथम् ॥ 130
9.m: or by knowledge, so long as it is not yet oriented towards the ripening of fruits. / On the other hand, how could karma that has already commenced its effect in this body

9.s:
ucchidyatāmantyadaśaṃ niroddhuṃ nahi śakyate /
tatraiva dehe yattvanyadadyagaṃ vā purātanam // 131
9.d:
उच्छिद्यतामन्त्यदशं निरोद्धुं नहि शक्यते ।
तत्रैव देहे यत्त्वन्यदद्यगं वा पुरातनम् ॥ 131
9.m: be cut off? For that which has reached its final stage cannot be arrested. / But whatever other karma exists in that very body, whether belonging to the present or to the past,

9.s:
karma tajjñānadīkṣādyaiḥ śaṇḍhīkartuṃ prasahyate /
tathā saṃskāradārḍhya hi phalāya dṛḍhatā punaḥ // 132
9.d:
कर्म तज्ज्ञानदीक्षाद्यैः शण्ढीकर्तुं प्रसह्यते ।
तथा संस्कारदार्ढ्य हि फलाय दृढता पुनः ॥ 132
9.m: that can be rendered sterile through knowledge, initiation, and the like. / Likewise, the firmness of the impression is indeed for the sake of the fruit; but whenever that firmness

9.s:
yadā yadā vinaśyeta karmadhvastaṃ tadā tadā /
ato mohaparādhīno yadyapyakṛta kiṃcana // 133
9.d:
यदा यदा विनश्येत कर्मध्वस्तं तदा तदा ।
अतो मोहपराधीनो यद्यप्यकृत किंचन ॥ 133
9.m: should perish, at that very time the karma is destroyed. / Therefore, although one subject to delusion may have done anything,

9.s:
tathāpi jñānakāle tatsarvameva pradahyate /
uktaṃ ca śrīpare'hānādānaḥ sarvadṛgulvaṇaḥ // 134
9.d:
तथापि ज्ञानकाले तत्सर्वमेव प्रदह्यते ।
उक्तं च श्रीपरेऽहानादानः सर्वदृगुल्वणः ॥ 134
9.m: nevertheless, at the time of knowledge all of that is utterly burned away. / And it is stated in the venerable Param: 'One who does not take and does not cast off, who is all-seeing and intense,

9.s:
muhūrtānnirdahetsarva dehasthamakṛtaṃ kṛtam /
dehasthamiti dehena saha tādātmyamāśritā // 135
9.d:
मुहूर्तान्निर्दहेत्सर्व देहस्थमकृतं कृतम् ।
देहस्थमिति देहेन सह तादात्म्यमाश्रिता ॥ 135
9.m: would in an instant burn away everything residing in the body, whether undone or done.' / 'Residing in the body' means that consciousness, through its autonomy, has embraced identity with the body;

9.s:
svācchandyātsaṃvidevoktā tatrasthaṃ karma dahyate /
dehaikyavāsanātyāgāt sa ca viśvātmatāsthiteḥ // 136
9.d:
स्वाच्छन्द्यात्संविदेवोक्ता तत्रस्थं कर्म दह्यते ।
देहैक्यवासनात्यागात् स च विश्वात्मतास्थितेः ॥ 136
9.m: the karma residing therein is burned / by abandoning the latent impression of oneness with the body, and that [abandonment] comes from abiding in the nature of the universe.

9.s:
akālakalite vyāpinyabhinne yā hi saṃskriyā /
saṃkoca eva sānena so'pi dehaikatāmayaḥ // 137
9.d:
अकालकलिते व्यापिन्यभिन्ने या हि संस्क्रिया ।
संकोच एव सानेन सोऽपि देहैकतामयः ॥ 137
9.m: For any impression in what is unconditioned by time, pervasive, and undivided / is merely a contraction; by this [contraction] it also consists of oneness with the body.

9.s:
etatkārmamalaṃ proktaṃ yena sākaṃ layākalāḥ /
syurguhāgahanāntaḥsthāḥ suptā iva sarīsṛpāḥ // 138
9.d:
एतत्कार्ममलं प्रोक्तं येन साकं लयाकलाः ।
स्युर्गुहागहनान्तःस्थाः सुप्ता इव सरीसृपाः ॥ 138
9.m: This has been declared to be the impurity of action (kārma mala), together with which the souls free of instruments in dissolution (layākala) / abide like serpents asleep inside a dense cave.

9.s:
tataḥ prabuddhasaṃskārāste yathocitabhāginaḥ /
brahmādisthāvarānte'smin saṃsranti punaḥ punaḥ // 139
9.d:
ततः प्रबुद्धसंस्कारास्ते यथोचितभागिनः ।
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेऽस्मिन् संस्रन्ति पुनः पुनः ॥ 139
9.m: Then, their impressions awakened, receiving their appropriate share, / they transmigrate again and again in this world from Brahmā down to immobile things.

9.s:
ye punaḥ karmasaṃskārahānyai prārabdhabhāvanāḥ /
bhāvanāpariniṣpattimaprāpya pralayaṃ gatāḥ // 140
9.d:
ये पुनः कर्मसंस्कारहान्यै प्रारब्धभावनाः ।
भावनापरिनिष्पत्तिमप्राप्य प्रलयं गताः ॥ 140
9.m: On the other hand, those who commenced contemplation for the destruction of karmic impressions, / but underwent dissolution before reaching the perfection of contemplation,

9.s:
mahāntaṃ te tathāntaḥsthabhāvanāpākasauṣṭhavāt /
mantratvaṃ pratipadyante citrāccitraṃ ca karmataḥ // 141
9.d:
महान्तं ते तथान्तःस्थभावनापाकसौष्ठवात् ।
मन्त्रत्वं प्रतिपद्यन्ते चित्राच्चित्रं च कर्मतः ॥ 141
9.m: owing to the excellence of the ripening of their internal contemplation, / attain the status of Mantras and diverse states from diverse karma in the great [dissolution].

9.s:
asya kārmamalasyeyanmāyāntādhvavisāriṇaḥ /
pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ proktamajñānātmāṇavo malaḥ // 142
9.d:
अस्य कार्ममलस्येयन्मायान्ताध्वविसारिणः ।
प्रधानं कारणं प्रोक्तमज्ञानात्माणवो मलः ॥ 142
9.m: Of this impurity of action, which extends across the path ending in Māyā, / the primary cause is declared to be the innate impurity (āṇava mala), which consists of ignorance.

9.s:
kṣobho'sya lolikākhyasya sahakāritayā sphuṭam /
tiṣṭhāsāyogyataunmukhyamīśvarecchāvaśācca tat // 143
9.d:
क्षोभोऽस्य लोलिकाख्यस्य सहकारितया स्फुटम् ।
तिष्ठासायोग्यतौन्मुख्यमीश्वरेच्छावशाच्च तत् ॥ 143
9.m: The agitation of this [Māyā] is called lolikā, clearly acting as an auxiliary cause; / it is the readiness and orientation to abide, and that arises through the will of the Lord.

9.s:
na jaḍaścidadhiṣṭhānaṃ vinā kvāpi kṣamo yataḥ /
aṇavo nāma naivānyatprakāśātmā maheśvaraḥ // 144
9.d:
न जडश्चिदधिष्ठानं विना क्वापि क्षमो यतः ।
अणवो नाम नैवान्यत्प्रकाशात्मा महेश्वरः ॥ 144
9.m: For what is inert is never capable anywhere without the presiding of consciousness. / The individual souls (aṇu) are indeed nothing other than the Great Lord whose nature is luminosity.

9.s:
cidacidrūpatābhāsī pudgalaḥ kṣetravitpaśuḥ /
cidrūpatvācca sa vyāpī nirguṇo niṣkriyastataḥ // 145
9.d:
चिदचिद्रूपताभासी पुद्गलः क्षेत्रवित्पशुः ।
चिद्रूपत्वाच्च स व्यापी निर्गुणो निष्क्रियस्ततः ॥ 145
9.m: Appearing as both conscious and unconscious, he is the individual soul (pudgala), the knower of the field, the bound soul (paśu). / And because his nature is consciousness, he is pervasive, devoid of qualities, and therefore inactive.

9.s:
yogopāyepsako nityo mūrtivandhyaḥ prabhāṣyate /
acittvādajñatā bhedo bhogyādbhoktrantarādatha // 146
9.d:
योगोपायेप्सको नित्यो मूर्तिवन्ध्यः प्रभाष्यते ।
अचित्त्वादज्ञता भेदो भोग्याद्भोक्त्रन्तरादथ ॥ 146
9.m: He is described as seeking the means of yoga, eternal, and free of bodily form. / Because of the unconscious aspect, there is ignorance and difference from what is enjoyed and from another experiencer.

9.s:
teṣāmaṇūnāṃ sa mala īśvarecchāvaśādbhṛśam /
prabudhyate tathā coktaṃ śāstre śrīpūrvanāmani // 147
9.d:
तेषामणूनां स मल ईश्वरेच्छावशाद्भृशम् ।
प्रबुध्यते तथा चोक्तं शास्त्रे श्रीपूर्वनामनि ॥ 147
9.m: Through the will of the Lord, that impurity of those individual souls / is intensely awakened; and so it has been said in the scripture named the venerable Pūrva (Mālinīvijayottara):

9.s:
īśvarecchāvaśādasya bhogecchā saṃprajāyate /
bhogecchorupakārārthamādyo mantramaheśvaraḥ // 148
9.d:
ईश्वरेच्छावशादस्य भोगेच्छा संप्रजायते ।
भोगेच्छोरुपकारार्थमाद्यो मन्त्रमहेश्वरः ॥ 148
9.m: 'Under the influence of the will of the Lord, the desire for enjoyment arises in him.' / For the benefit of the one who desires enjoyment, the first Lord of Mantras (Mantramaheśvara),

9.s:
māyāṃ vikṣobhya saṃsāraṃ nirmimīte vicitrakam /
māyā ca nāma devasya śaktiravyatirekiṇī // 149
9.d:
मायां विक्षोभ्य संसारं निर्मिमीते विचित्रकम् ।
माया च नाम देवस्य शक्तिरव्यतिरेकिणी ॥ 149
9.m: having agitated Māyā, creates the manifold transmigratory world. / And Māyā is the inseparable power of the Lord,

9.s:
bhedāvabhāsasvātantryaṃ tathāhi sa tayā kṛtaḥ /
ādyo bhedāvabhāso yo vibhāgamanupeyivān // 150
9.d:
भेदावभासस्वातन्त्र्यं तथाहि स तया कृतः ।
आद्यो भेदावभासो यो विभागमनुपेयिवान् ॥ 150
9.m: the absolute autonomy of the manifestation of difference. For it is thus that he was made by Her. / The initial manifestation of difference, which has not yet attained distinction,

9.s:
garbhīkṛtānantabhāvivibhāsā sā parā niśā /
sā jaḍā bhedarūpatvāt kāryaṃ cāsyā jaḍaṃ yataḥ // 151
9.d:
गर्भीकृतानन्तभाविविभासा सा परा निशा ।
सा जडा भेदरूपत्वात् कार्यं चास्या जडं यतः ॥ 151
9.m: and which contains within itself the infinite future manifestations, is the supreme night. / That [night] is inert because its nature is difference, for its effect is inert.

9.s:
vyāpinī viśvahetutvāt sūkṣmā kāryaikakalpanāt /
śivaśaktyavinābhāvānnityaikā mūlakāraṇam // 152
9.d:
व्यापिनी विश्वहेतुत्वात् सूक्ष्मा कार्यैककल्पनात् ।
शिवशक्त्यविनाभावान्नित्यैका मूलकारणम् ॥ 152
9.m: It is all-pervading because it is the cause of all; it is subtle because it is inferred only from its effect; / because it is inseparable from the power of Śiva, it is eternal, single, and the root cause.

9.s:
acetanamanekātma sarva kārya yathā ghaṭaḥ /
pradhānaṃ ca tathā tasmāt kārya nātmā tu cetanaḥ // 153
9.d:
अचेतनमनेकात्म सर्व कार्य यथा घटः ।
प्रधानं च तथा तस्मात् कार्य नात्मा तु चेतनः ॥ 153
9.m: Every effect is insentient and plural, like a pot, / and pradhāna is like that. Therefore [pradhāna] is an effect; the conscious self, however, is not.

9.s:
ata evādhvani proktā pūrvaṃ māyā dvidhā sthitā /
yathā ca māyā devasya śaktirabhyeti bhedinam // 154
9.d:
अत एवाध्वनि प्रोक्ता पूर्वं माया द्विधा स्थिता ।
यथा च माया देवस्य शक्तिरभ्येति भेदिनम् ॥ 154
9.m: For this very reason, māyā was previously stated to exist in two ways in the path. / And just as māyā, the power of the Lord, takes on the state of an differentiated

9.s:
tattvabhāvaṃ tathānyo'pi kalādistattvavistaraḥ /
niruddhaśakteryā kiṃcitkartṛtodvalanātmikā // 155
9.d:
तत्त्वभावं तथान्योऽपि कलादिस्तत्त्वविस्तरः ।
निरुद्धशक्तेर्या किंचित्कर्तृतोद्वलनात्मिका ॥ 155
9.m: tattva, so too does the rest of the expansion of tattvas, beginning with kalā. / That power of the Lord which—for [the soul] whose capacity is obstructed—consists in stimulating limited agency,

9.s:
nāthasya śaktiḥ sādhastātpuṃsaḥ kṣeptrī kalocyate /
evaṃ vidyādayo'pyete dharāntāḥ paramārthataḥ // 156
9.d:
नाथस्य शक्तिः साधस्तात्पुंसः क्षेप्त्री कलोच्यते ।
एवं विद्यादयोऽप्येते धरान्ताः परमार्थतः ॥ 156
9.m: and which casts the puruṣa down, is called kalā. / In this way, even these [tattvas] beginning with vidyā down to the earth are in the ultimate sense

9.s:
śivaśaktimayā eva proktanyāyānusārataḥ /
tathāpi yatpṛthagbhānaṃ kalāderīśvarecchayā // 157
9.d:
शिवशक्तिमया एव प्रोक्तन्यायानुसारतः ।
तथापि यत्पृथग्भानं कलादेरीश्वरेच्छया ॥ 157
9.m: identical with the power of Śiva, in accordance with the previously stated reasoning. / Nevertheless, the separate appearance of kalā and the rest through the will of the Lord

9.s:
tato jaḍatve kāryatve pṛthaktattvasthitau dhruvam /
upādānaṃ smṛtā māyā kvacittatkāryameva ca // 158
9.d:
ततो जडत्वे कार्यत्वे पृथक्तत्त्वस्थितौ ध्रुवम् ।
उपादानं स्मृता माया क्वचित्तत्कार्यमेव च ॥ 158
9.m: is the reason why, in being insentient, being effects, and existing as distinct tattvas, / māyā is indeed remembered as the material cause, and sometimes its effect itself is so.

9.s:
tathāvabhāsacitraṃ ca rūpamanyonyavarjitam /
yadbhāti kila saṃkalpe tadasti ghaṭavadvahiḥ // 159
9.d:
तथावभासचित्रं च रूपमन्योन्यवर्जितम् ।
यद्भाति किल संकल्पे तदस्ति घटवद्वहिः ॥ 159
9.m: So too, a form that is variegated in its manifestation and mutually exclusive, / which appears within conception, truly exists externally like a pot.

9.s:
khapuṣpādyastitāṃ brūmastato na vyabhicāritā /
khapuṣpaṃ kāladiṅmātṛsāpekṣaṃ nāstiśabdataḥ // 160
9.d:
खपुष्पाद्यस्तितां ब्रूमस्ततो न व्यभिचारिता ।
खपुष्पं कालदिङ्मातृसापेक्षं नास्तिशब्दतः ॥ 160
9.m: We assert that even an empty-flower and the like have existence; therefore there is no deviation. / An empty-flower is [said] not to exist through the word 'is not' relative to time, space, and a cognizer,

9.s:
dharādivat tathātyantābhāvo'pyevaṃ vivicyatām /
yatsaṃkalpyaṃ tathā tasya bahirdeho'sti cetanaḥ // 161
9.d:
धरादिवत् तथात्यन्ताभावोऽप्येवं विविच्यताम् ।
यत्संकल्प्यं तथा तस्य बहिर्देहोऽस्ति चेतनः ॥ 161
9.m: just like the earth and the like. Absolute non-existence should also be examined in this way. / That which is conceivable in this way has a conscious body outside,

9.s:
caitravatsauśivāntaṃ tat sarva tādṛśadehavat /
yasya deho yathā tasya tajjātīyaṃ puraṃ bahiḥ // 162
9.d:
चैत्रवत्सौशिवान्तं तत् सर्व तादृशदेहवत् ।
यस्य देहो यथा तस्य तज्जातीयं पुरं बहिः ॥ 162
9.m: like Caitra; all that up to Suśiva has such a body. / Whatever body one has, outside of it is an abode of that same class.

9.s:
ataḥ suśivaparyantā siddhā bhuvanapaddhatiḥ /
ātmanām tatpuraṃ prāpyaṃ deśatvādanyadeśavat // 163
9.d:
अतः सुशिवपर्यन्ता सिद्धा भुवनपद्धतिः ।
आत्मनाम् तत्पुरं प्राप्यं देशत्वादन्यदेशवत् ॥ 163
9.m: Therefore, the series of worlds extending up to Suśiva is established. / That city is to be reached by souls because it is a place, like any other place.

9.s:
ātmanāmadhvabhoktṛtvaṃ tato'yatnena siddhyati /
sā māyā kṣobhamāpannā viśvaṃ sūte samantataḥ // 164
9.d:
आत्मनामध्वभोक्तृत्वं ततोऽयत्नेन सिद्ध्यति ।
सा माया क्षोभमापन्ना विश्वं सूते समन्ततः ॥ 164
9.m: Hence, the souls' status as enjoyers of the path is established effortlessly. / That māyā, undergoing agitation, brings forth the universe on every side,

9.s:
daṇḍāhatevāmalakī phalāni kila yadyapi /
tathāpi tu tathā citrapaurvāparyāvabhāsanāt // 165
9.d:
दण्डाहतेवामलकी फलानि किल यद्यपि ।
तथापि तु तथा चित्रपौर्वापर्यावभासनात् ॥ 165
9.m: just as an āmalakī tree struck with a stick [brings forth] fruits, indeed, although / even so, by appearing in such variegated succession,

9.s:
māyākārye'pi tattvaughe kāryakāraṇatā mithaḥ /
sā yadyapyanyaśāstreṣu bahudhā dṛśyate sphuṭam // 166
9.d:
मायाकार्येऽपि तत्त्वौघे कार्यकारणता मिथः ।
सा यद्यप्यन्यशास्त्रेषु बहुधा दृश्यते स्फुटम् ॥ 166
9.m: even in the mass of tattvas that are the effects of māyā, there is mutual cause-and-effect relation. / Although this is clearly seen in many ways in other scriptures,

9.s:
tathāpi mālinīśāstradṛśā tāṃ saṃpracakṣmahe /
kalādivasudhāntaṃ yanmāyāntaḥ saṃpracakṣate // 167
9.d:
तथापि मालिनीशास्त्रदृशा तां संप्रचक्ष्महे ।
कलादिवसुधान्तं यन्मायान्तः संप्रचक्षते ॥ 167
9.m: nonetheless we explain it according to the perspective of the Mālinīvijayottara. / What they explain within māyā, beginning with kalā and ending with the earth,

9.s:
pratyātmabhinnamevaitat sukhaduḥkhādibhedataḥ /
ekasyāmeva jagati bhogasādhanasaṃhatau // 168
9.d:
प्रत्यात्मभिन्नमेवैतत् सुखदुःखादिभेदतः ।
एकस्यामेव जगति भोगसाधनसंहतौ ॥ 168
9.m: is distinct for each individual soul, on account of the distinction of pleasure, pain, and the like. / In the single world, amidst the collection of instruments of enjoyment,

9.s:
sukhādīnāṃ samaṃ vyakterbhogabhedaḥ kuto bhavet /
na cāsau karmabhedena tasyaivānupapattitaḥ // 169
9.d:
सुखादीनां समं व्यक्तेर्भोगभेदः कुतो भवेत् ।
न चासौ कर्मभेदेन तस्यैवानुपपत्तितः ॥ 169
9.m: since pleasure and the rest are manifest equally, whence would arise difference in enjoyment? / Nor is this [difference] due to difference in karma, for that itself would be inexplicable.

9.s:
tasmāt kalādiko vargo bhinna eva kadācana /
aikyametīśvarecchāto nṛttagītādivādane // 170
9.d:
तस्मात् कलादिको वर्गो भिन्न एव कदाचन ।
ऐक्यमेतीश्वरेच्छातो नृत्तगीतादिवादने ॥ 170
9.m: Therefore, the group beginning with kalā is indeed distinct; at times / it attains unity through the will of the Lord, as in the performance of dance, song, and the like.

9.s:
eṣāṃ kalāditattvānāṃ sarveṣāmapi bhāvinām /
śuddhatvamasti teṣāṃ ye śaktipātapavitritāḥ // 171
9.d:
एषां कलादितत्त्वानां सर्वेषामपि भाविनाम् ।
शुद्धत्वमस्ति तेषां ये शक्तिपातपवित्रिताः ॥ 171
9.m: For all these existing tattvas beginning with kalā, / there is purity for those who have been purified by the descent of power.

9.s:
kalā hi śuddhā tattādṛk karmatvaṃ saṃprasūyate /
mitamapyāśu yenāsmāt saṃsārādeṣa mucyate // 172
9.d:
कला हि शुद्धा तत्तादृक् कर्मत्वं संप्रसूयते ।
मितमप्याशु येनास्मात् संसारादेष मुच्यते ॥ 172
9.m: For when kalā is pure, it brings forth that kind of state of action, / though limited, by which one is swiftly liberated from this saṃsāra.

9.s:
rāgavidyākālayatiprakṛtyakṣārthasaṃcayaḥ /
itthaṃ śuddha iti procya gururmānastutau vibhuḥ // 173
9.d:
रागविद्याकालयतिप्रकृत्यक्षार्थसंचयः ।
इत्थं शुद्ध इति प्रोच्य गुरुर्मानस्तुतौ विभुः ॥ 173
9.m: The collection consisting of rāga, vidyā, kāla, niyati, prakṛti, the senses, and objects / is thus pure; having declared this, the omnipresent guru in the hymn of the instruments of knowledge [said]:

9.s:
evameṣā kalādīnāmutpattiḥ pravivicyate /
māyātattvāt kalā jātā kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇā // 174
9.d:
एवमेषा कलादीनामुत्पत्तिः प्रविविच्यते ।
मायातत्त्वात् कला जाता किंचित्कर्तृत्वलक्षणा ॥ 174
9.m: In this way, this emergence of kalā and the rest is clearly discerned. / From the māyā-tattva arose kalā, characterized by limited agency.

9.s:
māyā hi cinmayādbhedaṃ śivādvidadhatī paśoḥ /
suṣuptatāmivādhatte tata eva hyadṛkkriyaḥ // 175
9.d:
माया हि चिन्मयाद्भेदं शिवाद्विदधती पशोः ।
सुषुप्ततामिवाधत्ते तत एव ह्यदृक्क्रियः ॥ 175
9.m: For māyā, producing the bound soul's separation from Śiva who is composed of consciousness, / brings about as it were a state of deep sleep; for that very reason, he is devoid of perception and action.

9.s:
kalā hi kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ sūte svāliṅganādaṇoḥ /
tasyāścāpyaṇunānyonyaṃ hyañjane sā prasūyate // 176
9.d:
कला हि किंचित्कर्तृत्वं सूते स्वालिङ्गनादणोः ।
तस्याश्चाप्यणुनान्योन्यं ह्यञ्जने सा प्रसूयते ॥ 176
9.m: Kalā indeed generates limited agency by embracing the atom; / and when it is mutually tainted by the atom, it brings [effects] forth.

9.s:
sadyonirvāṇadīkṣotthapuṃviśleṣe hi sā satī /
śliṣyantyapi ca no sūte tathāpi svaphalaṃ kvacit // 177
9.d:
सद्योनिर्वाणदीक्षोत्थपुंविश्लेषे हि सा सती ।
श्लिष्यन्त्यपि च नो सूते तथापि स्वफलं क्वचित् ॥ 177
9.m: Indeed, when there is detachment of the soul arising from immediate-liberation initiation, even if it persists, / and even if it embraces, it never produces its fruit.

9.s:
ucchūnateva prathamā sūkṣmāṅkurakaleva ca /
bījasyāmbvagnimṛtkambutuṣayogāt prasūtikṛt // 178
9.d:
उच्छूनतेव प्रथमा सूक्ष्माङ्कुरकलेव च ।
बीजस्याम्ब्वग्निमृत्कम्बुतुषयोगात् प्रसूतिकृत् ॥ 178
9.m: Just like the first swelling and like the subtle sprout-portion / of a seed brings about generation through contact with water, heat, soil, shell, and chaff,

9.s:
kalā māyāṇusaṃyogajāpyeṣā nirvikārakam /
nāṇuṃ kuryādupādānaṃ kiṃtu māyāṃ vikāriṇīm // 179
9.d:
कला मायाणुसंयोगजाप्येषा निर्विकारकम् ।
नाणुं कुर्यादुपादानं किंतु मायां विकारिणीम् ॥ 179
9.m: so kalā, even though arisen from the contact of māyā and the atom, / does not make the immutable atom its material cause, but rather mutable māyā.

9.s:
malaścāvārako māyā bhāvopādānakāraṇam /
karma syāt sahakāryeva sukhaduḥkhodbhavaṃ prati // 180
9.d:
मलश्चावारको माया भावोपादानकारणम् ।
कर्म स्यात् सहकार्येव सुखदुःखोद्भवं प्रति ॥ 180
9.m: Mala is the obscuring [factor], māyā is the material cause of entities, / and karma would be merely an auxiliary cause with respect to the arising of pleasure and pain.

9.s:
ataḥ saṃcchannacaitanyasamudbalanakāryakṛt /
kalaivānantanāthasya śaktyā saṃpreritā jaḍā // 181
9.d:
अतः संच्छन्नचैतन्यसमुद्बलनकार्यकृत् ।
कलैवानन्तनाथस्य शक्त्या संप्रेरिता जडा ॥ 181
9.m: Therefore, insentient kalā alone, impelled by the power of Anantanātha, / accomplishes the effect of stimulating veiled consciousness.

9.s:
na ceśaśaktirevāsya caitanyaṃ balayiṣyati /
tadupodbalitaṃ taddhi na kiṃcitkartṛtāṃ vrajet // 182
9.d:
न चेशशक्तिरेवास्य चैतन्यं बलयिष्यति ।
तदुपोद्बलितं तद्धि न किंचित्कर्तृतां व्रजेत् ॥ 182
9.m: It is not the power of the Lord itself that will strengthen his consciousness; / for that which is stimulated by that would not enter into the state of limited agency.

9.s:
seyaṃ kalā na karaṇaṃ mukhyaṃ vidyādikaṃ yathā /
puṃsi kartari sā kartrī prayojakatayā yataḥ // 183
9.d:
सेयं कला न करणं मुख्यं विद्यादिकं यथा ।
पुंसि कर्तरि सा कर्त्री प्रयोजकतया यतः ॥ 183
9.m: This kalā is not an instrument in the primary sense, like vidyā and the rest; / for while the soul is the agent, it is an agent by virtue of being an instigator.

9.s:
alakṣyāntarayoritthaṃ yadā puṃskalayorbhavet /
māyāgarbheśaśaktyāderantarajñānamāntaram // 184
9.d:
अलक्ष्यान्तरयोरित्थं यदा पुंस्कलयोर्भवेत् ।
मायागर्भेशशक्त्यादेरन्तरज्ञानमान्तरम् ॥ 184
9.m: When, between the puruṣa and kalā whose distinction is thus unnoticed, / there arises an internal knowledge of difference, through the power of the Lord within māyā,

9.s:
tadā māyāpuṃvivekaḥ sarvakarmakṣayādbhavet /
vijñānākalatā māyādhastānno yātyadhaḥ pumān // 185
9.d:
तदा मायापुंविवेकः सर्वकर्मक्षयाद्भवेत् ।
विज्ञानाकलता मायाधस्तान्नो यात्यधः पुमान् ॥ 185
9.m: then the discernment of māyā and the puruṣa takes place through the exhaustion of all karma. / The state of being a knower free of instruments [arises]; the puruṣa does not go down below māyā.

9.s:
dhīpuṃviveke vijñāte pradhānapuruṣāntare /
api na kṣīṇakarmā syāt kalāyāṃ taddhi saṃbhavet // 186
9.d:
धीपुंविवेके विज्ञाते प्रधानपुरुषान्तरे ।
अपि न क्षीणकर्मा स्यात् कलायां तद्धि संभवेत् ॥ 186
9.m: Even when the discernment of intellect and puruṣa is known, between pradhāna and the puruṣa, / one would not have one's karma destroyed; for that can occur [only] at [the level of] kalā.

9.s:
ataḥ sāṃkhyadṛśā siddhaḥ pradhānādho na saṃsaret /
kalāpuṃsorviveke tu māyādho naiva gacchati // 187
9.d:
अतः सांख्यदृशा सिद्धः प्रधानाधो न संसरेत् ।
कलापुंसोर्विवेके तु मायाधो नैव गच्छति ॥ 187
9.m: Therefore, one who is perfected according to the Sāṃkhya view does not transmigrate below pradhāna; / but when discernment between kalā and the puruṣa occurs, he never goes below māyā.

9.s:
malādviviktamātmānaṃ paśyaṃstu śivatāṃ vrajet /
sarvatra caiśvaraḥ śaktipāto'tra sahakāraṇam // 188
9.d:
मलाद्विविक्तमात्मानं पश्यंस्तु शिवतां व्रजेत् ।
सर्वत्र चैश्वरः शक्तिपातोऽत्र सहकारणम् ॥ 188
9.m: Seeing himself distinguished from mala, however, he attains the state of Śiva. / And in every case, the divine descent of power is the auxiliary cause here.

9.s:
māyāgarbhādhikārīyo dvayorantye tu nirmalaḥ /
seyaṃ kalā kāryabhedādanyaiva hyanumīyate // 189
9.d:
मायागर्भाधिकारीयो द्वयोरन्त्ये तु निर्मलः ।
सेयं कला कार्यभेदादन्यैव ह्यनुमीयते ॥ 189
9.m: In the case of the [first] two, [the soul] is qualified within the womb of māyā; in the last, however, he is free of impurity. / This kalā is inferred to be distinct precisely through the difference in effects;

9.s:
anyathaikaṃ bhavedviśvaṃ kāryāyetyanyanihnavaḥ /
iti mataṅgaśāstrādau yā proktā sā kalā svayam // 190
9.d:
अन्यथैकं भवेद्विश्वं कार्यायेत्यन्यनिह्नवः ।
इति मतङ्गशास्त्रादौ या प्रोक्ता सा कला स्वयम् ॥ 190
9.m: otherwise, the universe would be one for an effect, and thus there would be denial of others. / That which is stated in the Mataṅga and other scriptures is itself kalā.

9.s:
kiṃcidrūpatayākṣipya kartṛtvamiti bhaṅgitaḥ /
kiṃcidrūpaviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ tatkathaṃ bhavet // 191
9.d:
किंचिद्रूपतयाक्षिप्य कर्तृत्वमिति भङ्गितः ।
किंचिद्रूपविशिष्टं यत् कर्तृत्वं तत्कथं भवेत् ॥ 191
9.m: Impugning agency as having a limited nature, in this indirect way: / How could agency qualified by a limited nature exist

9.s:
ajñasyeti tataḥ sūte kiṃcijjñatvātmikāṃ vidam /
buddhiṃ paśyati sā vidyā buddhidarpaṇacāriṇaḥ // 192
9.d:
अज्ञस्येति ततः सूते किंचिज्ज्ञत्वात्मिकां विदम् ।
बुद्धिं पश्यति सा विद्या बुद्धिदर्पणचारिणः ॥ 192
9.m: for an ignorant one? Hence, it produces vidyā, which consists in limited knowing. / That vidyā perceives the intellect; moving in the mirror of the intellect,

9.s:
sukhādīn pratyayān mohaprabhṛtīn kāryakāraṇe /
karmajālaṃ ca tatrasthaṃ vivinakti nijātmanā // 193
9.d:
सुखादीन् प्रत्ययान् मोहप्रभृतीन् कार्यकारणे ।
कर्मजालं च तत्रस्थं विविनक्ति निजात्मना ॥ 193
9.m: it distinguishes through itself the mental states of pleasure and the like, delusion and so forth, in effect and cause, / as well as the web of karma situated there.

9.s:
buddhistu guṇasaṃkīrṇā vivekena kathaṃ sukham /
duḥkhaṃ mohātmakaṃ vāpi viṣayaṃ darśayedapi // 194
9.d:
बुद्धिस्तु गुणसंकीर्णा विवेकेन कथं सुखम् ।
दुःखं मोहात्मकं वापि विषयं दर्शयेदपि ॥ 194
9.m: The intellect, however, is blended with the guṇas; how could it reveal, through discrimination, / an object consisting of pleasure, pain, or delusion?

9.s:
svacchāyāṃ dhiyi saṃkrāmanbhāvaḥ saṃvedyatāṃ katham /
tayā vinaiti sāpyanyatkaraṇaṃ puṃsi kartari // 195
9.d:
स्वच्छायां धियि संक्रामन्भावः संवेद्यतां कथम् ।
तया विनैति साप्यन्यत्करणं पुंसि कर्तरि ॥ 195
9.m: How could an entity entering the transparent intellect attain the state of being cognized / without that [vidyā]? It too is another instrument for the puruṣa as agent.

9.s:
nanu cobhayataḥ śubhrādarśadaśīyadhīgatāt /
puṃsprakāśādbhāti bhāvaḥ maivaṃ tatpratibimbanam // 196
9.d:
ननु चोभयतः शुभ्रादर्शदशीयधीगतात् ।
पुंस्प्रकाशाद्भाति भावः मैवं तत्प्रतिबिम्बनम् ॥ 196
9.m: 'Surely, an entity shines from the puruṣa's light, which is situated in the intellect acting as a mirror pure on both sides?' / Not so; that reflection

9.s:
jaḍameva hi mukhyo'tha puṃsprakāśo'sya bhāsanam /
bahiḥsthasyaiva tasyāstu buddheḥ kiṃkalpanā kṛtā // 197
9.d:
जडमेव हि मुख्योऽथ पुंस्प्रकाशोऽस्य भासनम् ।
बहिःस्थस्यैव तस्यास्तु बुद्धेः किंकल्पना कृता ॥ 197
9.m: is indeed insentient. Or if the primary light of the puruṣa is its manifestation / while remaining strictly external, why was the conception of the intellect fabricated?

9.s:
abhedabhūmireṣā ca bhedaśceha vicāryate /
tasmādbuddhigato bhāvo vidyākaraṇagocaraḥ // 198
9.d:
अभेदभूमिरेषा च भेदश्चेह विचार्यते ।
तस्माद्बुद्धिगतो भावो विद्याकरणगोचरः ॥ 198
9.m: And this is the ground of non-difference, whereas here difference is being investigated. / Therefore, an object situated in the intellect is the province of the instrument of [limited] knowledge (vidyā).

9.s:
bhāvānāṃ pratibimbaṃ ca vedyaṃ dhīkalpanā tataḥ /
kiṃcittu kurute tasmānnūnamastyaparaṃ tu tat // 199
9.d:
भावानां प्रतिबिम्बं च वेद्यं धीकल्पना ततः ।
किंचित्तु कुरुते तस्मान्नूनमस्त्यपरं तु तत् ॥ 199
9.m: And the reflection of objects is the knowable; the construct of the intellect [arises] therefrom. / Yet [the soul] acts to some limited extent; therefore, that other [factor] certainly exists.

9.s:
rāgatattvamiti proktaṃ yattatraivoparañjakam /
na cāvairāgyamātraṃ tattatrāpyāsaktivṛttitaḥ // 200
9.d:
रागतत्त्वमिति प्रोक्तं यत्तत्रैवोपरञ्जकम् ।
न चावैराग्यमात्रं तत्तत्राप्यासक्तिवृत्तितः ॥ 200
9.m: The principle of attachment (rāga) is taught to be that which causes coloring precisely there. / Nor is it merely the absence of dispassion, because an orientation toward attachment exists even there,

9.s:
viraktāvapi tṛptasya sūkṣmarāgavyavasthiteḥ /
kālastuṭyādibhiścaitat kartṛtvaṃ kalayatyataḥ // 201
9.d:
विरक्तावपि तृप्तस्य सूक्ष्मरागव्यवस्थितेः ।
कालस्तुट्यादिभिश्चैतत् कर्तृत्वं कलयत्यतः ॥ 201
9.m: Since subtle attachment persists even in one who is dispassionate and satisfied. / But time (kāla) limits this agency through moments (tuṭi) and the like; therefore,

9.s:
kāryāvacchedi kartṛtvaṃ kālo'vaśyaṃ kaliṣyati /
niyatiryojanāṃ dhatte viśiṣṭe kāryamaṇḍale // 202
9.d:
कार्यावच्छेदि कर्तृत्वं कालोऽवश्यं कलिष्यति ।
नियतिर्योजनां धत्ते विशिष्टे कार्यमण्डले ॥ 202
9.m: Time must inevitably restrict agency by delimiting its effects. / Restriction (niyati) brings about connection with a specific sphere of effects.

9.s:
vidyā rāgo'tha niyatiḥ kālaścaitaccatuṣṭayam /
kalākāryaṃ bhoktṛbhāve tiṣṭhadbhoktṛtvapūritam // 203
9.d:
विद्या रागोऽथ नियतिः कालश्चैतच्चतुष्टयम् ।
कलाकार्यं भोक्तृभावे तिष्ठद्भोक्तृत्वपूरितम् ॥ 203
9.m: [Limited] knowledge (vidyā), attachment (rāga), restriction (niyati), and time (kāla)—this group of four / is the effect of limited agency (kalā); abiding in the state of the experiencer, it fulfills the nature of being an experiencer.

9.s:
māyā kalā rāgavidye kālo niyatireva ca /
kañcukāni ṣaḍuktāni saṃvidastatsthitau paśuḥ // 204
9.d:
माया कला रागविद्ये कालो नियतिरेव च ।
कञ्चुकानि षडुक्तानि संविदस्तत्स्थितौ पशुः ॥ 204
9.m: Māyā, limited agency (kalā), attachment, [limited] knowledge, time, and restriction— / these are taught to be the six cuirasses of consciousness; when abiding therein, [consciousness] is a bound soul.

9.s:
dehapuryaṣṭakādyeṣu vedyeṣu kila vedanam /
etatṣaṭkasasaṃkocaṃ yadavedyamasāvaṇuḥ // 205
9.d:
देहपुर्यष्टकाद्येषु वेद्येषु किल वेदनम् ।
एतत्षट्कससंकोचं यदवेद्यमसावणुः ॥ 205
9.m: Among the knowables such as the body, the subtle body (puryaṣṭaka), and so on, cognition indeed [arises]; / that which, having the contraction of this group of six, is unknowable—that is the individual soul (aṇu).

9.s:
uktaṃ śivatanuśāstre tadidaṃ bhaṅgyantareṇa punaḥ /
āvaraṇaṃ sarvātmagamaśuddhiranyāpyananyarūpeva // 206
9.d:
उक्तं शिवतनुशास्त्रे तदिदं भङ्ग्यन्तरेण पुनः ।
आवरणं सर्वात्मगमशुद्धिरन्याप्यनन्यरूपेव ॥ 206
9.m: This same point has been stated once more in another manner in the Śivatanuśāstra: / ‘The covering is all-pervading; the other impurity is as if non-different in form.’

9.s:
śivadahanakiraṇajālairdāhyatvāt sā yato'nyarūpaiva /
anidaṃpūrvatayā yadrañjayati nijātmanā tato'nanyā // 207
9.d:
शिवदहनकिरणजालैर्दाह्यत्वात् सा यतोऽन्यरूपैव ।
अनिदंपूर्वतया यद्रञ्जयति निजात्मना ततोऽनन्या ॥ 207
9.m: Because it can be burned by the cluster of rays of the fire of Śiva, it is indeed different in form; / because it colors by its own nature without being preceded by ‘thisness’, it is non-different.

9.s:
sahajāśuddhimato'ṇorīśaguhābhyāṃ hi kañcukastrividhaḥ /
tasya dvitīyacitiriva svacchasya niyujyate kalā ślakṣṇā // 208
9.d:
सहजाशुद्धिमतोऽणोरीशगुहाभ्यां हि कञ्चुकस्त्रिविधः ।
तस्य द्वितीयचितिरिव स्वच्छस्य नियुज्यते कला श्लक्ष्णा ॥ 208
9.m: For the individual soul possessed of innate impurity, a threefold cuirass is produced by the Lord and Guha; / for that clear [soul], subtle kalā is joined like a second consciousness.

9.s:
anayā vidvasya paśorupabhogasamarthatā bhavati /
vidyā cāsya kalātaḥ śaraṇāntardīpakaprabhevābhūt // 209
9.d:
अनया विद्वस्य पशोरुपभोगसमर्थता भवति ।
विद्या चास्य कलातः शरणान्तर्दीपकप्रभेवाभूत् ॥ 209
9.m: Being impelled by this, the bound soul’s capacity for enjoyment arises; / and from kalā his [limited] knowledge arose, like the light of a lamp inside a house,

9.s:
sukhaduḥkhasaṃvidaṃ yā vivinakti paśorvibhāgena /
rāgaśca kalātattvācchucivastrakaṣāyavat samutpannaḥ // 210
9.d:
सुखदुःखसंविदं या विविनक्ति पशोर्विभागेन ।
रागश्च कलातत्त्वाच्छुचिवस्त्रकषायवत् समुत्पन्नः ॥ 210
9.m: Which discerns the consciousness of pleasure and pain distinctly for the bound soul. / And attachment is produced from the principle of kalā, like an astringent dye on a clean cloth,

9.s:
tyaktuṃ vāñchati na yataḥ saṃsṛtisukhasaṃvidānandam /
evamavidyāmalinaḥsamarthitastriguṇakañcukabalena // 211
9.d:
त्यक्तुं वाञ्छति न यतः संसृतिसुखसंविदानन्दम् ।
एवमविद्यामलिनःसमर्थितस्त्रिगुणकञ्चुकबलेन ॥ 211
9.m: Since he does not wish to abandon the joy of experiencing pleasure in cyclic existence (saṃsāra). / In this way, soiled by ignorance and empowered by the force of the three-attribute cuirass,

9.s:
gahanopabhogagarbhe paśuravaśamadhomukhaḥ patati /
etena malaḥ kathitaḥ kambukavadaṇoḥ kalādikaṃ tuṣavat // 212
9.d:
गहनोपभोगगर्भे पशुरवशमधोमुखः पतति ।
एतेन मलः कथितः कम्बुकवदणोः कलादिकं तुषवत् ॥ 212
9.m: The bound soul falls helplessly headlong into the abyss of enjoyment. / By this, impurity is described as being like the husk of the grain for the individual soul, and kalā and the rest like the chaff.

9.s:
evaṃ kalākhyatattvasya kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇe /
viśeṣabhāge kartṛtvaṃ carcitaṃ bhoktṛpūrvakam // 213
9.d:
एवं कलाख्यतत्त्वस्य किंचित्कर्तृत्वलक्षणे ।
विशेषभागे कर्तृत्वं चर्चितं भोक्तृपूर्वकम् ॥ 213
9.m: Thus, in the specific aspect characterized as ‘limited agency’ belonging to the principle called kalā, / agency has been discussed, preceded by the experiencer.

9.s:
viśeṣaṇatayā yo'tra kiñcidbhāgastadotthitam /
vedyamātraṃ sphuṭaṃ bhinnaṃ pradhānaṃ sūyate kalā // 214
9.d:
विशेषणतया योऽत्र किञ्चिद्भागस्तदोत्थितम् ।
वेद्यमात्रं स्फुटं भिन्नं प्रधानं सूयते कला ॥ 214
