9.m: The limited aspect which is present here as a qualification—from that arises / the mere knowable, distinct and differentiated: kalā gives birth to the primal matter (pradhāna).

9.s:
samameva hi bhogyaṃ ca bhoktāraṃ ca prasūyate /
kalā bhedābhisaṃdhānādaviyuktaṃ parasparam // 215
9.d:
सममेव हि भोग्यं च भोक्तारं च प्रसूयते ।
कला भेदाभिसंधानादवियुक्तं परस्परम् ॥ 215
9.m: For simultaneously kalā gives birth to both the enjoyable and the experiencer / without separation from one another, through the intent toward differentiation.

9.s:
bhoktṛbhogyātmatā na syādviyogācca parasparam /
vilīnāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ syānmāyāsyāpi na kiṃcana // 216
9.d:
भोक्तृभोग्यात्मता न स्याद्वियोगाच्च परस्परम् ।
विलीनायां च तस्यां स्यान्मायास्यापि न किंचन ॥ 216
9.m: Nor can there be the nature of experiencer and enjoyable if there is mutual separation; / and when that [kalā] is dissolved, there would be nothing at all even for māyā.

9.s:
nanu śrīmadrauravādau rāgavidyātmakaṃ dvayam /
sūte kalā hi yugapattato'vyaktamiti sthitiḥ // 217
9.d:
ननु श्रीमद्रौरवादौ रागविद्यात्मकं द्वयम् ।
सूते कला हि युगपत्ततोऽव्यक्तमिति स्थितिः ॥ 217
9.m: [Objection:] But in the venerable Raurava and other scriptures [it is said that] the dyad consisting of attachment and [limited] knowledge / is indeed produced by kalā simultaneously, and after that the unmanifest (avyakta)—such is the established view.

9.s:
uktamatra vibhātyeṣa kramaḥ satyaṃ tathā hyalam /
rajyamāno veda sarva vidaṃścāpyatra rajyate // 218
9.d:
उक्तमत्र विभात्येष क्रमः सत्यं तथा ह्यलम् ।
रज्यमानो वेद सर्व विदंश्चाप्यत्र रज्यते ॥ 218
9.m: [Response:] It has been stated in this regard that this sequence appears; it is true, for fully indeed / one who is attached knows all, and knowing, one is also attached in this regard.

9.s:
tathāpi vastusatteyamihāsmābhirnirūpitā /
tasyāṃ ca na kramaḥ ko'pi syādvā so'pi viparyayāt // 219
9.d:
तथापि वस्तुसत्तेयमिहास्माभिर्निरूपिता ।
तस्यां च न क्रमः कोऽपि स्याद्वा सोऽपि विपर्ययात् ॥ 219
9.m: Nevertheless, it is the true state of the entity that has been determined by us here; / and in that regard, there is no sequence whatever, or that [order] too may be from inverted view.

9.s:
tasmādvipratipattiṃ no kuryācchāstrodite vidhau /
evaṃ saṃvedyamātraṃ yat sukhaduḥkhavimohataḥ // 220
9.d:
तस्माद्विप्रतिपत्तिं नो कुर्याच्छास्त्रोदिते विधौ ।
एवं संवेद्यमात्रं यत् सुखदुःखविमोहतः ॥ 220
9.m: Therefore, one should not raise a contradiction against the rule stated in the scripture. / In this way, whatever is merely to be experienced through pleasure, pain, and delusion,

9.s:
bhotsyate yattataḥ proktaṃ tatsāmyātmakamāditaḥ /
sukhaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśatvāt prakāśo hlāda ucyate // 221
9.d:
भोत्स्यते यत्ततः प्रोक्तं तत्साम्यात्मकमादितः ।
सुखं सत्त्वं प्रकाशत्वात् प्रकाशो ह्लाद उच्यते ॥ 221
9.m: Is experienced; therefore it is taught from the beginning to consist of their equilibrium. / Pleasure is sattva because it is luminous; luminosity is said to be delight.

9.s:
duḥkhaṃ rajaḥ kriyātmatvād kriyā hi tadatatkramaḥ /
mohastamo varaṇakaḥ prakāśābhāvayogataḥ // 222
9.d:
दुःखं रजः क्रियात्मत्वाद् क्रिया हि तदतत्क्रमः ।
मोहस्तमो वरणकः प्रकाशाभावयोगतः ॥ 222
9.m: Pain is rajas because it consists of action, for action is indeed the sequence of this and not-this; / delusion is tamas, a veil, because of its association with the absence of light.

9.s:
ta ete kṣobhamāpannā guṇāḥ kārya pratanvate /
akṣubdhasya vijātīyaṃ na syāt kāryamadaḥ purā // 223
9.d:
त एते क्षोभमापन्ना गुणाः कार्य प्रतन्वते ।
अक्षुब्धस्य विजातीयं न स्यात् कार्यमदः पुरा ॥ 223
9.m: These very qualities (guṇa), having attained agitation, spread forth their effects. / For an unagitated [entity], there could not be a heterogeneous effect such as this; earlier

9.s:
uktameveti śāstre'smin guṇāṃstattvāntaraṃ viduḥ /
bhuvanaṃ pṛthagevātra darśitaṃ guṇabhedataḥ // 224
9.d:
उक्तमेवेति शास्त्रेऽस्मिन् गुणांस्तत्त्वान्तरं विदुः ।
भुवनं पृथगेवात्र दर्शितं गुणभेदतः ॥ 224
9.m: It has indeed been stated thus: in this scripture, they understand the qualities to be a distinct reality; / a distinct realm is shown here due to the differentiation of the qualities.

9.s:
īśvarecchāvaśakṣubdhalolikaṃ puruṣaṃ prati /
bhoktṛtvāya svatantreśaḥ prakṛtiṃ kṣobhayed bhṛśam // 225
9.d:
ईश्वरेच्छावशक्षुब्धलोलिकं पुरुषं प्रति ।
भोक्तृत्वाय स्वतन्त्रेशः प्रकृतिं क्षोभयेद् भृशम् ॥ 225
9.m: Toward the individual soul whose desire is stirred under the influence of the Lord’s will, / the autonomous Lord violently agitates prakṛti for the sake of [his] status as an experiencer.

9.s:
tena yaccodyate sāṃkhyaṃ muktāṇuṃ prati kiṃ na sā /
sūte puṃso vikāritvāditi tannātra bādhakam // 226
9.d:
तेन यच्चोद्यते सांख्यं मुक्ताणुं प्रति किं न सा ।
सूते पुंसो विकारित्वादिति तन्नात्र बाधकम् ॥ 226
9.m: Therefore, the objection raised against the Sāṅkhya—why does it not / produce for the liberated soul, since the soul is mutable?—does not subvert our position.

9.s:
guṇebhyo buddhitattvaṃ tat sarvato nirmalaṃ tataḥ /
puṃsprakāśaḥ sa vedyo'tra pratibimbatvamārchati // 227
9.d:
गुणेभ्यो बुद्धितत्त्वं तत् सर्वतो निर्मलं ततः ।
पुंस्प्रकाशः स वेद्योऽत्र प्रतिबिम्बत्वमार्छति ॥ 227
9.m: From the qualities [arises] the principle of intellect, which is completely pure; therefore / the luminosity of the soul, as an object of knowledge, attains reflection in it.

9.s:
viṣayapratibimbaṃ ca tasyāmakṣakṛtaṃ bahiḥ /
ataddvāraṃ samutprekṣāpratibhādiṣu tādṛśī // 228
9.d:
विषयप्रतिबिम्बं च तस्यामक्षकृतं बहिः ।
अतद्द्वारं समुत्प्रेक्षाप्रतिभादिषु तादृशी ॥ 228
9.m: And the reflection of external objects in it is produced by the senses; / in conjecture, intuition, and so on, such an operation of the intellect

9.s:
vṛttirbodho bhavedbuddheḥ sā cāpyālambanaṃ dhruvam /
ātmasaṃvitprakāśasya bodho'sau tajjaḍo'pyalam // 229
9.d:
वृत्तिर्बोधो भवेद्बुद्धेः सा चाप्यालम्बनं ध्रुवम् ।
आत्मसंवित्प्रकाशस्य बोधोऽसौ तज्जडोऽप्यलम् ॥ 229
9.m: Independent of those [external senses] is cognition; and that is certainly the support / for the luminosity of the consciousness of the Self; although insentient, that cognition is fully [adequate for this].

9.s:
buddherahaṃkṛt tādṛkṣe pratibimbitapuṃskṛteḥ /
prakāśe vedyakaluṣe yadahaṃmananātmatā // 230
9.d:
बुद्धेरहंकृत् तादृक्षे प्रतिबिम्बितपुंस्कृतेः ।
प्रकाशे वेद्यकलुषे यदहंमननात्मता ॥ 230
9.m: From the intellect [arises] the ego (ahaṃkāra) in such [a condition]: when in the light wherein the soul is reflected / and which is tainted by knowables, there is the state of conceiving an ‘I’.

9.s:
tayā pañcavidhaścaiṣa vāyuḥ saṃrambharūpayā /
prerito jīvanāya syādanyathā maraṇaṃ punaḥ // 231
9.d:
तया पञ्चविधश्चैष वायुः संरम्भरूपया ।
प्रेरितो जीवनाय स्यादन्यथा मरणं पुनः ॥ 231
9.m: By this [ego], which takes the form of zealous effort, this fivefold vital breath / is impelled for the sake of living; otherwise, death would ensue.

9.s:
ata eva viśuddhātmasvātantryāhaṃsvabhāvataḥ /
akṛtrimādidaṃ tvanyadityuktaṃ kṛtiśabdataḥ // 232
9.d:
अत एव विशुद्धात्मस्वातन्त्र्याहंस्वभावतः ।
अकृत्रिमादिदं त्वन्यदित्युक्तं कृतिशब्दतः ॥ 232
9.m: Precisely for this reason, this is [taught to be] different from the unartificial nature of ‘I’ which is the absolute autonomy of the pure Self; / this is indicated by the word ‘making’ (kṛti) [in ahaṃkāra].

9.s:
ityayaṃ karaṇaskandho'haṃkārasya nirūpitaḥ /
tridhāsya prakṛtiskandhaḥ sāttvarājasatāmasaḥ // 233
9.d:
इत्ययं करणस्कन्धोऽहंकारस्य निरूपितः ।
त्रिधास्य प्रकृतिस्कन्धः सात्त्वराजसतामसः ॥ 233
9.m: Thus this instrument-aggregate of the ego has been described. / Its aggregate of prakṛti is threefold: sāttvika, rājasika, and tāmasika.

9.s:
sattvapradhānāhaṃkārādbhoktraṃśasparśinaḥ sphuṭam /
manobuddhyakṣaṣaṭkaṃ tu jātaṃ bhedastu kathyate // 234
9.d:
सत्त्वप्रधानाहंकाराद्भोक्त्रंशस्पर्शिनः स्फुटम् ।
मनोबुद्ध्यक्षषट्कं तु जातं भेदस्तु कथ्यते ॥ 234
9.m: From the ego dominated by sattva, touching the aspect of the experiencer, clearly / the group of six consisting of the mind and the cognitive senses is born; but the division is explained:

9.s:
mano yatsarvaviṣayaṃ tenātra pravivakṣitam /
sarvatanmātrakartṛtvaṃ viśeṣaṇamahaṃkṛteḥ // 235
9.d:
मनो यत्सर्वविषयं तेनात्र प्रविवक्षितम् ।
सर्वतन्मात्रकर्तृत्वं विशेषणमहंकृतेः ॥ 235
9.m: Because the mind has all things as its object, what is intended to be expressed here / is agency over all subtle elements (tanmātra) as a qualification of the ego.

9.s:
buddhyahaṃkṛnmanaḥ prāhurbodhasaṃrabhaṇaiṣaṇe /
karaṇaṃ bāhyadevairyannaivāpyantarmukhaiḥ kṛtam // 236
9.d:
बुद्ध्यहंकृन्मनः प्राहुर्बोधसंरभणैषणे ।
करणं बाह्यदेवैर्यन्नैवाप्यन्तर्मुखैः कृतम् ॥ 236
9.m: They say that intellect, ego, and mind are the instruments in cognizing, making effort, and willing, / which are not accomplished by external deities, nor even by internal-facing ones.

9.s:
prāṇaśca nāntaḥkaraṇaṃ jaḍatvāt preraṇātmanaḥ /
prayatnecchāvibodhāṃśahetutvāditi niścitam // 237
9.d:
प्राणश्च नान्तःकरणं जडत्वात् प्रेरणात्मनः ।
प्रयत्नेच्छाविबोधांशहेतुत्वादिति निश्चितम् ॥ 237
9.m: And the vital breath is not an internal organ because it is insentient, being an impelling force, / whereas [the internal organ] is determined to be the cause of the aspects of exertion, will, and knowledge.

9.s:
avasāyo'bhimānaśca kalpanā ceti na kriyā /
ekarūpā tatastritvaṃ yuktamantaḥkṛtau sphuṭam // 238
9.d:
अवसायोऽभिमानश्च कल्पना चेति न क्रिया ।
एकरूपा ततस्त्रित्वं युक्तमन्तःकृतौ स्फुटम् ॥ 238
9.m: Ascertainment, conceit, and mental construction—the action is not / of a single form; therefore, the threefold division in the internal organ is clearly justified.

9.s:
na ca buddhirasaṃvedyā karaṇatvānmano yathā /
pradhānavadasaṃvedyabuddhivādastadujjhitaḥ // 239
9.d:
न च बुद्धिरसंवेद्या करणत्वान्मनो यथा ।
प्रधानवदसंवेद्यबुद्धिवादस्तदुज्झितः ॥ 239
9.m: Nor is the intellect unexperienced, because it is an instrument, like the mind; / therefore the doctrine that the intellect is unexperienced like pradhāna is discarded.

9.s:
śabdatanmātrahetutvaviśiṣṭā yā tvahaṃkṛtiḥ /
sā śrotre karaṇaṃ yāvadghrāṇe gandhatvabhoditā // 240
9.d:
शब्दतन्मात्रहेतुत्वविशिष्टा या त्वहंकृतिः ।
सा श्रोत्रे करणं यावद्घ्राणे गन्धत्वभोदिता ॥ 240
9.m: The ego qualified by being the cause of the subtle element of sound / is the instrument with respect to the ear, up to [that which is] awakened by the quality of odor in the nose.

9.s:
bhautikatvamato'pyastu niyamādviṣayeṣvalam /
ahaṃ śṛṇomi paśyāmi jighrāmītyādisaṃvidi // 241
9.d:
भौतिकत्वमतोऽप्यस्तु नियमाद्विषयेष्वलम् ।
अहं शृणोमि पश्यामि जिघ्रामीत्यादिसंविदि ॥ 241
9.m: Let it also be elemental on account of the restriction to specific objects; / in the experience ‘I hear, I see, I smell,’ and so on,

9.s:
ahaṃtānugamādāhaṃkārikatvaṃ sphuṭaṃ sthitam /
karaṇatvamato yuktaṃ kartraśaspṛktvayogataḥ // 242
9.d:
अहंतानुगमादाहंकारिकत्वं स्फुटं स्थितम् ।
करणत्वमतो युक्तं कर्त्रशस्पृक्त्वयोगतः ॥ 242
9.m: Because it follows the sense of ‘I’, origin from the ego is clearly established; / therefore, its nature as an instrument is appropriate, through its connection with touching the aspect of the agent.

9.s:
karturvibhinnaṃ karaṇaṃ preryatvāt karaṇaṃ kutaḥ /
karaṇāntaravāñchāyāṃ bhavettatrānavasthitiḥ // 243
9.d:
कर्तुर्विभिन्नं करणं प्रेर्यत्वात् करणं कुतः ।
करणान्तरवाञ्छायां भवेत्तत्रानवस्थितिः ॥ 243
9.m: How can an instrument distinct from the agent be an instrument, since it must be impelled [by him]? / If another instrument is required [to impel it], there would be an infinite regress. // 243

9.s:
tasmāt svātantryayogena kartā svaṃ bhedayan vapuḥ /
karmāśasparśinaṃ svāṃśaṃ karaṇīkurute svayam // 244
9.d:
तस्मात् स्वातन्त्र्ययोगेन कर्ता स्वं भेदयन् वपुः ।
कर्माशस्पर्शिनं स्वांशं करणीकुरुते स्वयम् ॥ 244
9.m: Therefore, by virtue of his absolute autonomy, the agent, differentiating his own body, / makes a part of himself that touches the object-portion into an instrument by himself. // 244

9.s:
karaṇīkṛtatatsvāṃśatanmayībhāvanāvaśāt /
karaṇīkurute'tyantavyatiriktaṃ kuṭhāravat // 245
9.d:
करणीकृततत्स्वांशतन्मयीभावनावशात् ।
करणीकुरुतेऽत्यन्तव्यतिरिक्तं कुठारवत् ॥ 245
9.m: Through the power of identifying with that part of himself made into an instrument, / he turns something entirely distinct into an instrument, just like an axe. // 245

9.s:
tenāśuddhaiva vidyāsya sāmānyaṃ karaṇaṃ purā /
jñaptau kṛtau tu sāmānyaṃ kalā karaṇamucyate // 246
9.d:
तेनाशुद्धैव विद्यास्य सामान्यं करणं पुरा ।
ज्ञप्तौ कृतौ तु सामान्यं कला करणमुच्यते ॥ 246
9.m: For this reason, impure vidyā alone is his general instrument beforehand / in knowing; but in action, kalā is said to be the general instrument. // 246

9.s:
nanu śrīmanmataṅgādau kalāyāḥ kartṛtoditā /
tasyāṃ satyāṃ hi vidyādyāḥ karaṇatvārhatājuṣaḥ // 247
9.d:
ननु श्रीमन्मतङ्गादौ कलायाः कर्तृतोदिता ।
तस्यां सत्यां हि विद्याद्याः करणत्वार्हताजुषः ॥ 247
9.m: [Objection:] But in the venerable Mataṅga and other texts, kalā is declared to possess agency; / indeed, when it exists, vidyā and the others partake of suitability to be instruments. // 247

9.s:
ucyate kartṛtaivoktā karaṇatve prayojikā /
tayā vinā tu nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ sthitiryataḥ // 248
9.d:
उच्यते कर्तृतैवोक्ता करणत्वे प्रयोजिका ।
तया विना तु नान्येषां करणानां स्थितिर्यतः ॥ 248
9.m: [Response:] It is said in reply: agency alone is taught as the instigator in instrumentness, / for without it there is no existence of the other instruments. // 248

9.s:
ato'sāmānyakaraṇavargāt tatra pṛthak kṛtā /
vidyāṃ vinā hi nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ nijā sthitiḥ // 249
9.d:
अतोऽसामान्यकरणवर्गात् तत्र पृथक् कृता ।
विद्यां विना हि नान्येषां करणानां निजा स्थितिः ॥ 249
9.m: Therefore, it is separated there from the class of general instruments, / for without vidyā the other instruments have no existence of their own. // 249

9.s:
kalāṃ vinā na tasyāśca kartṛtve jñātṛtā yataḥ /
kalāvidye tataḥ puṃso mukhyaṃ tatkaraṇaṃ viduḥ // 250
9.d:
कलां विना न तस्याश्च कर्तृत्वे ज्ञातृता यतः ।
कलाविद्ये ततः पुंसो मुख्यं तत्करणं विदुः ॥ 250
9.m: And without kalā, [vidyā] has no [existence], since knowership exists within agency; / therefore, they consider kalā and vidyā to be the primary instruments of the person. // 250

9.s:
ata eva vihīne'pi buddhikarmendriyaiḥ kvacit /
andhe paṅgau rūpagatiprakāśo na na bhāsate // 251
9.d:
अत एव विहीनेऽपि बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियैः क्वचित् ।
अन्धे पङ्गौ रूपगतिप्रकाशो न न भासते ॥ 251
9.m: Precisely for this reason, even when a person is deprived of the cognitive and active senses in some respects, / being blind or lame, the manifestation of forms and locomotion does not fail to appear. // 251

9.s:
kiṃtu sāmānyakaraṇabalādvedye'pi tādṛśi /
rūpasāmānya evāndhaḥ pratipattiṃ prapadyate // 252
9.d:
किंतु सामान्यकरणबलाद्वेद्येऽपि तादृशि ।
रूपसामान्य एवान्धः प्रतिपत्तिं प्रपद्यते ॥ 252
9.m: Rather, by the power of the general instrument, even when such an object of knowledge exists, / the blind person attains perception only in the universal of form. // 252

9.s:
tata eva tvahaṃkārāt tanmātrasparśino'dhikam /
karmendriyāṇi vākpāṇipāyūpasthāṅghri jajñire // 253
9.d:
तत एव त्वहंकारात् तन्मात्रस्पर्शिनोऽधिकम् ।
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि वाक्पाणिपायूपस्थाङ्घ्रि जज्ञिरे ॥ 253
9.m: From that very ahaṃkāra, however, surpassing that which touches the subtle elements, / the active senses arose: voice, hands, anus, genitals, and feet. // 253

9.s:
vacmyādade tyajāmyāśu visṛjāmi vrajāmi ca /
iti yāhaṃkriyā kāryakṣamā karmendriyaṃ tu tat // 254
9.d:
वच्म्याददे त्यजाम्याशु विसृजामि व्रजामि च ।
इति याहंक्रिया कार्यक्षमा कर्मेन्द्रियं तु तत् ॥ 254
9.m: "I speak, I grasp, I swiftly discard, I emit, and I go"— / the sense of ego capable of doing such tasks is indeed an active sense. // 254

9.s:
tena cchinnakarasyāsti hastaḥ karmendriyātmakaḥ /
tasya pradhānādhiṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ pañcāṅguliḥ karaḥ // 255
9.d:
तेन च्छिन्नकरस्यास्ति हस्तः कर्मेन्द्रियात्मकः ।
तस्य प्रधानाधिष्ठानं परं पञ्चाङ्गुलिः करः ॥ 255
9.m: Therefore, even a person whose physical hand has been severed possesses the hand as an active sense; / the five-fingered hand is merely its primary physical base. // 255

9.s:
mukhenāpi yadādānaṃ tatra yat karaṇaṃ sthitam /
sa pāṇireva karaṇaṃ vinā kiṃ saṃbhavet kriyā // 256
9.d:
मुखेनापि यदादानं तत्र यत् करणं स्थितम् ।
स पाणिरेव करणं विना किं संभवेत् क्रिया ॥ 256
9.m: Even when grasping is done with the mouth, the instrument operating there / is indeed the hand: how could action occur without an instrument? // 256

9.s:
tathābhāve tu buddhyakṣairapi kiṃ syātprayojanam /
darśanaṃ karaṇāpekṣaṃ kriyātvāditi cocyate // 257
9.d:
तथाभावे तु बुद्ध्यक्षैरपि किं स्यात्प्रयोजनम् ।
दर्शनं करणापेक्षं क्रियात्वादिति चोच्यते ॥ 257
9.m: If it were otherwise, what purpose would there be even for the sense organs? / And it is said that seeing depends upon an instrument because it is an action. // 257

9.s:
parairgamau tu karaṇaṃ neṣyate ceti vismayaḥ /
gamanotkṣepaṇādīni mukhyaṃ karmopalambhanam // 258
9.d:
परैर्गमौ तु करणं नेष्यते चेति विस्मयः ।
गमनोत्क्षेपणादीनि मुख्यं कर्मोपलम्भनम् ॥ 258
9.m: It is astonishing that others do not accept an instrument in locomotion; / locomotion, upward projection, and so forth are the primary perceptible forms of action. // 258

9.s:
punarguṇaḥ kriyā tveṣā vaiyākaraṇadarśane /
kriyā karaṇapūrveti vyāptyā karaṇapūrvakam // 259
9.d:
पुनर्गुणः क्रिया त्वेषा वैयाकरणदर्शने ।
क्रिया करणपूर्वेति व्याप्त्या करणपूर्वकम् ॥ 259
9.m: According to the Grammarian system, however, this action is a secondary attribute; / through the invariable concomitance that "action is preceded by an instrument," [to say that] / knowledge is preceded by an instrument, while grasping is not, is clearly the flourishing of blindness. // 259

9.s:
jñānaṃ nādānamityetat sphuṭamāndhyavijṛmbhitam /
tasmāt karmendriyāṇyāhustvagvadvyāptṝṇi mukhyataḥ // 260
9.d:
ज्ञानं नादानमित्येतत् स्फुटमान्ध्यविजृम्भितम् ।
तस्मात् कर्मेन्द्रियाण्याहुस्त्वग्वद्व्याप्तॄणि मुख्यतः ॥ 260
9.m: Therefore, my teachers have said in the Mataṅga that the active senses primarily / pervade [the body] like the sense of touch, functioning in their respective locations. // 260

9.s:
tatsthāne vṛttimantīti mataṅge guravo mama /
nanvanyānyapi karmāṇi santi bhūyāṃsi tatkṛte // 261
9.d:
तत्स्थाने वृत्तिमन्तीति मतङ्गे गुरवो मम ।
नन्वन्यान्यपि कर्माणि सन्ति भूयांसि तत्कृते ॥ 261
9.m: [Objection:] But there are many other actions; for their sake, / instruments would also have to be stated, and thus there would be no finality regarding the senses! // 261

9.s:
karaṇānyapi vācyāni tathā cākṣeṣvaniṣṭhitiḥ /
nanvetat kheṭapālādyairnirākāri na karmaṇām // 262
9.d:
करणान्यपि वाच्यानि तथा चाक्षेष्वनिष्ठितिः ।
नन्वेतत् खेटपालाद्यैर्निराकारि न कर्मणाम् ॥ 262
9.m: Is it not true that Kheṭapāla and others refuted this, saying: "That which is an instrument of actions / is not an organ of sense; but rather, [an organ exists] for specific actions"? // 262

9.s:
yatsādhanaṃ tadakṣaṃ syāt kiṃtu kasyāpi karmaṇaḥ /
etannāsmatkṛtapraśnatṛṣṇāsaṃtāpaśāntaye // 263
9.d:
यत्साधनं तदक्षं स्यात् किंतु कस्यापि कर्मणः ।
एतन्नास्मत्कृतप्रश्नतृष्णासंतापशान्तये ॥ 263
9.m: This does not pacify the burning thirst of the question we have posed; / for peacocks are never satisfied with turbid, meager waters! // 263

9.s:
nahyasvacchamitaprāyairjalaistṛpyanti barhiṇaḥ /
ucyate śrīmatādiṣṭaṃ śaṃbhunātra mamottaram // 264
9.d:
नह्यस्वच्छमितप्रायैर्जलैस्तृप्यन्ति बर्हिणः ।
उच्यते श्रीमतादिष्टं शंभुनात्र ममोत्तरम् ॥ 264
9.m: The answer taught to me here by the venerable Śambhunātha is stated: // 264

9.s:
svacchasaṃvedanodāravikalāprabalīkṛtam /
iha karmānusaṃdhānabhedādekaṃ vibhidyate // 265
9.d:
स्वच्छसंवेदनोदारविकलाप्रबलीकृतम् ।
इह कर्मानुसंधानभेदादेकं विभिद्यते ॥ 265
9.m: Strengthened by pure consciousness and noble determinative reflection, / here a single action becomes differentiated through the division of mental intention. // 265

9.s:
tatrānusaṃdhiḥ pañcātmā pañca karmendriyāṇyataḥ /
tyāgāyādānasaṃpattyai dvayāya dvitayaṃ vinā // 266
9.d:
तत्रानुसंधिः पञ्चात्मा पञ्च कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यतः ।
त्यागायादानसंपत्त्यै द्वयाय द्वितयं विना ॥ 266
9.m: In that regard, mental intention is fivefold; therefore, the active senses are five: / for discarding, for attaining grasping, for the pair [of urination and evacuation], and—aside from this pair— // 266

9.s:
svarūpaviśrāntikṛte caturdhā karma yadbahiḥ /
pāyupāṇyaṅghrijananaṃ karaṇaṃ taccaturvidham // 267
9.d:
स्वरूपविश्रान्तिकृते चतुर्धा कर्म यद्बहिः ।
पायुपाण्यङ्घ्रिजननं करणं तच्चतुर्विधम् ॥ 267
9.m: for resting in one's own nature. The action that is external is fourfold; / the fourfold instrument is the anus, hands, feet, and genitals. // 267

9.s:
antaṃ prāṇāśrayaṃ yattu karmātra karaṇaṃ hi vāk /
uktāḥ samāsataścaiṣāṃ citrāḥ kāryeṣu vṛttayaḥ // 268
9.d:
अन्तं प्राणाश्रयं यत्तु कर्मात्र करणं हि वाक् ।
उक्ताः समासतश्चैषां चित्राः कार्येषु वृत्तयः ॥ 268
9.m: The internal action resting upon the vital breath, however, has voice as its instrument. / Thus the varied functions of these [senses] in their operations have been stated in brief. // 268

9.s:
tadetadvyatiriktaṃ hi na karma kvāpi dṛśyate /
tatkasyārthe prakalpyeyamindriyāṇāmaniṣṭhitiḥ // 269
9.d:
तदेतद्व्यतिरिक्तं हि न कर्म क्वापि दृश्यते ।
तत्कस्यार्थे प्रकल्प्येयमिन्द्रियाणामनिष्ठितिः ॥ 269
9.m: Indeed, no action is seen anywhere distinct from these; / for what purpose, then, should this lack of finality regarding the senses be conjectured? // 269

9.s:
etatkartavyacakraṃ tadasāṃkaryeṇa kurvate /
akṣāṇi sahavṛttyā tu buddhyante saṃkaraṃ jaḍāḥ // 270
9.d:
एतत्कर्तव्यचक्रं तदसांकर्येण कुर्वते ।
अक्षाणि सहवृत्त्या तु बुद्ध्यन्ते संकरं जडाः ॥ 270
9.m: The senses execute this wheel of duties without confusion; / but unintelligent people, because the functions occur together, perceive confusion. // 270

9.s:
ukta indriyavargo'yamahaṃkārāt tu rājasāt /
tamaḥpradhānāhaṃkārād bhoktraṃśacchādanātmanaḥ // 271
9.d:
उक्त इन्द्रियवर्गोऽयमहंकारात् तु राजसात् ।
तमःप्रधानाहंकाराद् भोक्त्रंशच्छादनात्मनः ॥ 271
9.m: This group of senses has been declared to arise from rājasika ahaṃkāra. / From ahaṃkāra dominated by tamas, whose nature is the concealing of the experiencer's portion, // 271

9.s:
bhūtādināmnastanmātrapañcakaṃ bhūtakāraṇam /
manobuddhyakṣakarmākṣavargastanmātravargakaḥ // 272
9.d:
भूतादिनाम्नस्तन्मात्रपञ्चकं भूतकारणम् ।
मनोबुद्ध्यक्षकर्माक्षवर्गस्तन्मात्रवर्गकः ॥ 272
9.m: called bhūtādi, [arises] the group of five subtle elements, the cause of the gross elements. / The group of the mind, cognitive senses, and active senses, and the group of subtle elements— // 272

9.s:
ityatra rājasāhaṃkṛdyogaḥ saṃśleṣako dvaye /
anye tvāhurmano jātaṃ rājasāhaṃkṛteryataḥ // 273
9.d:
इत्यत्र राजसाहंकृद्योगः संश्लेषको द्वये ।
अन्ये त्वाहुर्मनो जातं राजसाहंकृतेर्यतः ॥ 273
9.m: here the connection with rājasika ahaṃkāra is the unifying factor in both. / Others, however, say that the mind arose from rājasika ahaṃkāra, because // 273

9.s:
samastendriyasaṃcāracaturaṃ laghu vegavat /
anye tu sāttvikāt svāntaṃ buddhikarmendriyāṇi tu // 274
9.d:
समस्तेन्द्रियसंचारचतुरं लघु वेगवत् ।
अन्ये तु सात्त्विकात् स्वान्तं बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियाणि तु ॥ 274
9.m: it is skillful, light, and swift in operating through all the senses. / Yet others believe that the mind arises from the sāttvika, while the cognitive and active senses // 274

9.s:
rājasādgrāhakagrāhyabhāgasparśīni manvate /
kheṭapālāstu manyante karmendriyagaṇaḥ sphuṭam // 275
9.d:
राजसाद्ग्राहकग्राह्यभागस्पर्शीनि मन्वते ।
खेटपालास्तु मन्यन्ते कर्मेन्द्रियगणः स्फुटम् ॥ 275
9.m: arise from the rājasika, touching the divisions of subject and object. / But Kheṭapāla and his followers consider that the group of active senses clearly // 275

9.s:
rājasāhaṃkṛterjāto rajasaḥ karmatā yataḥ /
śrīpūrvaśāstre tu mano rājasāt sāttvikātpunaḥ // 276
9.d:
राजसाहंकृतेर्जातो रजसः कर्मता यतः ।
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तु मनो राजसात् सात्त्विकात्पुनः ॥ 276
9.m: arose from rājasika ahaṃkāra, because activity belongs to rajas. / In the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, however, the mind is said to arise from the rājasika, and all the senses, // 276

9.s:
indriyāṇi samastāni yuktaṃ caitadvibhāti naḥ /
tathāhi bāhyavṛttīnāmakṣāṇāṃ vṛttibhāsane // 277
9.d:
इन्द्रियाणि समस्तानि युक्तं चैतद्विभाति नः ।
तथाहि बाह्यवृत्तीनामक्षाणां वृत्तिभासने ॥ 277
9.m: moreover, from the sāttvika; and this appears sound to us. / For, regarding the manifestation of the functioning of the senses whose operation is external, // 277

9.s:
ālocane śaktirantaryojane manasaḥ punaḥ /
uktaṃ ca guruṇā kuryānmano'nuvyavasāyi sat // 278
9.d:
आलोचने शक्तिरन्तर्योजने मनसः पुनः ।
उक्तं च गुरुणा कुर्यान्मनोऽनुव्यवसायि सत् ॥ 278
9.m: their power lies in indeterminate perception, whereas that of the mind lies in internal synthesising. / And it was said by the master: "The mind, being reflective, should execute // 278

9.s:
taddvayālambanā mātṛvyāpārātmakriyā iti /
tānmātrastu gaṇo dhvāntapradhānāyā ahaṃkṛteḥ // 279
9.d:
तद्द्वयालम्बना मातृव्यापारात्मक्रिया इति ।
तान्मात्रस्तु गणो ध्वान्तप्रधानाया अहंकृतेः ॥ 279
9.m: actions consisting of the operations of the knower resting on both of these." / The group of subtle elements, however, arises from ahaṃkāra dominated by darkness; // 279

9.s:
atrāvivādaḥ sarvasya grāhyopakrama eva hi /
pṛthivyāṃ saurabhānyādivicitre gandhamaṇḍale // 280
9.d:
अत्राविवादः सर्वस्य ग्राह्योपक्रम एव हि ।
पृथिव्यां सौरभान्यादिविचित्रे गन्धमण्डले ॥ 280
9.m: on this point there is no dispute, for it is indeed the beginning of the object of perception. / In earth, within the manifold sphere of odor such as fragrance and the rest, // 280

9.s:
yatsāmānyaṃ hi gandhatvaṃ gandhatanmātranāma tat /
vyāpakaṃ tata evoktaṃ sahetutvāttu na dhruvam // 281
9.d:
यत्सामान्यं हि गन्धत्वं गन्धतन्मात्रनाम तत् ।
व्यापकं तत एवोक्तं सहेतुत्वात्तु न ध्रुवम् ॥ 281
9.m: the universal which is odorness is called the subtle element of odor. / For that reason it is declared all-pervasive, but because it has a cause, it is not permanent. // 281

9.s:
svakāraṇe tirobhūtirdhvaso yattena nādhruvam /
evaṃ rasādiśabdāntatanmātreṣvapi yojanā // 282
9.d:
स्वकारणे तिरोभूतिर्ध्वसो यत्तेन नाध्रुवम् ।
एवं रसादिशब्दान्ततन्मात्रेष्वपि योजना ॥ 282
9.m: Because its destruction is its disappearance into its own cause, it is not permanent. / The same application holds for the subtle elements beginning with taste up to sound. // 282

9.s:
viśeṣāṇāṃ yato'vaśyaṃ daśā prāgaviśeṣiṇī /
kṣubhitaṃ śabdatanmātraṃ citrākārāḥ śratīrdadhat // 283
9.d:
विशेषाणां यतोऽवश्यं दशा प्रागविशेषिणी ।
क्षुभितं शब्दतन्मात्रं चित्राकाराः श्रतीर्दधत् ॥ 283
9.m: Because particulars necessarily have a preceding non-particularized state. / The agitated subtle element of sound, bearing audibles of varied forms, // 283

9.s:
nabhaḥ śabdo'vakāśātmā vācyādhyāsasaho yataḥ /
tadetatsparśatanmātrayogāt prakṣobhamāgatam // 284
9.d:
नभः शब्दोऽवकाशात्मा वाच्याध्याससहो यतः ।
तदेतत्स्पर्शतन्मात्रयोगात् प्रक्षोभमागतम् ॥ 284
9.m: is space, since sound is of the nature of accommodation, sustaining the superimposition of the expressible. / When this [space] becomes agitated through contact with the subtle element of touch, // 284

9.s:
vāyutāmeti tenātra śabdasparśobhayātmatā /
anye tvāhurdhvaniḥ khaikaguṇastadapi yujyate // 285
9.d:
वायुतामेति तेनात्र शब्दस्पर्शोभयात्मता ।
अन्ये त्वाहुर्ध्वनिः खैकगुणस्तदपि युज्यते ॥ 285
9.m: it becomes wind; therefore, here there is the dual nature of sound and touch. / Others say that sound is the exclusive quality of space, and that is also fitting, // 285

9.s:
yato vāyurnijaṃ rūpaṃ labhate na vināmbarāt /
uttarottarabhūteṣu pūrvapūrvasthitiryataḥ // 286
9.d:
यतो वायुर्निजं रूपं लभते न विनाम्बरात् ।
उत्तरोत्तरभूतेषु पूर्वपूर्वस्थितिर्यतः ॥ 286
9.m: because wind does not attain its own nature without space, / since the preceding elements exist within each successive element. // 286

9.s:
tata eva marudvyomnoraviyogo mithaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śabdasparśau tu rūpeṇa samaṃ prakṣobhamāgatau // 287
9.d:
तत एव मरुद्व्योम्नोरवियोगो मिथः स्मृतः ।
शब्दस्पर्शौ तु रूपेण समं प्रक्षोभमागतौ ॥ 287
9.m: Precisely for this reason, wind and space are remembered as inseparable from one another. / Sound and touch, however, having become agitated together with form, // 287

9.s:
tejastattvaṃ tribhirdharmaiḥ prāhuḥ pūrvavadeva tat /
taistribhiḥ sarasairāpaḥ sagandhairbhūriti kramaḥ // 288
9.d:
तेजस्तत्त्वं त्रिभिर्धर्मैः प्राहुः पूर्ववदेव तत् ।
तैस्त्रिभिः सरसैरापः सगन्धैर्भूरिति क्रमः ॥ 288
9.m: are called the element of fire, possessing three properties, just as before. / Water possesses those three along with taste, and earth along with odor: such is the order. // 288

9.s:
tatra pratyakṣataḥ siddho dharādiguṇasaṃcayaḥ /
nahi gandhādidharmaughavyatiriktā vibhāti bhūḥ // 289
9.d:
तत्र प्रत्यक्षतः सिद्धो धरादिगुणसंचयः ।
नहि गन्धादिधर्मौघव्यतिरिक्ता विभाति भूः ॥ 289
9.m: In that context, the collection of properties belonging to earth and the others is established through direct perception; / for earth does not appear as something separate from the multitude of properties such as fragrance. // 289

9.s:
yathā guṇaguṇidvaitavādināmekamapyadaḥ /
citraṃ rūpaṃ paṭe bhāti kramāddharmāstathā bhuvi // 290
9.d:
यथा गुणगुणिद्वैतवादिनामेकमप्यदः ।
चित्रं रूपं पटे भाति क्रमाद्धर्मास्तथा भुवि ॥ 290
9.m: Just as for those who assert a duality between quality and possessor of quality, this single / variegated colour appears on a cloth, so too properties appear successively in earth. // 290

9.s:
yathā ca vistṛte vastre yugapadbhāti citratā /
tathaiva yogināṃ dharmasāmastyenāvabhāti bhūḥ // 291
9.d:
यथा च विस्तृते वस्त्रे युगपद्भाति चित्रता ।
तथैव योगिनां धर्मसामस्त्येनावभाति भूः ॥ 291
9.m: And just as when a cloth is unfolded its variegated nature appears all at once, / in the very same way earth appears to yogins in the totality of its properties. // 291

9.s:
gandhādiśabdaparyantacitrarūpā dharā tataḥ /
upāyabhedādbhātyeṣā kramākramavibhāgataḥ // 292
9.d:
गन्धादिशब्दपर्यन्तचित्ररूपा धरा ततः ।
उपायभेदाद्भात्येषा क्रमाक्रमविभागतः ॥ 292
9.m: Therefore, earth, consisting of variegated forms beginning with fragrance and ending with sound, / appears in this way through the distinction of succession and non-succession according to differences of means. // 292

9.s:
tata eva kramavyaktikṛto dhībheda ucyate /
ṣaṣṭhīprayogo dhībhedādbhedyabhedakatā tathā // 293
9.d:
तत एव क्रमव्यक्तिकृतो धीभेद उच्यते ।
षष्ठीप्रयोगो धीभेदाद्भेद्यभेदकता तथा ॥ 293
9.m: For that very reason, a distinction in cognition brought about by the successive manifestation is spoken of; / the use of the genitive case arises from the distinction in cognition, as does the relation of qualificand and qualifier. // 293

9.s:
tena dharmātirikto'tra dharmī nāma na kaścana /
tatrānekaprakārāḥ syurgandharūparasāḥ kṣitau // 294
9.d:
तेन धर्मातिरिक्तोऽत्र धर्मी नाम न कश्चन ।
तत्रानेकप्रकाराः स्युर्गन्धरूपरसाः क्षितौ ॥ 294
9.m: Therefore, there is no substantive distinct from its properties here at all. / Among them, fragrance, colour, and taste in earth are of manifold kinds; // 294

9.s:
saṃsparśaḥ pākajo'nuṣṇāśītaḥ śabdo vicitrakaḥ /
śauklyaṃ mādhuryaśītatve citrāḥ śabdāśca vāriṇi // 295
9.d:
संस्पर्शः पाकजोऽनुष्णाशीतः शब्दो विचित्रकः ।
शौक्ल्यं माधुर्यशीतत्वे चित्राः शब्दाश्च वारिणि ॥ 295
9.m: its touch is produced by heat and is neither hot nor cold; its sound is varied. / Whiteness, sweetness, coolness, and varied sounds are in water. // 295

9.s:
śuklabhāsvaratoṣṇatvaṃ citrāḥ śabdāśca pāvake /
apākajaścāśītoṣṇo dhvaniścitraśca mārute // 296
9.d:
शुक्लभास्वरतोष्णत्वं चित्राः शब्दाश्च पावके ।
अपाकजश्चाशीतोष्णो ध्वनिश्चित्रश्च मारुते ॥ 296
9.m: Bright white radiance, heat, and varied sounds are in fire. / Touch not produced by heat, neither cold nor hot, and varied sound are in wind. // 296

9.s:
varṇātmako dhvaniḥ śabdapratibimbānyathāmbare /
yattu na sparśavaddharmaḥ śabda ityādi bhaṇyate // 297
9.d:
वर्णात्मको ध्वनिः शब्दप्रतिबिम्बान्यथाम्बरे ।
यत्तु न स्पर्शवद्धर्मः शब्द इत्यादि भण्यते ॥ 297
9.m: Sound in the form of articulate phonemes, and as echoes of sound, is in space. / As for what is asserted [by opponents] that sound is not a property possessing touch, and so forth, // 297

9.s:
kāṇādaistatsvapratītiviruddhaṃ kena gṛhyatām /
paṭahe dhvanirityeva bhātyabādhitameva yat // 298
9.d:
काणादैस्तत्स्वप्रतीतिविरुद्धं केन गृह्यताम् ।
पटहे ध्वनिरित्येव भात्यबाधितमेव यत् ॥ 298
9.m: how could that assertion of the Kāṇādas be accepted, since it contradicts one's own direct experience? / For the awareness 'sound is in the drum' appears entirely uncontradicted. // 298

9.s:
na ca hetutvamātreṇa tadādānatvavedanāt /
śrotraṃ cāsmanmate'haṃkṛtkāraṇaṃ tatra tatra tat // 299
9.d:
न च हेतुत्वमात्रेण तदादानत्ववेदनात् ।
श्रोत्रं चास्मन्मतेऽहंकृत्कारणं तत्र तत्र तत् ॥ 299
9.m: Nor is this [awareness] due merely to causality, since it is experienced as its recipient material cause. / And in our doctrine the ear has the ego as its cause, and in each respective place it // 299

9.s:
vṛttibhāgīti taddeśaṃ śabdaṃ gṛhṇātyalaṃ tathā /
yastvāha śrotramākāśaṃ karṇasaṃyogabheditam // 300
9.d:
वृत्तिभागीति तद्देशं शब्दं गृह्णात्यलं तथा ।
यस्त्वाह श्रोत्रमाकाशं कर्णसंयोगभेदितम् ॥ 300
9.m: possesses a cognitive function, and thus fully grasps the sound in that place. / As for him who says that the ear is space delimited by its contact with the ear-canal, // 300

9.s:
śabdajaḥ śabda āgatya śabdabuddhiṃ prasūyate /
tasya mande'pi murajadhvanāvākarṇake sati // 301
9.d:
शब्दजः शब्द आगत्य शब्दबुद्धिं प्रसूयते ।
तस्य मन्देऽपि मुरजध्वनावाकर्णके सति ॥ 301
9.m: [and that] sound produced by sound arrives and generates the cognition of sound— / even when the drum-sound is faint and has reached the ear, // 301

9.s:
amutra śrutireṣeti dūre saṃvedanaṃ katham /
nahi śabdajaśabdasya dūrādūraravoditeḥ // 302
9.d:
अमुत्र श्रुतिरेषेति दूरे संवेदनं कथम् ।
नहि शब्दजशब्दस्य दूरादूररवोदितेः ॥ 302
9.m: how could there be the awareness at a distance: 'this hearing is over there'? / For sound generated by sound, arising from a distant or near sound, // 302

9.s:
śrotrākāśagatasyāsti dūrādūrasvabhāvatā /
na cāsau prathamaḥ śabdastāvadvyāpīti yujyate // 303
9.d:
श्रोत्राकाशगतस्यास्ति दूरादूरस्वभावता ।
न चासौ प्रथमः शब्दस्तावद्व्यापीति युज्यते ॥ 303
9.m: and situated in the space of the ear, does not possess the nature of being distant or near. / Nor is it reasonable that this initial sound pervades that far: // 303

9.s:
tatrasthaiḥ saha tīvrātmā śrūyamāṇastvanena tu /
kathaṃ śrūyeta mandaḥsannahi dharmāntarāśrayaḥ // 304
9.d:
तत्रस्थैः सह तीव्रात्मा श्रूयमाणस्त्वनेन तु ।
कथं श्रूयेत मन्दःसन्नहि धर्मान्तराश्रयः ॥ 304
9.m: for while heard by those standing near as intense, how could it, / being faint, be heard by this [distant person]? For it cannot be the substratum of opposing properties. // 304

9.s:
etaccānyairapākāri bahudheti vṛthā punaḥ /
nāyastaṃ patitāghātadāne ko hi na paṇḍitaḥ // 305
9.d:
एतच्चान्यैरपाकारि बहुधेति वृथा पुनः ।
नायस्तं पतिताघातदाने को हि न पण्डितः ॥ 305
9.m: And this has been refuted in many ways by others, so no further effort / was made [here] in vain; for who is not an expert at striking one who has already fallen? // 305

9.s:
amīṣāṃ tu dharādīnāṃ yāvāṃstattvagaṇaḥ purā /
guṇādhikatayā tiṣṭhan vyāptā tāvān prakāśate // 306
9.d:
अमीषां तु धरादीनां यावांस्तत्त्वगणः पुरा ।
गुणाधिकतया तिष्ठन् व्याप्ता तावान् प्रकाशते ॥ 306
9.m: Now, the entire host of tattvas that existed prior to these [gross elements] beginning with earth / is revealed as a pervader, abiding with an increase of qualities. // 306

9.s:
vyāpyavyāpakatā yaiṣā tattvānāṃ darśitā kila /
sā guṇādhikyataḥ siddhā na hetutvānna lāghavāt // 307
9.d:
व्याप्यव्यापकता यैषा तत्त्वानां दर्शिता किल ।
सा गुणाधिक्यतः सिद्धा न हेतुत्वान्न लाघवात् ॥ 307
9.m: This relation of pervaded and pervader of the tattvas that has indeed been shown / is established through an increase of qualities, not from causality nor from lightness. // 307

9.s:
ahetunāpi rāgo hi vyāpto vidyādinā sphuṭam /
tadvinā na bhavedyattadvyāptamityucyate yataḥ // 308
9.d:
अहेतुनापि रागो हि व्याप्तो विद्यादिना स्फुटम् ।
तद्विना न भवेद्यत्तद्व्याप्तमित्युच्यते यतः ॥ 308
9.m: For attachment is clearly pervaded by vidyā and the rest even without being its cause; / for whatever cannot exist without something is said to be pervaded by it. // 308

9.s:
na lāghavaṃ ca nāmāsti kiṃcidatra svadarśane /
guṇādhikyādato jñeyā vyāpyavyāpakatā sphuṭā // 309
9.d:
न लाघवं च नामास्ति किंचिदत्र स्वदर्शने ।
गुणाधिक्यादतो ज्ञेया व्याप्यव्यापकता स्फुटा ॥ 309
9.m: Nor is there any so-called 'lightness' in our own doctrine. / Therefore, the relation of pervaded and pervader must be clearly understood to arise from the increase of qualities. // 309

9.s:
yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmādūrdhva ucyate /
ūrdhvatā vyāptṛtā śrīmanmālinīvijaye sphuṭā // 310
9.d:
यो हि यस्माद्गुणोत्कृष्टः स तस्मादूर्ध्व उच्यते ।
ऊर्ध्वता व्याप्तृता श्रीमन्मालिनीविजये स्फुटा ॥ 310
9.m: For whatever is superior to something in qualities is said to be higher than it; / that being higher is being a pervader is clear in the venerable Mālinīvijaya. // 310

9.s:
ataḥ śivatvātprabhṛti prakāśatāsvarūpamādāya nijātmani dhruvam /
samastatattvāvalidharmasaṃcayairvibhāti bhūrvyāptṛtayā sthitairalam // 311
9.d:
अतः शिवत्वात्प्रभृति प्रकाशतास्वरूपमादाय निजात्मनि ध्रुवम् ।
समस्ततत्त्वावलिधर्मसंचयैर्विभाति भूर्व्याप्तृतया स्थितैरलम् ॥ 311
9.m: Therefore, taking the essential nature of luminosity into its own self, constant from the state of Śiva onward, / earth fully appears through the assemblies of properties of all the series of tattvas, abiding as their pervader. // 311

9.s:
evaṃ jalāderapi śaktitattvaparyantadhāmno vapurasti tādṛk /
kiṃ tūttaraṃ śaktitayaiva tattvaṃ pūrva tu taddharmatayeti bhedaḥ // 312
9.d:
एवं जलादेरपि शक्तितत्त्वपर्यन्तधाम्नो वपुरस्ति तादृक् ।
किं तूत्तरं शक्तितयैव तत्त्वं पूर्व तु तद्धर्मतयेति भेदः ॥ 312
9.m: In this way, water and the others too, up to the realm of the tattva of śakti, have such a nature; / the distinction, however, is that a higher tattva exists as śakti, while a lower exists as its property. // 312

9.s:
anuttaraprakriyāyāṃ vaitatyena pradarśitam /
etat tasmāt tataḥ paśyedvistarārthī vivecakaḥ // 313
9.d:
अनुत्तरप्रक्रियायां वैतत्येन प्रदर्शितम् ।
एतत् तस्मात् ततः पश्येद्विस्तरार्थी विवेचकः ॥ 313
9.m: This has been shown in detail in the Anuttaraprakriyā; / therefore, a discriminating person desiring detailed explanation should look there. // 313

9.s: iti tattvasyarūpasya kṛtaṃ samyak prakāśanam // 314
9.d: इति तत्त्वस्यरूपस्य कृतं सम्यक् प्रकाशनम् ॥ 314
9.m: Thus the nature of the tattvas has been correctly revealed. // 314

10.s: ucyate trikaśāstrekarahasyaṃ tattvabhedanam // 1
10.d: उच्यते त्रिकशास्त्रेकरहस्यं तत्त्वभेदनम् ॥ 1
10.m: The differentiation of tattvas, the singular secret of the Trika teachings, is now explained. // 1b

10.s:
teṣāmamīṣāṃ tattvānāṃ svavargeṣvanugāminām /
bhedāntaramapi proktaṃ śāstre'tra śrītrikābhidhe // 2
10.d:
तेषाममीषां तत्त्वानां स्ववर्गेष्वनुगामिनाम् ।
भेदान्तरमपि प्रोक्तं शास्त्रेऽत्र श्रीत्रिकाभिधे ॥ 2
10.m: A further differentiation of these tattvas that follow their respective categories / is also taught in this scripture named the venerable Trika. // 2

10.s:
śaktimacchaktibhedena dharādyaṃ mūlapaścimam /
bhidyate pañcadaśadhā svarūpeṇa sahānarāt // 3
10.d:
शक्तिमच्छक्तिभेदेन धराद्यं मूलपश्चिमम् ।
भिद्यते पञ्चदशधा स्वरूपेण सहानरात् ॥ 3
10.m: Through the distinction between possessor of power and power, [each tattva] from earth to the ultimate root / is divided fifteenfold, together with its essential nature, continuously. // 3

10.s:
kalāntaṃ bhedayugghīnaṃ rudravatpralayākalaḥ /
tadvanmāyā ca navadhā jñākalāḥ saptadhā punaḥ // 4
10.d:
कलान्तं भेदयुग्घीनं रुद्रवत्प्रलयाकलः ।
तद्वन्माया च नवधा ज्ञाकलाः सप्तधा पुनः ॥ 4
10.m: Up to kalā, it is without a pair of divisions, like Rudra; the pralayākala / is like that, and māyā is ninefold; knowers free of instruments, moreover, are sevenfold. // 4

10.s:
mantrāstadīśāḥ pāñcadhye mantreśapatayastridhā /
śivo na bhidyate svaikaprakāśaghanacinmayaḥ // 5
10.d:
मन्त्रास्तदीशाः पाञ्चध्ये मन्त्रेशपतयस्त्रिधा ।
शिवो न भिद्यते स्वैकप्रकाशघनचिन्मयः ॥ 5
10.m: Mantras and their lords are fivefold; the supreme lords of mantras are threefold; / Śiva is not divided, consisting of pure consciousness compacted of his own unique luminosity. // 5

10.s:
śivo mantramaheśeśamantrā akalayukkalī /
śaktimantaḥ sapta tathā śaktayastaccaturdaśa // 6
10.d:
शिवो मन्त्रमहेशेशमन्त्रा अकलयुक्कली ।
शक्तिमन्तः सप्त तथा शक्तयस्तच्चतुर्दश ॥ 6
10.m: Śiva, mantramaheśvaras, mantreśvaras, mantras, those endowed with no kalā, those with kalā: / these possessors of power are seven, and likewise their powers are [seven]; that makes fourteen. // 6

10.s:
svaṃ svarūpaṃ pañcadaśaṃ tadbhūḥ pañcadaśātmikā /
tathāhi tisro devasya śaktayo varṇitāḥ purā // 7
10.d:
स्वं स्वरूपं पञ्चदशं तद्भूः पञ्चदशात्मिका ।
तथाहि तिस्रो देवस्य शक्तयो वर्णिताः पुरा ॥ 7
10.m: Its own essential nature is the fifteenth; hence earth has fifteen forms. / To explain: three powers of the Lord were described earlier; // 7

10.s:
tā eva mātṛmāmeyatrairūpyeṇa vyavasthitāḥ /
parāṃśo mātṛrūpo'tra pramāṇāṃśaḥ parāparaḥ // 8
10.d:
ता एव मातृमामेयत्रैरूप्येण व्यवस्थिताः ।
परांशो मातृरूपोऽत्र प्रमाणांशः परापरः ॥ 8
10.m: they indeed abide in the threefold form of knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge. / Here, the supreme aspect has the form of the knower; the intermediate aspect is the means of knowledge; // 8

10.s:
meyo'paraḥ śaktimāṃśca śaktiḥ svaṃ rūpamityadaḥ /
tatra svarūpaṃ bhūmeryatpṛthagjaḍamavasthitam // 9
10.d:
मेयोऽपरः शक्तिमांश्च शक्तिः स्वं रूपमित्यदः ।
तत्र स्वरूपं भूमेर्यत्पृथग्जडमवस्थितम् ॥ 9
10.m: the lower aspect is the object of knowledge; and the possessor of power, power, and own nature are this: / in that regard, the essential nature of earth is that which abides distinct as insentient, // 9

10.s:
mātṛmānādyupadhibhirasaṃjātoparāgakam /
sakalādiśivāntaistu mātṛbhirvedyatāsya yā // 10
10.d:
मातृमानाद्युपधिभिरसंजातोपरागकम् ।
सकलादिशिवान्तैस्तु मातृभिर्वेद्यतास्य या ॥ 10
10.m: with no tint produced by conditioning factors such as knower and means of knowledge. / But its state of being known by the knowers from sakala up to Śiva— // 10

10.s:
śaktimadbhiranudbhūtaśaktibhiḥ sapta tadbhidaḥ /
sakalādiśivāntānāṃ śaktiṣūdrecitātmasu // 11
10.d:
शक्तिमद्भिरनुद्भूतशक्तिभिः सप्त तद्भिदः ।
सकलादिशिवान्तानां शक्तिषूद्रेचितात्मसु ॥ 11
10.m: as possessors of power whose powers are unmanifest—constitutes seven divisions of it; / when the powers of those from sakala up to Śiva have become intensified in their nature, // 11

10.s:
vedyatājanitāḥ sapta bhedā iti caturdaśa /
sakalasya pramāṇāṃśo yo'sau vidyākalātmakaḥ // 12
10.d:
वेद्यताजनिताः सप्त भेदा इति चतुर्दश ।
सकलस्य प्रमाणांशो योऽसौ विद्याकलात्मकः ॥ 12
10.m: there are seven divisions produced by being known [by them]: thus there are fourteen. / The aspect of the means of knowledge belonging to a sakala, which consists of vidyā and kalā, // 12

10.s:
sāmānyātmā sa śaktitve gaṇito natu tadbhidaḥ /
layākalasya mānāṃśaḥ sa eva paramasphuṭaḥ // 13
10.d:
सामान्यात्मा स शक्तित्वे गणितो नतु तद्भिदः ।
लयाकलस्य मानांशः स एव परमस्फुटः ॥ 13
10.m: is generic in nature and is counted as power, but not as its divisions. / The aspect of the means of knowledge of a layākala is that very same [vidyā and kalā] in an extremely clear state. // 13

10.s:
jñānākalasya mānaṃ tu galadvidyākalāvṛti /
aśuddhavidyākalanādhvaṃsasaṃskārasaṃgatā // 14
10.d:
ज्ञानाकलस्य मानं तु गलद्विद्याकलावृति ।
अशुद्धविद्याकलनाध्वंससंस्कारसंगता ॥ 14
10.m: The means of knowledge of a knower free of instruments has the covering of vidyā and kalā dropping away, / joined with the latent impression of the destruction of the grasp of impure knowledge. // 14

10.s:
prabubhutsuḥ śuddhavidyā santrāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ bhavet /
prabuddhā śuddhavidyā tu tatsaṃskāreṇa saṃgatā // 15
10.d:
प्रबुभुत्सुः शुद्धविद्या सन्त्राणां करणं भवेत् ।
प्रबुद्धा शुद्धविद्या तु तत्संस्कारेण संगता ॥ 15
10.m: Pure knowledge desiring awakening would be the instrument of mantras; / pure knowledge fully awakened, however, joined with that latent impression, // 15

10.s:
mānaṃ mantreśvarāṇāṃ syāttatsaṃskāravivarjitā /
mānaṃ mantramaheśānāṃ karaṇaṃ śaktirucyate // 16
10.d:
मानं मन्त्रेश्वराणां स्यात्तत्संस्कारविवर्जिता ।
मानं मन्त्रमहेशानां करणं शक्तिरुच्यते ॥ 16
10.m: would be the means of knowledge of mantreśvaras; devoid of that latent impression, / it is the means of knowledge of mantramaheśas: this instrument is called śakti. // 16

10.s:
svātantryamātrasadbhāvā yā tvicchā śaktiraiśvarī /
śivasya saiva karaṇaṃ tayā vetti karoti ca // 17
10.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यमात्रसद्भावा या त्विच्छा शक्तिरैश्वरी ।
शिवस्य सैव करणं तया वेत्ति करोति च ॥ 17
10.m: The power of will belonging to the Lord, however, which exists purely as absolute autonomy, / is the very instrument of Śiva; by means of it he knows and acts. // 17

10.s:
ā śivātsakalāntaṃ ye mātāraḥ sapta te dvidhā /
nyagbhūtodriktaśaktitvāttadbhedo vedyabhedakaḥ // 18
10.d:
आ शिवात्सकलान्तं ये मातारः सप्त ते द्विधा ।
न्यग्भूतोद्रिक्तशक्तित्वात्तद्भेदो वेद्यभेदकः ॥ 18
10.m: The seven knowers from Śiva down to sakala are twofold / because their power is either subordinated or intensified; this division differentiates the object of knowledge. // 18

10.s:
tathāhi vedyatā nāma bhāvasyaiva nijaṃ vapuḥ /
caitreṇa vedyaṃ vedmīti kiṃhyatra pratibhāsatām // 19
10.d:
तथाहि वेद्यता नाम भावस्यैव निजं वपुः ।
चैत्रेण वेद्यं वेद्मीति किंह्यत्र प्रतिभासताम् ॥ 19
10.m: To explain: the state of being known is indeed the intrinsic form of an existing thing; / for what else could appear here when one thinks, 'I know the knowable object with Caitra'? // 19

10.s:
nanu caitrīyavijñānamātramatra prakāśate /
vedyatākhyastu no dharmo bhāti bhāvasya nīlavat // 20
10.d:
ननु चैत्रीयविज्ञानमात्रमत्र प्रकाशते ।
वेद्यताख्यस्तु नो धर्मो भाति भावस्य नीलवत् ॥ 20
10.m: [Opponent:] 'Surely here only the cognition belonging to Caitra is revealed, / but the property called "being known" does not appear as belonging to the object, as blueness does.' // 20

10.s:
vedyatā ca svabhāvena dharmo bhāvasya cettataḥ /
sarvānpratyeva vedyaḥ syāddhaṭanīlādidharmavat // 21
10.d:
वेद्यता च स्वभावेन धर्मो भावस्य चेत्ततः ।
सर्वान्प्रत्येव वेद्यः स्याद्धटनीलादिधर्मवत् ॥ 21
10.m:
And if object-hood is by nature a property of an entity, then
it would be known to all without exception, just like properties such as being a blue pot.

10.s:
atha vedakasaṃvittibalādvedyatvadharmabhāk /
bhāvastathāpi doṣo'sau kuvindakṛtavastravat // 22
10.d:
अथ वेदकसंवित्तिबलाद्वेद्यत्वधर्मभाक् ।
भावस्तथापि दोषोऽसौ कुविन्दकृतवस्त्रवत् ॥ 22
10.m:
Now, if through the power of the consciousness of the knower the entity possesses the property of object-hood,
even so, this flaw remains, like cloth made by a weaver.

10.s:
vedyatākhyastu yo dharmaḥ so'vedyaścetkhapuṣpavat /
vedyaścedasti tatrāpi vedyetatyanavasthitiḥ // 23
10.d:
वेद्यताख्यस्तु यो धर्मः सोऽवेद्यश्चेत्खपुष्पवत् ।
वेद्यश्चेदस्ति तत्रापि वेद्येतत्यनवस्थितिः ॥ 23
10.m:
Furthermore, if that property called object-hood is unmanifest, it is like a sky-flower;
if it is manifest, then there too [another] object-hood would apply, leading to infinite regress.

10.s:
tato na kiṃcidvedyaṃ syānmūrchitaṃ tu jagadbhavet /
nanu vijñātrupādhyaṃ śo paskṛtaṃ vapurucyatām // 24
10.d:
ततो न किंचिद्वेद्यं स्यान्मूर्छितं तु जगद्भवेत् ।
ननु विज्ञात्रुपाध्यं शो पस्कृतं वपुरुच्यताम् ॥ 24
10.m:
Therefore nothing would be an object of knowledge, and the world would be plunged into stupor.
[Opponent:] But surely it should be stated that the entity has a form qualified by a part consisting of the knower,

10.s:
bhāvasyārthaprakāśātma yathā jñānamidaṃ tvasat /
ekavijñātṛvedyatve na jñātrantaravedyatā // 25
10.d:
भावस्यार्थप्रकाशात्म यथा ज्ञानमिदं त्वसत् ।
एकविज्ञातृवेद्यत्वे न ज्ञात्रन्तरवेद्यता ॥ 25
10.m:
which consists of the manifestation of the object, just like knowledge—[Reply:] but this is incorrect.
If it were knowable by one knower, it would not be knowable by another knower;

10.s:
samastajñātṛvedyatve naikavijñātṛvedyatā /
tasmānna vedyatā nāma bhāvadharmo'sti kaścana // 26
10.d:
समस्तज्ञातृवेद्यत्वे नैकविज्ञातृवेद्यता ।
तस्मान्न वेद्यता नाम भावधर्मोऽस्ति कश्चन ॥ 26
10.m:
if it were knowable by all knowers, it could not be knowable by a single knower.
Therefore there is no property of an entity at all called object-hood.

10.s:
bhāvasya vedyatā saiva saṃvido yaḥ samudbhavaḥ /
arthagrahaṇarūpaṃ hi yatra vijñānamātmani // 27
10.d:
भावस्य वेद्यता सैव संविदो यः समुद्भवः ।
अर्थग्रहणरूपं हि यत्र विज्ञानमात्मनि ॥ 27
10.m:
[Opponent:] The object-hood of an entity is merely the arising of consciousness;
for when knowledge having the nature of apprehending an object inheres in the self,

10.s:
samavaiti prakāśyo'rthastaṃ pratyeṣaiva vedyatā /
atra brūmaḥ padārthānāṃ na dharmo yadi vedyatā // 28
10.d:
समवैति प्रकाश्योऽर्थस्तं प्रत्येषैव वेद्यता ।
अत्र ब्रूमः पदार्थानां न धर्मो यदि वेद्यता ॥ 28
10.m:
in relation to that object to be illuminated, this alone is its object-hood.
To this we reply: if object-hood is not a property of things,

10.s:
avedyā eva te saṃsyurjñāne satyapi varṇite /
yathāhi pṛthubudhnādirūpe kumbhasya satyapi // 29
10.d:
अवेद्या एव ते संस्युर्ज्ञाने सत्यपि वर्णिते ।
यथाहि पृथुबुध्नादिरूपे कुम्भस्य सत्यपि ॥ 29
10.m:
they would be entirely unknowable, even when knowledge as described exists.
For just as, although the form of a pot possessing a broad base and the like exists,

10.s:
atadātmā paṭo naiti pṛthubudhnādirūpatām /
tathā satyapi vijñāne vijñātṛsamavāyini // 30
10.d:
अतदात्मा पटो नैति पृथुबुध्नादिरूपताम् ।
तथा सत्यपि विज्ञाने विज्ञातृसमवायिनि ॥ 30
10.m:
a cloth, not having that nature, does not attain the form of having a broad base and the like;
even so, although knowledge inheres in the knower,

10.s:
avedyadharmakā bhāvāḥ kathaṃ vedyatvamāpnuyuḥ /
anarthaḥ sumahāṃścaiṣa dṛśyatāṃ vastu yatsvayam // 31
10.d:
अवेद्यधर्मका भावाः कथं वेद्यत्वमाप्नुयुः ।
अनर्थः सुमहांश्चैष दृश्यतां वस्तु यत्स्वयम् ॥ 31
10.m:
how could entities, which lack the property of knowability, attain object-hood?
Moreover, observe this very great absurdity: that an entity, which of itself

10.s:
prakāśātma na tatsaṃviccāprakāśā tadāśrayaḥ /
aprakāśo manodīpacakṣurādi tathaiva tat // 32
10.d:
प्रकाशात्म न तत्संविच्चाप्रकाशा तदाश्रयः ।
अप्रकाशो मनोदीपचक्षुरादि तथैव तत् ॥ 32
10.m:
does not consist of luminosity, consciousness [itself] is unilluminated, its locus
is unilluminated, and mind, lamp, eye, and the like are likewise so.

10.s:
kiṃ tatprakāśatāṃ nāma supte jagati sarvataḥ /
jñānasyārthaprakāśatvaṃ nanu rūpaṃ pradīpavat // 33
10.d:
किं तत्प्रकाशतां नाम सुप्ते जगति सर्वतः ।
ज्ञानस्यार्थप्रकाशत्वं ननु रूपं प्रदीपवत् ॥ 33
10.m:
With the whole world utterly asleep, what indeed could be illuminated?
[Opponent:] Surely the very nature of knowledge is to illuminate objects, like a lamp!

10.s:
apūrvamatra viditaṃ narīnṛtyāmahe tataḥ /
arthaprakāśo jñānasya yadrūpaṃ tannirūpyatām // 34
10.d:
अपूर्वमत्र विदितं नरीनृत्यामहे ततः ।
अर्थप्रकाशो ज्ञानस्य यद्रूपं तन्निरूप्यताम् ॥ 34
10.m:
[Reply:] A unprecedented novelty has been revealed here, so we dance with joy!
Let this nature of knowledge, which is the illumination of an object, be examined:

10.s:
arthaḥ prakāśaścedrūpamartho vā jñānameva vā /
athārthasya prakāśo yastadrūpamiti bhaṇyate // 35
10.d:
अर्थः प्रकाशश्चेद्रूपमर्थो वा ज्ञानमेव वा ।
अथार्थस्य प्रकाशो यस्तद्रूपमिति भण्यते ॥ 35
10.m:
if the object is luminosity, is its nature the object or knowledge itself?
Or is it said that its nature is the illumination of an object?

10.s:
ṣaṣṭhī kartari cedukto doṣa eva duruddharaḥ /
atha karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyeṣā ṇyarthastatra hṛdi sthitaḥ // 36
10.d:
षष्ठी कर्तरि चेदुक्तो दोष एव दुरुद्धरः ।
अथ कर्मणि षष्ठ्येषा ण्यर्थस्तत्र हृदि स्थितः ॥ 36
10.m:
If the genitive has an agentive sense, the very flaw stated earlier is irremediable;
if this genitive has an objective sense, then the causative meaning lies at heart.

10.s:
tathā cedaṃ darśayāmaḥ kiṃ prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
aprakāśo'pi naivāsau tathāpi ca na kiṃcana // 37
10.d:
तथा चेदं दर्शयामः किं प्रकाशः प्रकाशते ।
अप्रकाशोऽपि नैवासौ तथापि च न किंचन ॥ 37
10.m:
In that case, we show this: does luminosity shine forth?
Even if it is unilluminated, it does not exist, and even so, nothing at all [is illuminated].

10.s:
tarhi loke kathaṃ ṇyarthaḥ ucyate cetanasthitau /
mukhyo ṇyarthasya viṣayo jaḍeṣu tvaupacārikaḥ // 38
10.d:
तर्हि लोके कथं ण्यर्थः उच्यते चेतनस्थितौ ।
मुख्यो ण्यर्थस्य विषयो जडेषु त्वौपचारिकः ॥ 38
10.m:
How then is the causative sense used in worldly usage? It is explained: in the domain of the conscious,
the causative sense has its primary application, but with regard to insentient things it is metaphorical.

10.s:
tathāhi gantuṃ śakto'pi caitro'nyāyattatāṃ gateḥ /
manvāna eva vaktyasmi gamitaḥ svāmineti hi // 39
10.d:
तथाहि गन्तुं शक्तोऽपि चैत्रोऽन्यायत्ततां गतेः ।
मन्वान एव वक्त्यस्मि गमितः स्वामिनेति हि ॥ 39
10.m:
For instance, Caitra, although capable of walking, thinking that his walking is dependent on another,
says: 'Indeed, I was made to walk by my master.'

10.s:
svāmyapyasya gatau śaktiṃ buddhvā svādhīnatāṃ sphuṭam /
paśyannivṛttimāśaṃkya gamayāmīti bhāṣate // 40
10.d:
स्वाम्यप्यस्य गतौ शक्तिं बुद्ध्वा स्वाधीनतां स्फुटम् ।
पश्यन्निवृत्तिमाशंक्य गमयामीति भाषते ॥ 40
10.m:
The master, too, knowing his capacity to walk and clearly seeing his obedience,
suspecting that he might stop, says: 'I make him walk.'

10.s:
preryaprerakayorevaṃ maulikī ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ /
tadabhiprāyato'nyo'pi loke vyavaharettathā // 41
10.d:
प्रेर्यप्रेरकयोरेवं मौलिकी ण्यर्थसंगतिः ।
तदभिप्रायतोऽन्योऽपि लोके व्यवहरेत्तथा ॥ 41
10.m:
Thus the primary connection of the causative sense occurs between the impeller and the impelled;
based on that intention, another person also speaks similarly in worldly usage.

10.s:
śaraṃ gamayatītyatra punarvegākhyasaṃskriyām /
vidadhatprerakammanya upacāreṇa jāyate // 42
10.d:
शरं गमयतीत्यत्र पुनर्वेगाख्यसंस्क्रियाम् ।
विदधत्प्रेरकम्मन्य उपचारेण जायते ॥ 42
10.m:
When one says, 'He makes the arrow go,'
producing an impulse called velocity, he considers himself an impeller only metaphorically.

10.s:
vāyuradriṃ pātayatītyatra dvāvapi tau jaḍau /
draṣṭṛbhiḥ prerakapreryavapuṣā parikalpitau // 43
10.d:
वायुरद्रिं पातयतीत्यत्र द्वावपि तौ जडौ ।
द्रष्टृभिः प्रेरकप्रेर्यवपुषा परिकल्पितौ ॥ 43
10.m:
In 'The wind brings down the mountain,' both are insentient,
[yet] they are conceptualized by observers in the guise of impeller and impelled.

10.s:
itthaṃ jaḍena saṃbandhe na mukhyā ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ /
āstāmanyatra vitatametadvistarato mayā // 44
10.d:
इत्थं जडेन संबन्धे न मुख्या ण्यर्थसंगतिः ।
आस्तामन्यत्र विततमेतद्विस्तरतो मया ॥ 44
10.m:
Thus, in relation to the insentient, the causative connection is not primary.
Let this rest; I have discussed this extensively elsewhere.

10.s:
arthe prakāśanā seyamupacārastato bhavet /
astu cedbhāsate tarhi sa eva patadadrivat // 45
10.d:
अर्थे प्रकाशना सेयमुपचारस्ततो भवेत् ।
अस्तु चेद्भासते तर्हि स एव पतदद्रिवत् ॥ 45
10.m:
Therefore, this illumination in the object would be metaphorical;
if that be accepted, then that [object] alone appears, like the falling mountain.

10.s:
upacāre nimittena kenāpi kila bhūyate /
vāyuḥ pātayatītyatra nimittaṃ tatkṛtā kriyā // 46
10.d:
उपचारे निमित्तेन केनापि किल भूयते ।
वायुः पातयतीत्यत्र निमित्तं तत्कृता क्रिया ॥ 46
10.m:
For a metaphor requires some basis or other;
in 'The wind brings down [the mountain],' the basis is the action performed by it,

10.s:
girau yenaiṣa saṃyoganāśādbhraṃśaṃ prapadyate /
iha tu jñānamarthasya na kiṃcitkarameva tat // 47
10.d:
गिरौ येनैष संयोगनाशाद्भ्रंशं प्रपद्यते ।
इह तु ज्ञानमर्थस्य न किंचित्करमेव तत् ॥ 47
10.m:
whereby the mountain, through the destruction of its conjunction, undergoes a fall;
but here, knowledge does nothing whatsoever to the object.

10.s:
upacāraḥ kathaṃ nāma bhavetso'pi hyavastusan /
aprakāśita evārthaḥ prakāśatvopacārataḥ // 48
10.d:
उपचारः कथं नाम भवेत्सोऽपि ह्यवस्तुसन् ।
अप्रकाशित एवार्थः प्रकाशत्वोपचारतः ॥ 48
10.m:
How could a metaphor occur if it is entirely unreal?
An object is completely unilluminated through a metaphorical attribution of luminosity.

10.s:
tādṛgeva śiśuḥ kiṃ hi dahatyagnyupacārataḥ /
śiśau vahnyupacāre yadbījaṃ taikṣṇyādi tacca sat // 49
10.d:
तादृगेव शिशुः किं हि दहत्यग्न्युपचारतः ।
शिशौ वह्न्युपचारे यद्बीजं तैक्ष्ण्यादि तच्च सत् ॥ 49
10.m:
Does a child burn just because he is metaphorically called fire?
In metaphorically calling a child fire, the basis—sharpness and the like—is real.

10.s:
prakāśatvopacāre tu kiṃ bījaṃ yatra satyatā /
siddhe hi cetane yukta upacāraḥ sa hi sphuṭam // 50
10.d:
प्रकाशत्वोपचारे तु किं बीजं यत्र सत्यता ।
सिद्धे हि चेतने युक्त उपचारः स हि स्फुटम् ॥ 50
10.m:
But what is the basis in the metaphorical attribution of luminosity, where truth lies?
For only when a conscious being is established is metaphor appropriate, clearly so;

10.s:
adhyāropātmakaḥ so'pi pratisaṃdhānajīvitaḥ /
na cādyāpi kimapyasti cetanaṃ jñānamapyadaḥ // 51
10.d:
अध्यारोपात्मकः सोऽपि प्रतिसंधानजीवितः ।
न चाद्यापि किमप्यस्ति चेतनं ज्ञानमप्यदः ॥ 51
10.m:
even that consists of superimposition, enlivened by synthesis.
And here, not even a single conscious being exists, nor is this knowledge [conscious];

10.s:
aprakāśaṃ tadanyena tatprakāśe'pyayaṃ vidhiḥ /
nanu pradīpo rūpasya prakāśaḥ kathamīdṛśam // 52
10.d:
अप्रकाशं तदन्येन तत्प्रकाशेऽप्ययं विधिः ।
ननु प्रदीपो रूपस्य प्रकाशः कथमीदृशम् ॥ 52
10.m:
it is unilluminated; even if it is illuminated by another, this same rule applies.
[Opponent:] Surely a lamp is the illumination of visible form; how can this be so?

10.s:
atrāpi na vahantyetāḥ kiṃ nu yuktivikalpanāḥ /
yādṛśā svena rūpeṇa dīpo rūpaṃ prakāśayet // 53
10.d:
अत्रापि न वहन्त्येताः किं नु युक्तिविकल्पनाः ।
यादृशा स्वेन रूपेण दीपो रूपं प्रकाशयेत् ॥ 53
10.m:
Do these dialectical arguments not hold sway here as well?
In the manner in which a lamp illuminates visible form through its own form,

10.s:
tādṛśā svayamapyeṣa bhāti jñānaṃ tu no tathā /
pradīpaścaiṣa bhāvānāṃ prakāśatvaṃ dadā[dhā]tyalam // 54
10.d:
तादृशा स्वयमप्येष भाति ज्ञानं तु नो तथा ।
प्रदीपश्चैष भावानां प्रकाशत्वं ददा[धा]त्यलम् ॥ 54
10.m:
in that same manner it shines by itself; but knowledge does not do so.
And this lamp sufficiently bestows luminosity upon things;

10.s:
anyathā na prakāśerannabhede cedṛśo vidhiḥ /
tasmātprakāśa evāyaṃ pūrvoktaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ // 55
10.d:
अन्यथा न प्रकाशेरन्नभेदे चेदृशो विधिः ।
तस्मात्प्रकाश एवायं पूर्वोक्तः परमः शिवः ॥ 55
10.m:
otherwise, they would not be illuminated; in non-difference, such is the rule.
Therefore, it is this very luminosity, previously described as supreme Śiva,

10.s:
yathā yathā prakāśeta tattadbhāvavapuḥ sphuṭam /
evaṃ ca nīlatā nāma yathā kācitprakāśate // 56
10.d:
यथा यथा प्रकाशेत तत्तद्भाववपुः स्फुटम् ।
एवं च नीलता नाम यथा काचित्प्रकाशते ॥ 56
10.m:
which shines forth clearly in the form of each respective entity.
And just as a particular blueness shines forth,

10.s:
tadvaccakāsti vedyatvaṃ tacca bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam /
phalaṃ prakaṭatārthasya saṃvidveti dvayaṃ tataḥ // 57
10.d:
तद्वच्चकास्ति वेद्यत्वं तच्च भावांशपृष्ठगम् ।
फलं प्रकटतार्थस्य संविद्वेति द्वयं ततः ॥ 57
10.m:
so also shines forth object-hood, and that follows upon a part of the entity.
Therefore, whether the result is the manifestation of the object or consciousness—this pair

10.s:
vipakṣato rakṣitaṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ cāpi tanmithaḥ /
tathāhi nibhṛtaścauraścaitravedyamiti sphuṭam // 58
10.d:
विपक्षतो रक्षितं च संधानं चापि तन्मिथः ।
तथाहि निभृतश्चौरश्चैत्रवेद्यमिति स्फुटम् ॥ 58
10.m:
is protected from the opposing view, and their mutual connection is maintained.
To explain: a hidden thief, clearly understanding

10.s:
buddhvā nādatta evāśu parīpsāvivaśo'pi san /
seyaṃ paśyati māṃ netratribhāgeneti sādaram // 59
10.d:
बुद्ध्वा नादत्त एवाशु परीप्साविवशोऽपि सन् ।
सेयं पश्यति मां नेत्रत्रिभागेनेति सादरम् ॥ 59
10.m:
that a thing is an object known to Caitra, does not seize it at once, even though overcome by craving;
[and thinking] with delight: 'She looks at me with a sidelong glance,'

10.s:
svaṃ dehamamṛteneva siktaṃ paśyati kāmukaḥ /
na caitajjñānasaṃvittimātraṃ bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam // 60
10.d:
स्वं देहममृतेनेव सिक्तं पश्यति कामुकः ।
न चैतज्ज्ञानसंवित्तिमात्रं भावांशपृष्ठगम् ॥ 60
10.m:
a lover sees his body as if sprinkled with nectar;
and this is not mere consciousness of knowledge, but follows upon a part of the entity;

10.s:
arthakriyākaraṃ taccenna dharmaḥ konvasau bhavet /
yaccoktaṃ vedyatādharmā bhāvaḥ sarvānapi prati // 61
10.d:
अर्थक्रियाकरं तच्चेन्न धर्मः कोन्वसौ भवेत् ।
यच्चोक्तं वेद्यताधर्मा भावः सर्वानपि प्रति ॥ 61
10.m:
if it produces causal efficacy, what property would it be if not [object-hood]?
And as for the statement that an entity possessing the property of object-hood would be so towards all,

10.s:
syādityetatsvapakṣaghnaṃ duṣprayogāstravattava /
asmākaṃ tu svaprakāśaśivatāmātravādinām // 62
10.d:
स्यादित्येतत्स्वपक्षघ्नं दुष्प्रयोगास्त्रवत्तव ।
अस्माकं तु स्वप्रकाशशिवतामात्रवादिनाम् ॥ 62
10.m:
this destroys your own position, like a badly aimed missile.
For us, however, who maintain only the self-luminous nature of Śiva,

10.s:
anyaṃ prati cakāstīti vaca eva na vidyate /
sarvānprati ca tannīlaṃ sa ghaṭaśceti yadvacaḥ // 63
10.d:
अन्यं प्रति चकास्तीति वच एव न विद्यते ।
सर्वान्प्रति च तन्नीलं स घटश्चेति यद्वचः ॥ 63
10.m:
the statement 'it shines forth in relation to another' does not even exist.
And as for the claim that 'it is blue to all' and 'it is a pot [to all],'

10.s:
tadapyaviditaprāyaṃ gṛhītaṃ mugdhabuddhibhiḥ /
nahi kālāgnirudrīyakāyāvagatanīlimā // 64
10.d:
तदप्यविदितप्रायं गृहीतं मुग्धबुद्धिभिः ।
नहि कालाग्निरुद्रीयकायावगतनीलिमा ॥ 64
10.m:
even that has been accepted largely without understanding by simple-minded people.
For the blueness perceived in the body of Kālāgnirudra

10.s:
tava nīlaḥ kiṃ nu pīto maivaṃ bhūnnatu nīlakaḥ /
na kaṃcitprati nīlo'sau nīlo vā yaṃ prati sthitaḥ // 65
10.d:
तव नीलः किं नु पीतो मैवं भून्नतु नीलकः ।
न कंचित्प्रति नीलोऽसौ नीलो वा यं प्रति स्थितः ॥ 65
10.m:
is not blue to you; could it be yellow? Let it not be so, yet it is not blue [to you].
It is not blue to anyone, or rather, to whomsoever it is present as blue,

10.s:
taṃ pratyeva sa vedyaḥ syātsaṃkalpadvārako'ntataḥ /
yathā cārthaprakāśātma jñānaṃ saṃgīryate tvayā // 66
10.d:
तं प्रत्येव स वेद्यः स्यात्संकल्पद्वारकोऽन्ततः ।
यथा चार्थप्रकाशात्म ज्ञानं संगीर्यते त्वया ॥ 66
10.m:
in relation to that one alone it would be an object of knowledge, mediated ultimately by conceptual thought.
And just as knowledge consisting of the manifestation of the object is admitted by you,

10.s:
tathā tajjñātṛvedyatvaṃ bhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyatām /
na ca jñātātra niyataḥ kaścijjñāne yathā tava // 67
10.d:
तथा तज्ज्ञातृवेद्यत्वं भावीयं रूपमुच्यताम् ।
न च ज्ञातात्र नियतः कश्चिज्ज्ञाने यथा तव ॥ 67
10.m:
So too, let its knowability by a [particular] knower be declared the nature belonging to the thing.
And no [single] knower is fixed here, just as in the case of your cognition. // 67

10.s:
arthe jñātā yadā yo yastadvedyaṃ vapurucyatām /
tattadvijñātṛvedyatvaṃ sarvānpratyeva bhāsatām // 68
10.d:
अर्थे ज्ञाता यदा यो यस्तद्वेद्यं वपुरुच्यताम् ।
तत्तद्विज्ञातृवेद्यत्वं सर्वान्प्रत्येव भासताम् ॥ 68
10.m:
When whichever knower relates to an object, let that knowable form be spoken of.
Let that knowability by respective knowers shine forth to all indeed. // 68

10.s:
ityevaṃ codayanmanye vrajedbadhiradhuryatām /
nahyanyaṃ prati vai kaṃcidbhāti sā vedyatā tathā // 69
10.d:
इत्येवं चोदयन्मन्ये व्रजेद्बधिरधुर्यताम् ।
नह्यन्यं प्रति वै कंचिद्भाति सा वेद्यता तथा ॥ 69
10.m:
One who objects thus, I consider, would attain the foremost rank among the deaf;
for that knowability does not shine forth to anyone else in that way! // 69

10.s:
bhāvasya rūpamityukte keyamasthānavaidhurī /
anena nītimārgeṇa nirmūlamapasāritā // 70
10.d:
भावस्य रूपमित्युक्ते केयमस्थानवैधुरी ।
अनेन नीतिमार्गेण निर्मूलमपसारिता ॥ 70
10.m:
When it is said to be the 'nature of an entity', what is this groundless agitation?
By this line of reasoning, it is completely removed at its root. // 70

10.s:
anavasthā tathā hyanyairnīlādyaiḥ sadṛśī na sā /
vedyatā kiṃtu dharmo'sau yadyogātsarvadharmavān // 71
10.d:
अनवस्था तथा ह्यन्यैर्नीलाद्यैः सदृशी न सा ।
वेद्यता किंतु धर्मोऽसौ यद्योगात्सर्वधर्मवान् ॥ 71
10.m:
For such an infinite regress does not exist; that knowability is not like other [properties] such as blue,
but it is a property through connection with which a possessor of properties possessing all properties // 71

10.s:
dharmī vedyatvamabhyeti sa sattāsamavāyavat /
brūṣe yathā hi kurute sattā satyasataḥ sataḥ // 72
10.d:
धर्मी वेद्यत्वमभ्येति स सत्तासमवायवत् ।
ब्रूषे यथा हि कुरुते सत्ता सत्यसतः सतः ॥ 72
10.m:
—a subject—attains knowability, just like the inherence of beingness.
For as you say, beingness makes non-existent things existent in an entity; // 72

10.s:
samavāyo'pi saṃśliṣṭaḥ śliṣṭānaśliṣṭatājuṣaḥ /
antyo viśeṣo vyāvṛttirūpo vyāvṛttivarjitān // 73
10.d:
समवायोऽपि संश्लिष्टः श्लिष्टानश्लिष्टताजुषः ।
अन्त्यो विशेषो व्यावृत्तिरूपो व्यावृत्तिवर्जितान् ॥ 73
10.m:
inherence also, conjoined, makes those sharing connection or non-connection connected;
the ultimate differentiator, whose nature is distinction, makes those devoid of distinction // 73

10.s:
vyāvṛttān śvetimā śuklamaśuklaṃ gamanaṃ tathā /
tadvannīlādidharmāṃśayukto dharmī svayaṃ sthitaḥ // 74
10.d:
व्यावृत्तान् श्वेतिमा शुक्लमशुक्लं गमनं तथा ।
तद्वन्नीलादिधर्मांशयुक्तो धर्मी स्वयं स्थितः ॥ 74
10.m:
distinct; whiteness makes the non-white white, and motion likewise [moves the stationary].
In the same way, the subject, standing by itself, endowed with portions of properties such as blue, // 74

10.s:
avedyo vedyatārūpāddharmādvedyatvamāgataḥ /
vedyatā bhāsamānā ca svayaṃ nīlādidharmavat // 75
10.d:
अवेद्यो वेद्यतारूपाद्धर्माद्वेद्यत्वमागतः ।
वेद्यता भासमाना च स्वयं नीलादिधर्मवत् ॥ 75
10.m:
unknowable [in itself], attains knowability from the property consisting of knowability;
and knowability, shining forth by itself like properties such as blue, // 75

10.s:
aprakāśā svaprakāśāddharmādeti prakāśatām /
prakāśe khalu viśrāntiṃ viśvaṃ śrayati cettataḥ // 76
10.d:
अप्रकाशा स्वप्रकाशाद्धर्मादेति प्रकाशताम् ।
प्रकाशे खलु विश्रान्तिं विश्वं श्रयति चेत्ततः ॥ 76
10.m:
unilluminated [in itself], comes to luminosity from a self-luminous property.
If, indeed, the universe takes rest in luminosity, then // 76

10.s:
nānyā kācidapekṣāsya kṛtakṛtyasya sarvataḥ /
yathā ca śivanāthena svātantryādbhāsyate bhidā // 77
10.d:
नान्या काचिदपेक्षास्य कृतकृत्यस्य सर्वतः ।
यथा च शिवनाथेन स्वातन्त्र्याद्भास्यते भिदा ॥ 77
10.m:
it has accomplished all its ends and has no other expectation whatsoever.
And just as difference is illuminated by the Lord Śiva out of absolute autonomy, // 77

10.s:
nīlādivattathaivāyaṃ vedyatā dharma ucyate /
evaṃ siddhaṃ hi vedyatvaṃ bhāvadharmo'stu kā ghṛṇā // 78
10.d:
नीलादिवत्तथैवायं वेद्यता धर्म उच्यते ।
एवं सिद्धं हि वेद्यत्वं भावधर्मोऽस्तु का घृणा ॥ 78
10.m:
just like blue and the rest, so too this property called knowability is explained.
Thus knowability is established; let it be a property of an entity, what shame is there? // 78

10.s:
idaṃ tu cintyaṃ sakalaparyantoktapramātṛbhiḥ /
vedyatvamekarūpaṃ syāccāturdaśyamataḥ kutaḥ // 79
10.d:
इदं तु चिन्त्यं सकलपर्यन्तोक्तप्रमातृभिः ।
वेद्यत्वमेकरूपं स्याच्चातुर्दश्यमतः कुतः ॥ 79
10.m:
This, however, must be considered: with the knowers mentioned up to the sakala,
knowability would be uniform; whence, then, is there a fourteenfold division? // 79

10.s:
ucyate paripūrṇaṃ cedbhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyate /
tadvibhurbhairavo devo bhagavāneva bhaṇyate // 80
10.d:
उच्यते परिपूर्णं चेद्भावीयं रूपमुच्यते ।
तद्विभुर्भैरवो देवो भगवानेव भण्यते ॥ 80
10.m:
The reply is: if the nature belonging to an entity is said to be completely full,
then the all-pervading divine Lord Bhairava alone is spoken of. // 80

10.s:
atha tannijamāhātmyakalpito'ṃśāṃśikākramaḥ /
sahyate kiṃ kṛtaṃ tarhi proktakalpanayānayā // 81
10.d:
अथ तन्निजमाहात्म्यकल्पितोऽंशांशिकाक्रमः ।
सह्यते किं कृतं तर्हि प्रोक्तकल्पनयानया ॥ 81
10.m:
If, on the other hand, the succession of parts and sub-parts fashioned by his own majesty
is accepted, what then is accomplished by this aforementioned assumption? // 81

10.s:
ata eva yadā yena vapuṣā bhāti yadyathā /
tadā tathā tattadrūpamityeṣopaniṣatparā // 82
10.d:
अत एव यदा येन वपुषा भाति यद्यथा ।
तदा तथा तत्तद्रूपमित्येषोपनिषत्परा ॥ 82
10.m:
Therefore, when, through whichever form, something shines forth in whatever manner,
then in that way that is its nature: this is the supreme secret doctrine. // 82

10.s:
caitreṇa vedyaṃ jānāmi dvābhyāṃ bahubhirapyatha /
mantreṇa tanmaheśena śivenodriktaśaktinā // 83
10.d:
चैत्रेण वेद्यं जानामि द्वाभ्यां बहुभिरप्यथ ।
मन्त्रेण तन्महेशेन शिवेनोद्रिक्तशक्तिना ॥ 83
10.m:
‘I know what is to be known by Caitra, or by two, or by many,
or by a mantra, or by that great lord Śiva whose power has surged forth, // 83

10.s:
anyādṛśena vetyevaṃ bhāvo bhāti yathā tathā /
arthakriyādivaicitryamabhyetyaparisaṃkhyayā // 84
10.d:
अन्यादृशेन वेत्येवं भावो भाति यथा तथा ।
अर्थक्रियादिवैचित्र्यमभ्येत्यपरिसंख्यया ॥ 84
10.m:
or by someone of another kind’—in this way, however the entity shines forth,
it attains a manifold variety of causal efficacy and the like beyond counting. // 84

10.s:
tathā hyekāgrasakalasāmājikajanaḥ khalu /
nṛttaṃ gītaṃ sudhāsārasāgaratvena manyate // 85
10.d:
तथा ह्येकाग्रसकलसामाजिकजनः खलु ।
नृत्तं गीतं सुधासारसागरत्वेन मन्यते ॥ 85
10.m:
For thus, indeed, the entire audience, when single-minded,
regards the dance and song as an ocean of the essence of nectar. // 85

10.s:
tata evocyate mallanaṭaprekṣopadeśane /
sarvapramātṛtādātmyaṃ pūrṇarūpānubhāvakam // 86
10.d:
तत एवोच्यते मल्लनटप्रेक्षोपदेशने ।
सर्वप्रमातृतादात्म्यं पूर्णरूपानुभावकम् ॥ 86
10.m:
For that very reason, it is said in the instruction on witnessing wrestlers and actors:
identity with all knowers brings about the experience of the full form. // 86

10.s:
tāvanmātrārthasaṃvittituṣṭāḥ pratyekaśo yadi /
kaḥ saṃbhūya guṇasteṣāṃ pramātraikyaṃ bhavecca kim // 87
10.d:
तावन्मात्रार्थसंवित्तितुष्टाः प्रत्येकशो यदि ।
कः संभूय गुणस्तेषां प्रमात्रैक्यं भवेच्च किम् ॥ 87
10.m:
If each individually were satisfied merely with the consciousness of the object to that extent,
what collective excellence would they have, and what unity of knower would arise? // 87

10.s:
yadā tu tattadvedyatvadharmasaṃdarbhagarbhitam /
tadvastu śuṣkātprāgrūpādanyadyuktamidaṃ tadā // 88
10.d:
यदा तु तत्तद्वेद्यत्वधर्मसंदर्भगर्भितम् ।
तद्वस्तु शुष्कात्प्राग्रूपादन्यद्युक्तमिदं तदा ॥ 88
10.m:
When, however, that entity is pregnant with the fabric of various properties of knowability,
then it is fittingly different from its dry earlier form. // 88

10.s:
śāstre'pi tattadvedyatvaṃ viśiṣṭārthakriyākaram /
bhūyasaiva tathāca śrīmālinīvijayottare // 89
10.d:
शास्त्रेऽपि तत्तद्वेद्यत्वं विशिष्टार्थक्रियाकरम् ।
भूयसैव तथाच श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे ॥ 89
10.m:
In the scripture too, these various states of knowability produce differentiated causal efficacy
in abundant measure; and so it is in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara: // 89

10.s:
tathā ṣaḍvidhamadhvānamanenādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret /
adhiṣṭhānaṃ hi devena yadviśvasya pravedanam // 90
10.d:
तथा षड्विधमध्वानमनेनाधिष्ठितं स्मरेत् ।
अधिष्ठानं हि देवेन यद्विश्वस्य प्रवेदनम् ॥ 90
10.m:
‘Likewise, one should remember that the sixfold path is presided over by this [mantra].’
For the divine being’s presidership is the knowing of the universe; // 90

10.s:
tadīśavedyatvenetthaṃ jñātaṃ prakṛtakāryakṛt /
evaṃ siddhaṃ vedyatākhyo dharmo bhāvasya bhāsate // 91
10.d:
तदीशवेद्यत्वेनेत्थं ज्ञातं प्रकृतकार्यकृत् ।
एवं सिद्धं वेद्यताख्यो धर्मो भावस्य भासते ॥ 91
10.m:
known in this way as knowable by the Lord, it accomplishes the relevant function.
Thus it is established that the property called knowability shines forth as belonging to an entity. // 91

10.s:
tadanābhāsayoge tu svarūpamiti bhaṇyate /
upādhiyogitāśaṅkāmapahastayato'sphuṭam // 92
10.d:
तदनाभासयोगे तु स्वरूपमिति भण्यते ।
उपाधियोगिताशङ्कामपहस्तयतोऽस्फुटम् ॥ 92
10.m:
When it does not shine forth, however, it is spoken of as its own essential nature,
clearing away any indistinct apprehension of connection with an adjunct. // 92

10.s:
svātmano yena vapuṣā bhātyarthastatsvakaṃ vapuḥ /
jānāmi ghaṭamityatra vedyatānuparāgavān // 93
10.d:
स्वात्मनो येन वपुषा भात्यर्थस्तत्स्वकं वपुः ।
जानामि घटमित्यत्र वेद्यतानुपरागवान् ॥ 93
10.m:
Through whichever form belonging to itself an object shines forth, that is its own form.
In the experience ‘I know the pot’, the pot, untouched by knowability, // 93

10.s:
ghaṭa eva svarūpeṇa bhāta ityapadiśyate /
nanu tatra svayaṃvedyabhāvo mantrādyapekṣayā // 94
10.d:
घट एव स्वरूपेण भात इत्यपदिश्यते ।
ननु तत्र स्वयंवेद्यभावो मन्त्राद्यपेक्षया ॥ 94
10.m:
is designated as having shone forth in its own essential nature.
[Objection:] Now, in that case, does not the state of being known by oneself exist, in view of mantras and the like? // 94

10.s:
api cāstyeva nanvastu natu sanpratibhāsate /
avedyameva kālāgnivapurmeroḥ parā diśaḥ // 95
10.d:
अपि चास्त्येव नन्वस्तु नतु सन्प्रतिभासते ।
अवेद्यमेव कालाग्निवपुर्मेरोः परा दिशः ॥ 95
10.m:
[Reply:] It may indeed exist, but it does not shine forth as existing.
The body of the Fire of Time and the farther regions of Mount Meru are completely unknowable; // 95

10.s:
mameti saṃvidi paraṃ śuddhaṃ vastu prakāśate /
bhātatvādvedyamapi tanna vedyatvena bhāsanāt // 96
10.d:
ममेति संविदि परं शुद्धं वस्तु प्रकाशते ।
भातत्वाद्वेद्यमपि तन्न वेद्यत्वेन भासनात् ॥ 96
10.m:
only the pure object shines forth in consciousness as ‘mine’.
Though knowable because it has shone forth, it is not [experienced] through its shining as knowable. // 96

10.s:
avedyameva bhānaṃ hi tathā kamanuyuñjmahe /
evaṃ pañcadaśātmeyaṃ dharā tadvajjalādayaḥ // 97
10.d:
अवेद्यमेव भानं हि तथा कमनुयुञ्ज्महे ।
एवं पञ्चदशात्मेयं धरा तद्वज्जलादयः ॥ 97
10.m:
Its manifestation is indeed unknowable; how could we challenge that?
Thus this earth possesses fifteen forms, and similarly water and the rest, // 97

10.s:
avyaktāntā yato'styeṣāṃ sakalaṃ prati vedyatā /
yattūcyate kalādyena dharāntena samanvitāḥ // 98
10.d:
अव्यक्तान्ता यतोऽस्त्येषां सकलं प्रति वेद्यता ।
यत्तूच्यते कलाद्येन धरान्तेन समन्विताः ॥ 98
10.m:
extending up to the unmanifest, since they possess knowability with respect to a sakala.
As for what is said: ‘Those endowed [with tattvas] from kalā to earth // 98

10.s:
sakalā iti tatkośaṣaṭkodrekopalakṣaṇam /
udbhūtāśuddhacidrāgakalādirasakañcukāḥ // 99
10.d:
सकला इति तत्कोशषट्कोद्रेकोपलक्षणम् ।
उद्भूताशुद्धचिद्रागकलादिरसकञ्चुकाः ॥ 99
10.m:
are sakalas,’ that is an indicative mark of the predominance of the six sheaths.
They have the cuirasses of the flavor of kalā and so forth, in which impure consciousness and attachment have arisen. // 99

10.s:
sakalālayasaṃjñāstu nyagbhūtākhilakañcukāḥ /
jñānākalāstu dhvastaitatkañcukā iti nirṇayaḥ // 100
10.d:
सकलालयसंज्ञास्तु न्यग्भूताखिलकञ्चुकाः ।
ज्ञानाकलास्तु ध्वस्तैतत्कञ्चुका इति निर्णयः ॥ 100
10.m:
Those called sakalālayas, however, have all cuirasses submerged;
and the jñānākalas have these cuirasses destroyed: such is the determination. // 100

10.s:
tena pradhāne vedye'pi pumānudbhūtakañcukaḥ /
pramātāstyeva sakalaḥ pāñcadaśyamataḥ sthitam // 101
10.d:
तेन प्रधाने वेद्येऽपि पुमानुद्भूतकञ्चुकः ।
प्रमातास्त्येव सकलः पाञ्चदश्यमतः स्थितम् ॥ 101
10.m:
Therefore, even when the unmanifest is knowable, the soul with arisen cuirasses
exists as a sakala knower; hence the fifteenfold nature is established. // 101

10.s:
pāñcadaśyaṃ dharādhantarniviṣṭe sakale'pi ca /
sakalāntaramastyeva prameye'trāpi mātṛ hi // 102
10.d:
पाञ्चदश्यं धराधन्तर्निविष्टे सकलेऽपि च ।
सकलान्तरमस्त्येव प्रमेयेऽत्रापि मातृ हि ॥ 102
10.m:
There is a fifteenfold nature even in a sakala situated within the earth-path,
for another sakala exists as knower even regarding this knowable object. // 102

10.s:
sthūlāvṛtādisaṃkocatadanyavyāptṛtājuṣaḥ /
pītādyāḥ sthirakampratvāccaturdaśa dharādiṣu // 103
10.d:
स्थूलावृतादिसंकोचतदन्यव्याप्तृताजुषः ।
पीताद्याः स्थिरकम्प्रत्वाच्चतुर्दश धरादिषु ॥ 103
10.m:
Endowed with the contraction of being gross, covered, and the like, and with the pervasion of other [degrees],
yellow and so forth, because of stability and trembling, are fourteenfold in earth and the rest; // 103

10.s:
svarūpībhūtajaḍatāḥ prāṇadehapathe tataḥ /
pramātṛtājuṣaḥ proktā dhāraṇā vijayottare // 104
10.d:
स्वरूपीभूतजडताः प्राणदेहपथे ततः ।
प्रमातृताजुषः प्रोक्ता धारणा विजयोत्तरे ॥ 104
10.m:
having insentience as their own nature, in the path of breath and body,
they are taught in the Vijayottara as dharāṇās possessing knower-hood. // 104

10.s:
yadā tu meyatā puṃsaḥ kalāntasya prakalpyate /
tadudbhūtaḥ kañcukāṃśo meyo nāsya pramātṛtā // 105
10.d:
यदा तु मेयता पुंसः कलान्तस्य प्रकल्प्यते ।
तदुद्भूतः कञ्चुकांशो मेयो नास्य प्रमातृता ॥ 105
10.m:
When, however, the knowability of a soul ending with kalā is posited,
the arisen portion of the cuirass is knowable; he has no knower-hood. // 105

10.s:
ataḥ sakalasaṃjñasya pramātṛtvaṃ na vidyate /
trayodaśatvaṃ tacchaktiśaktimaddvayavarjanāt // 106
10.d:
अतः सकलसंज्ञस्य प्रमातृत्वं न विद्यते ।
त्रयोदशत्वं तच्छक्तिशक्तिमद्द्वयवर्जनात् ॥ 106
10.m:
Hence, there is no knower-hood for the one called sakala;
there is a thirteenfold nature, owing to the exclusion of the pair of power and power-holder. // 106

10.s:
nyagbhūtakañcuko mātā yukta[yata]statra layākalaḥ /
māyāniviṣṭo vijñānākalādyāḥ prāgvadeva tu // 107
10.d:
न्यग्भूतकञ्चुको माता युक्त[यत]स्तत्र लयाकलः ।
मायानिविष्टो विज्ञानाकलाद्याः प्राग्वदेव तु ॥ 107
10.m:
The knower whose cuirass is submerged is the layākala who is properly situated there;
resting in māyā, the vijñānākalas and the rest are just as before. // 107

10.s:
māyātattve jñeyarūpe kañcukanyagbhavo'pi yaḥ /
so'pi meyaḥ kañcukaikyaṃ yato māyā susūkṣmikā // 108
10.d:
मायातत्त्वे ज्ञेयरूपे कञ्चुकन्यग्भवोऽपि यः ।
सोऽपि मेयः कञ्चुकैक्यं यतो माया सुसूक्ष्मिका ॥ 108
10.m:
When the māyā-principle is in the form of the knowable, even the submersion of the cuirass
is also knowable, because the identity of the cuirasses is the exceedingly subtle māyā. // 108

10.s:
vijñānākala evātra tato mātāpakañcukaḥ /
māyāniviṣṭe'pyakale tathetyekādaśātmatā // 109
10.d:
विज्ञानाकल एवात्र ततो मातापकञ्चुकः ।
मायानिविष्टेऽप्यकले तथेत्येकादशात्मता ॥ 109
10.m:
Therefore, only the vijñānākala, whose cuirass has departed, is the knower here;
and when the akala situated in māyā is likewise [a knower], there is an elevenfold nature. // 109

10.s:
vijñānakevale vedye kañcukadhvaṃsasusthite /
udbubhūṣuprabodhānāṃ mantrāṇāmeva mātṛtā // 110
10.d:
विज्ञानकेवले वेद्ये कञ्चुकध्वंससुस्थिते ।
उद्बुभूषुप्रबोधानां मन्त्राणामेव मातृता ॥ 110
10.m:
When the vijñānakevala is the knowable, firmly abiding in the destruction of the cuirasses,
knower-hood belongs only to the mantras whose awakening desires to arise. // 110

10.s:
te'pi mantrā yadā meyāstadā mātā tadīśvaraḥ /
sa hyudbhavātpūrṇabodhastasminprāpte tu meyatām // 111
10.d:
तेऽपि मन्त्रा यदा मेयास्तदा माता तदीश्वरः ।
स ह्युद्भवात्पूर्णबोधस्तस्मिन्प्राप्ते तु मेयताम् ॥ 111
10.m:
When those mantras too are knowables, then their lord is the knower,
for he has full awakening from emergence; but when he has attained knowability, // 111

10.s:
udbhūtapūrṇarūpo'sau mātā mantramaheśvaraḥ /
tasminvijñeyatāṃ prāpte svaprakāśaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ // 112
10.d:
उद्भूतपूर्णरूपोऽसौ माता मन्त्रमहेश्वरः ।
तस्मिन्विज्ञेयतां प्राप्ते स्वप्रकाशः परः शिवः ॥ 112
10.m:
the Mantramaheśvara, whose full form has arisen, is the knower.
When he has attained the state of being known, the self-luminous supreme Śiva // 112

10.s:
pramātā svakatādātmyabhāsitākhilavedyakaḥ /
śivaḥ pramātā no meyo hyanyādhīnaprakāśatā // 113
10.d:
प्रमाता स्वकतादात्म्यभासिताखिलवेद्यकः ।
शिवः प्रमाता नो मेयो ह्यन्याधीनप्रकाशता ॥ 113
10.m:
is the knower, illuminating all knowables through identity with himself.
Śiva is the knower and not the knowable, for knowability is dependent on another. // 113

10.s:
meyatā sā na tatrāsti svaprakāśo hyasau prabhuḥ /
svaprakāśe'tra kasmiṃścidanabhyupagate sati // 114
10.d:
मेयता सा न तत्रास्ति स्वप्रकाशो ह्यसौ प्रभुः ।
स्वप्रकाशेऽत्र कस्मिंश्चिदनभ्युपगते सति ॥ 114
