10.m: That state of being an object of cognition does not exist there, for that Lord is self-luminous. / If someone self-luminous were not accepted here,

10.s:
aprakāśātprakāśatve hyanavasthā duruttarā /
tataśca suptaṃ viśvaṃ syānna caivaṃ bhāsate hi tat // 115
10.d:
अप्रकाशात्प्रकाशत्वे ह्यनवस्था दुरुत्तरा ।
ततश्च सुप्तं विश्वं स्यान्न चैवं भासते हि तत् ॥ 115
10.m: there would indeed be an insurmountable infinite regress in explaining luminosity through what is unilluminated, / and consequently the universe would be asleep; yet it is not so, for it shines forth.

10.s:
anyādhīnaprakāśaṃ hi tadbhātyanyastvasau śivaḥ /
ityasya svaprakāśatve kimanyairyuktiḍambaraiḥ // 116
10.d:
अन्याधीनप्रकाशं हि तद्भात्यन्यस्त्वसौ शिवः ।
इत्यस्य स्वप्रकाशत्वे किमन्यैर्युक्तिडम्बरैः ॥ 116
10.m: For it shines forth having its luminosity dependent upon another, while this other is Śiva. / Thus, regarding his self-luminosity, what need is there for other ostentatious arguments?

10.s:
mānānāṃ hi paro jīvaḥ sa evetyuktamāditaḥ /
nanvasti svaprakāśe'pi śive vedyatvamīdṛśaḥ // 117
10.d:
मानानां हि परो जीवः स एवेत्युक्तमादितः ।
नन्वस्ति स्वप्रकाशेऽपि शिवे वेद्यत्वमीदृशः ॥ 117
10.m: For it has been stated from the beginning that he alone is the supreme life of means of knowledge. / [Objection:] Now, even though Śiva is self-luminous, can there not be cognisability in him? Otherwise,

10.s:
upadeśo[śyo]padeṣṭṛtvavyavahāro'nyathā katham /
satyaṃ sa tu tathā sṛṣṭaḥ parameśena vedyatām // 118
10.d:
उपदेशो[श्यो]पदेष्टृत्वव्यवहारोऽन्यथा कथम् ।
सत्यं स तु तथा सृष्टः परमेशेन वेद्यताम् ॥ 118
10.m: how could the ordinary practice of instruction between teacher and pupil take place? / [Answer:] True, but when he is created thus by the Supreme Lord and brought to cognisability,

10.s:
nīto mantramaheśādikakṣyāṃ samadhiśāyyate /
tathābhūtaśca vedyo'sau nānavacchinnasaṃvidaḥ // 119
10.d:
नीतो मन्त्रमहेशादिकक्ष्यां समधिशाय्यते ।
तथाभूतश्च वेद्योऽसौ नानवच्छिन्नसंविदः ॥ 119
10.m: he is made to rest at the level of Mantramaheśvara and the like. / And an entity that has become an object of cognition in such a manner cannot belong to uncircumscribed consciousness.

10.s:
pūrṇasya vedyatā yuktā parasparavirodhataḥ /
tathā vedyasvabhāve'pi vastuto na śivātmatām // 120
10.d:
पूर्णस्य वेद्यता युक्ता परस्परविरोधतः ।
तथा वेद्यस्वभावेऽपि वस्तुतो न शिवात्मताम् ॥ 120
10.m: Cognisability of that which is full is inappropriate, because of mutual contradiction. / In that way, even if its nature is an object of cognition, in reality it does not abandon the nature of Śiva.

10.s:
ko'pi bhāvaḥ projjhatīti satyaṃ tadbhāvanā phalet /
śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ śivaḥ sākṣānna bhidyate // 121
10.d:
कोऽपि भावः प्रोज्झतीति सत्यं तद्भावना फलेत् ।
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तेनोक्तं शिवः साक्षान्न भिद्यते ॥ 121
10.m: No entity whatsoever abandons [that nature]; thus contemplation on that indeed bears fruit. / Therefore it was said in the venerated Pūrvaśāstra: 'Śiva is directly not differentiated.'

10.s:
sākṣātpadenāyamarthaḥ samastaḥ prasphuṭīkṛtaḥ /
nanvekarūpatāyuktaḥ śivastadvaśato bhavet // 122
10.d:
साक्षात्पदेनायमर्थः समस्तः प्रस्फुटीकृतः ।
नन्वेकरूपतायुक्तः शिवस्तद्वशतो भवेत् ॥ 122
10.m: By the word 'directly', this entire meaning has been made evident. / [Objection:] Surely, if Śiva is endowed with uniformity, then on that account,

10.s:
trivedatāmantramahānāthe kātra vivāditā /
maheśvareśamantrāṇāṃ tathā kevalinordvayoḥ // 123
10.d:
त्रिवेदतामन्त्रमहानाथे कात्र विवादिता ।
महेश्वरेशमन्त्राणां तथा केवलिनोर्द्वयोः ॥ 123
10.m: how can there be dispute regarding the threefold nature of Mantramahānātha? / Likewise, for the Maheśvaras, Īśas, Mantras, and the two classes of solitary souls,

10.s:
anantabhedataikaikaṃ sthitā sakalavatkila /
tato layākale meye pramātāsti layākalaḥ // 124
10.d:
अनन्तभेदतैकैकं स्थिता सकलवत्किल ।
ततो लयाकले मेये प्रमातास्ति लयाकलः ॥ 124
10.m: each remains distinct through endless divisions, just like the Sakala. / Therefore, when the layākala is an object of cognition, there is a layākala subject;

10.s:
atastrayodaśatvaṃ syāditthaṃ naikādaśātmatā /
vijñānākalavedyatve'pyanyo jñānākalo bhavet // 125
10.d:
अतस्त्रयोदशत्वं स्यादित्थं नैकादशात्मता ।
विज्ञानाकलवेद्यत्वेऽप्यन्यो ज्ञानाकलो भवेत् ॥ 125
10.m: hence there would be thirteen [classes], and in this way not an elevenfold nature. / When the vijñānākala is an object of cognition, there would also be another vijñānākala

10.s:
mātā tadekādaśatā syānnaiva tu navātmatā /
evaṃ mantratadīśānāṃ mantreśāntarasaṃbhave // 126
10.d:
माता तदेकादशता स्यान्नैव तु नवात्मता ।
एवं मन्त्रतदीशानां मन्त्रेशान्तरसंभवे ॥ 126
10.m: as subject, and thus it would be elevenfold, and not ninefold at all. / Similarly, in the case of the Mantras and their lords, if another Mantreśa were to exist

10.s:
vedyatvānnava sapta syuḥ sapta pañca tu te katham /
ucyate satyamastyeṣā kalanā kiṃtu susphuṭaḥ // 127
10.d:
वेद्यत्वान्नव सप्त स्युः सप्त पञ्च तु ते कथम् ।
उच्यते सत्यमस्त्येषा कलना किंतु सुस्फुटः ॥ 127
10.m: due to cognisability, nine would become seven, and seven would become five—how so? / It is said in reply: True, this enumeration exists, but just as differentiation

10.s:
yathātra sakale bhedo na tathā tvakalādike /
anantāvāntaredṛkṣayonibhedavataḥ sphuṭam // 128
10.d:
यथात्र सकले भेदो न तथा त्वकलादिके ।
अनन्तावान्तरेदृक्षयोनिभेदवतः स्फुटम् ॥ 128
10.m: is clearly evident here in the Sakala, it is not so in the Akala and the rest, / which possess clearly endless subdivisions belonging to such wombs [of rebirth].

10.s:
caturdaśavidhasyāsya sakalasyāsti bheditā /
layākale tu saṃskāramātrātsatyapyasau bhidā // 129
10.d:
चतुर्दशविधस्यास्य सकलस्यास्ति भेदिता ।
लयाकले तु संस्कारमात्रात्सत्यप्यसौ भिदा ॥ 129
10.m: This fourteenfold Sakala has distinct varieties. / In the layākala, however, although such distinction exists due merely to residual traces,

10.s:
akalena viśeṣāya sakalasyaiva yujyate /
vijñānakevalādīnāṃ tāvatyapi na vai bhidā // 130
10.d:
अकलेन विशेषाय सकलस्यैव युज्यते ।
विज्ञानकेवलादीनां तावत्यपि न वै भिदा ॥ 130
10.m: it serves as a distinctive mark only for the Sakala through the Akala. / Among the vijñānakevalas and the rest, not even so much distinction exists;

10.s:
śivasvācchandyamātraṃ tu bhedāyaiṣāṃ vijṛmbhate /
ityāśayena saṃpaśyanviśeṣaṃ sakalādiha // 131
10.d:
शिवस्वाच्छन्द्यमात्रं तु भेदायैषां विजृम्भते ।
इत्याशयेन संपश्यन्विशेषं सकलादिह ॥ 131
10.m: only Śiva's sovereign freedom unfolds to produce their distinction. / Seeing the distinction in this world beginning with the Sakala with this intention in mind,

10.s:
layākalādau novāca trāyodaśyādikaṃ vibhuḥ /
nanvastu vedyatā bhāvadharmaḥ kiṃtu layākalau // 132
10.d:
लयाकलादौ नोवाच त्रायोदश्यादिकं विभुः ।
नन्वस्तु वेद्यता भावधर्मः किंतु लयाकलौ ॥ 132
10.m: the all-pervading Lord did not teach a thirteenfold division or the like beginning with the layākala. / [Objection:] Granted that cognisability is a property of entities; but the two layākalas

10.s:
manvāte neha vai kiṃcittadapekṣā tvasau katham /
śrūyatāṃ saṃvidaikātmyatattve'sminsaṃvyavasthite // 133
10.d:
मन्वाते नेह वै किंचित्तदपेक्षा त्वसौ कथम् ।
श्रूयतां संविदैकात्म्यतत्त्वेऽस्मिन्संव्यवस्थिते ॥ 133
10.m: do not think of anything here at all, so how can there be a relation of dependency for them? / Hear this: when the truth of the oneness of consciousness is firmly established,

10.s:
jaḍe'pi citirastyeva bhotsyamāne tu kā kathā /
svabodhāvasare tāvadbhotsyate layakevalī // 134
10.d:
जडेऽपि चितिरस्त्येव भोत्स्यमाने तु का कथा ।
स्वबोधावसरे तावद्भोत्स्यते लयकेवली ॥ 134
10.m: consciousness exists even in the insentient, so what need be said of one who will awaken? / At the time of his own awakening, the layakevalin will indeed awaken.

10.s:
dvividhaśca prabodho'sya mantratvāya bhavāya ca /
bhāvanādibalādanyavaiṣṇavādinayoditāt // 135
10.d:
द्विविधश्च प्रबोधोऽस्य मन्त्रत्वाय भवाय च ।
भावनादिबलादन्यवैष्णवादिनयोदितात् ॥ 135
10.m: And his awakening is twofold: toward becoming a Mantra and toward mundane existence. / By the power of contemplation and the like taught in other traditions such as the Vaiṣṇava,

10.s:
yathāsvamādharauttaryavicitrātsaṃskṛtastathā /
līnaḥ prabuddho mantratvaṃ tadīśatvamathaiti vā // 136
10.d:
यथास्वमाधरौत्तर्यविचित्रात्संस्कृतस्तथा ।
लीनः प्रबुद्धो मन्त्रत्वं तदीशत्वमथैति वा ॥ 136
10.m: he is appropriately refined through diverse lower and higher [states]. / Having been dissolved, once awakened, he attains the state of a Mantra or its lord.

10.s:
svātantryavarjitā ye tu balānmohavaśīkṛtāḥ /
layākalātsvasaṃskārātprabuddhyante bhavāya te // 137
10.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यवर्जिता ये तु बलान्मोहवशीकृताः ।
लयाकलात्स्वसंस्कारात्प्रबुद्ध्यन्ते भवाय ते ॥ 137
10.m: Those, however, who are devoid of freedom and forcibly dominated by delusion, / awaken from the layākala toward mundane existence due to their own residual traces.

10.s:
jñānākalo'pi mantreśamaheśatvāya budhyate /
mantrāditvāya vā jātu jātu saṃsṛtaye'pi vā // 138
10.d:
ज्ञानाकलोऽपि मन्त्रेशमहेशत्वाय बुध्यते ।
मन्त्रादित्वाय वा जातु जातु संसृतयेऽपि वा ॥ 138
10.m: The jñānākala also awakens to the state of Mantreśa and Maheśa, / or sometimes to the state of Mantra and the rest, or even to transmigration.

10.s:
avatāro hi vijñāniyogibhāve'sya bhidyate /
uktaṃ ca bodhayāmāsa sa sisṛkṣurjagatprabhuḥ // 139
10.d:
अवतारो हि विज्ञानियोगिभावेऽस्य भिद्यते ।
उक्तं च बोधयामास स सिसृक्षुर्जगत्प्रभुः ॥ 139
10.m: For his descent into the state of a knowing yogin differs. / And it is stated in the venerated Pūrvaśāsana: 'The Lord of the universe, desiring to emanate,

10.s:
vijñānakevalānaṣṭāviti śrīpūrvaśāsane /
ataḥ prabhotsyamānatve yānayorbodhayogyatā // 140
10.d:
विज्ञानकेवलानष्टाविति श्रीपूर्वशासने ।
अतः प्रभोत्स्यमानत्वे यानयोर्बोधयोग्यता ॥ 140
10.m: awakened the eight vijñānakevalas.' / Therefore, since they are about to awaken, the suitability for awakening belonging to these two

10.s:
tadbalādvedyatāyogyabhāvenaivātra vedyatā /
tathāhi gāḍhanidre'pi priye'nāśaṅkitāgatām // 141
10.d:
तद्बलाद्वेद्यतायोग्यभावेनैवात्र वेद्यता ।
तथाहि गाढनिद्रेऽपि प्रियेऽनाशङ्कितागताम् ॥ 141
10.m: is, by virtue of that, cognisability here precisely through being an entity suitable for cognisability. / To explain: even when her beloved is in deep sleep, a woman going to meet him

10.s:
māṃ drakṣyatīti nāṅgeṣu sveṣu mātyabhisārikā /
evaṃ śivo'pi manute etasyaitatpravedyatām // 142
10.d:
मां द्रक्ष्यतीति नाङ्गेषु स्वेषु मात्यभिसारिका ।
एवं शिवोऽपि मनुते एतस्यैतत्प्रवेद्यताम् ॥ 142
10.m: overflows with joy in her own limbs, thinking, 'He will see me who have arrived unexpectedly.' / In this way, Śiva too considers, 'He will cognise this;

10.s:
yāsyatīti sṛjāmīti tadānīṃ yogyataiva sā /
vedyatā tasya bhāvasya bhoktṛtā tāvatī ca sā // 143
10.d:
यास्यतीति सृजामीति तदानीं योग्यतैव सा ।
वेद्यता तस्य भावस्य भोक्तृता तावती च सा ॥ 143
10.m: I emanate it'—at that time, that very suitability / is the cognisability of that entity, and it is to that extent its enjoyership.

10.s:
layākalasya citro hi bhogaḥ kena vikalpyate /
yathā yathā hi samvittiḥ sa hi bhogaḥ sphuṭo'sphuṭaḥ // 144
10.d:
लयाकलस्य चित्रो हि भोगः केन विकल्प्यते ।
यथा यथा हि सम्वित्तिः स हि भोगः स्फुटोऽस्फुटः ॥ 144
10.m: For by whom could the diverse experience of the layākala be mentally conceived? / According as consciousness is, so is that experience, clear or unclear.

10.s:
smṛtiyogyo'pyanyathā vā bhogyabhāvaṃ na tūjjhati /
gāḍhanidrāvimūḍho'pi kāntāliṅgitavigrahaḥ // 145
10.d:
स्मृतियोग्योऽप्यन्यथा वा भोग्यभावं न तूज्झति ।
गाढनिद्राविमूढोऽपि कान्तालिङ्गितविग्रहः ॥ 145
10.m: Even if suitable for memory or otherwise, it does not abandon the state of being an object of experience. / Even when bewildered in deep sleep, one whose body is embraced by his beloved

10.s:
bhoktaiva bhaṇyate so'pi manute bhoktṛtāṃ purā /
utprekṣāmātrahīno'pi kāṃcitkulavadhūṃ puraḥ // 146
10.d:
भोक्तैव भण्यते सोऽपि मनुते भोक्तृतां पुरा ।
उत्प्रेक्षामात्रहीनोऽपि कांचित्कुलवधूं पुरः ॥ 146
10.m: is said to be an enjoyer indeed; he too earlier thinks of his own state of being an enjoyer. / Even without any mental projection beforehand, seeing a noble wife in front of him

10.s:
saṃbhokṣyamāṇāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rabhasādyāti saṃmadam /
tāmeva dṛṣṭvā ca tadā samānāśayabhāgapi // 147
10.d:
संभोक्ष्यमाणां दृष्ट्वैव रभसाद्याति संमदम् ।
तामेव दृष्ट्वा च तदा समानाशयभागपि ॥ 147
10.m: about to be enjoyed, he experiences exhilaration out of impetuous passion; / whereas upon seeing that very same woman, another person, even if possessing a similar disposition,

10.s:
anyastathā na saṃvitte kamatropalabhāmahe /
loke rūḍhamidaṃ dṛṣṭirasminkāraṇamantarā // 148
10.d:
अन्यस्तथा न संवित्ते कमत्रोपलभामहे ।
लोके रूढमिदं दृष्टिरस्मिन्कारणमन्तरा ॥ 148
10.m: does not experience it in that way: whom can we perceive as a cause here? / This is well established in the world when one says, 'Without any external cause, the gaze in this matter

10.s:
prasīdatīva magneva nirvātīvetivādini /
itthaṃ vistaratastattvabhedo'yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ // 149
10.d:
प्रसीदतीव मग्नेव निर्वातीवेतिवादिनि ।
इत्थं विस्तरतस्तत्त्वभेदोऽयं समुदाहृतः ॥ 149
10.m: becomes serene, as if immersed, as if tranquil.' / In this manner, this division of principles has been explained in detail.

10.s:
śaktiśaktimatāṃ bhedādanyonyaṃ tatkṛteṣvapi /
bhedeṣvanyonyato bhedāttathā tattvāntaraiḥ saha // 150
10.d:
शक्तिशक्तिमतां भेदादन्योन्यं तत्कृतेष्वपि ।
भेदेष्वन्योन्यतो भेदात्तथा तत्त्वान्तरैः सह ॥ 150
10.m: Due to the mutual differentiation between powers and power-holders, even within the distinctions created by them, / due to mutual differentiation, and likewise with other principles,

10.s:
bhedopabhedagaṇanāṃ karvato nāvadhiḥ kvacit /
tata eva vicitro'yaṃ bhuvanādividhiḥ sthitaḥ // 151
10.d:
भेदोपभेदगणनां कर्वतो नावधिः क्वचित् ।
तत एव विचित्रोऽयं भुवनादिविधिः स्थितः ॥ 151
10.m: there is no limit anywhere for one calculating the divisions and subdivisions. / For that very reason, this manifold arrangement of worlds and so forth is established.

10.s:
pārthivatve'pi no sāmyaṃ rudravaiṣṇavalokayoḥ /
kā kathānyatra tu bhavedbhoge vāpi svarūpake // 152
10.d:
पार्थिवत्वेऽपि नो साम्यं रुद्रवैष्णवलोकयोः ।
का कथान्यत्र तु भवेद्भोगे वापि स्वरूपके ॥ 152
10.m: Even though both are earthly, there is no equality between the realms of Rudra and Viṣṇu; / what need be said elsewhere, whether in enjoyment or in essential nature?

10.s:
sa ca no vistaraḥ sākṣācchakyo yadyapi bhāṣitum /
tathāpi mārgamātreṇa kathyamāno vivicyatām // 153
10.d:
स च नो विस्तरः साक्षाच्छक्यो यद्यपि भाषितुम् ।
तथापि मार्गमात्रेण कथ्यमानो विविच्यताम् ॥ 153
10.m: And although that full extent cannot directly be spoken of, / nevertheless, let it be examined as it is being described merely by way of outline.

10.s:
saptānāṃ mātṛśaktīnāmanyonyaṃ bhedane sati /
rūpamekānnapañcāśatsvarūpaṃ cādhikaṃ tataḥ // 154
10.d:
सप्तानां मातृशक्तीनामन्योन्यं भेदने सति ।
रूपमेकान्नपञ्चाशत्स्वरूपं चाधिकं ततः ॥ 154
10.m: When the seven mother powers are mutually distinguished, / their form is forty-nine, and beyond that their own essential natures are even more.

10.s:
sarvaṃ sarvātmakaṃ yasmāttasmātsakalamātari /
layākalādiśaktīnāṃ saṃbhavo'styeva tattvataḥ // 155
10.d:
सर्वं सर्वात्मकं यस्मात्तस्मात्सकलमातरि ।
लयाकलादिशक्तीनां संभवोऽस्त्येव तत्त्वतः ॥ 155
10.m: Because everything consists of everything, therefore in the Sakala subject, / the powers of the layākala and the others certainly exist in reality.

10.s:
sa tvasphuṭo'stu bhedāṃśaṃ dātuṃ tāvatprabhurbhavet /
teṣāmapi ca bhedānāmanyonyaṃ bahubhedatā // 156
10.d:
स त्वस्फुटोऽस्तु भेदांशं दातुं तावत्प्रभुर्भवेत् ।
तेषामपि च भेदानामन्योन्यं बहुभेदता ॥ 156
10.m: Though it may be unmanifest, it would indeed have the power to impart a share of distinction. / And among those divisions also, there is mutual manifold distinction.

10.s:
mukhyānāṃ bhedabhedānāṃ jalādyairbhedane sati /
mukhyabhedaprakāreṇa vidherānantyamucyate // 157
10.d:
मुख्यानां भेदभेदानां जलाद्यैर्भेदने सति ।
मुख्यभेदप्रकारेण विधेरानन्त्यमुच्यते ॥ 157
10.m: When the primary divisions and subdivisions are diversified by water and the other elements, / infinity of the arrangement is declared in terms of the primary distinctions.

10.s:
sakalasya samudbhūtāścakṣurādisvaśaktayaḥ /
nyagbhūtāśca pratanvanti bhedāntaramapi sphuṭam // 158
10.d:
सकलस्य समुद्भूताश्चक्षुरादिस्वशक्तयः ।
न्यग्भूताश्च प्रतन्वन्ति भेदान्तरमपि स्फुटम् ॥ 158
10.m: In the Sakala, the innate faculties of sight and the other senses, whether fully emerged / or submerged, clearly unfold yet another division.

10.s:
evaṃ layākalādīnāṃ tatsaṃskārapadoditāt /
pāṭavātprakṣayādvāpi bhedāntaramudīyate // 159
10.d:
एवं लयाकलादीनां तत्संस्कारपदोदितात् ।
पाटवात्प्रक्षयाद्वापि भेदान्तरमुदीयते ॥ 159
10.m: In the same way, for the layākala and the rest, another distinction is stated / arising from the efficacy or the exhaustion originating from their state of residual traces.

10.s:
nyakkṛtāṃ śaktimāsthāyāpyudāsīnatayā sthitim /
anāviśyeva yadvetti tatrānyā vedyatā khalu // 160
10.d:
न्यक्कृतां शक्तिमास्थायाप्युदासीनतया स्थितिम् ।
अनाविश्येव यद्वेत्ति तत्रान्या वेद्यता खलु ॥ 160
10.m: When, though having suppressed [its sensory] power, it knows by resting in indifference without as it were entering into [the object], then the state of being an object of cognition is indeed of another kind.

10.s:
āviśyeva nimajjyeva vikāsyeva vighūrṇya ca /
vidato vedyatānyaiva bhedo'trārthakriyocitaḥ // 161
10.d:
आविश्येव निमज्ज्येव विकास्येव विघूर्ण्य च ।
विदतो वेद्यतान्यैव भेदोऽत्रार्थक्रियोचितः ॥ 161
10.m: When one knows by as it were entering, as it were plunging in, as it were expanding, and reeling, the state of being an object of cognition is quite different; here, the distinction is fit for purposeful action.

10.s:
anyaśaktitirobhāve kasyāścitsusphuṭodaye /
bhedāntaramapi jñeyaṃ vīṇāvādakadṛṣṭivat // 162
10.d:
अन्यशक्तितिरोभावे कस्याश्चित्सुस्फुटोदये ।
भेदान्तरमपि ज्ञेयं वीणावादकदृष्टिवत् ॥ 162
10.m: When another power is submerged and a particular one arises very clearly, another distinction should be recognized, as in the case of a vīṇā player.

10.s:
tirobhāvodbhavau śakteḥ svaśaktyantarato'nyataḥ /
cetyamānādacetyādvā tanvāte bahubhedatām // 163
10.d:
तिरोभावोद्भवौ शक्तेः स्वशक्त्यन्तरतोऽन्यतः ।
चेत्यमानादचेत्याद्वा तन्वाते बहुभेदताम् ॥ 163
10.m: The disappearance and emergence of a power, whether from another power of its own or from something else, whether from what is being cognized or what is not being cognized, bring about manifold diversity.

10.s:
evametaddharādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ yāvatī daśā /
kācidasti ghaṭākhyāpi tatra saṃdarśitā bhidaḥ // 164
10.d:
एवमेतद्धरादीनां तत्त्वानां यावती दशा ।
काचिदस्ति घटाख्यापि तत्र संदर्शिता भिदः ॥ 164
10.m: In this way, whatever state pertains to the principles beginning with earth, even that called a 'pot', the distinctions within it have been demonstrated.

10.s:
atrāpi vedyatā nāma tādātmyaṃ vedakaiḥ saha /
tataḥ sakalavedyo'sau ghaṭaḥ sakala eva hi // 165
10.d:
अत्रापि वेद्यता नाम तादात्म्यं वेदकैः सह ।
ततः सकलवेद्योऽसौ घटः सकल एव हि ॥ 165
10.m: Here too, the state of being an object of cognition is identity with the cognizers; therefore, that pot, which is knowable by a sakala, is indeed a sakala itself.

10.s:
yāvacchivaikavedyo'sau śiva evāvabhāsate /
tāvadekaśarīro hi bodho bhātyeva yāvatā // 166
10.d:
यावच्छिवैकवेद्योऽसौ शिव एवावभासते ।
तावदेकशरीरो हि बोधो भात्येव यावता ॥ 166
10.m: Until it shines forth as Śiva himself, knowable solely by Śiva, consciousness shines only as having a single body to that extent.

10.s:
adhunātra samastasya dharātattvasya darśyate /
sāmastya evābhihitaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ puroditam // 167
10.d:
अधुनात्र समस्तस्य धरातत्त्वस्य दर्श्यते ।
सामस्त्य एवाभिहितं पाञ्चदश्यं पुरोदितम् ॥ 167
10.m: Now, in regard to the earth-principle in its entirety, the fifteenfold nature previously declared is demonstrated as a whole.

10.s:
dharātattvāvibhedena yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
sa eva śivanātho'tra pṛthivī brahma tanmatam // 168
10.d:
धरातत्त्वाविभेदेन यः प्रकाशः प्रकाशते ।
स एव शिवनाथोऽत्र पृथिवी ब्रह्म तन्मतम् ॥ 168
10.m: That light which shines undifferentiated from the earth-principle is here the Lord Śiva himself; the earth is considered to be Brahman.

10.s:
dharātattvagatāḥ siddhīrvitarītuṃ samudyatān /
prerayanti śivecchāto ye te mantramaheśvarāḥ // 169
10.d:
धरातत्त्वगताः सिद्धीर्वितरीतुं समुद्यतान् ।
प्रेरयन्ति शिवेच्छातो ये ते मन्त्रमहेश्वराः ॥ 169
10.m: Those who, by Śiva's will, impel those intent upon bestowing the supernatural powers belonging to the earth-principle, are the Mantramaheśvaras.

10.s:
preryamāṇāstu mantreśā mantrāstadvācakāḥ sphuṭam /
dharātattvagataṃ yogamabhyasya śivavidyayā // 170
10.d:
प्रेर्यमाणास्तु मन्त्रेशा मन्त्रास्तद्वाचकाः स्फुटम् ।
धरातत्त्वगतं योगमभ्यस्य शिवविद्यया ॥ 170
10.m: The Mantreśas, however, are those being impelled; the Mantras clearly express them, having practiced the yoga belonging to the earth-principle by means of Śiva's wisdom;

10.s:
na tu pāśavasāṃkhyīyavaiṣṇavādidvitādṛśā /
aprāptadhruvadhāmāno vijñānākalatājuṣaḥ // 171
10.d:
न तु पाशवसांख्यीयवैष्णवादिद्वितादृशा ।
अप्राप्तध्रुवधामानो विज्ञानाकलताजुषः ॥ 171
10.m: not, however, those bound souls of the Sāṃkhyas, Vaiṣṇavas, and others, who, not having attained the immutable abode, participate in the state of vijñānākalas.

10.s:
tāvattattvopabhogena ye kalpānte layaṃ gatāḥ /
sauṣuptāvasthayopetāste'tra pralayakevalāḥ // 172
10.d:
तावत्तत्त्वोपभोगेन ये कल्पान्ते लयं गताः ।
सौषुप्तावस्थयोपेतास्तेऽत्र प्रलयकेवलाः ॥ 172
10.m: Those who, through experiencing that principle up to that point, have dissolved at the end of a cosmic age and are endowed with the state of deep sleep, are here the pralayakevalas.

10.s:
sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭameva hi lakṣyate /
anyathā niyatasvapnasaṃdṛṣṭirjāyate kutaḥ // 173
10.d:
सौषुप्ते तत्त्वलीनत्वं स्फुटमेव हि लक्ष्यते ।
अन्यथा नियतस्वप्नसंदृष्टिर्जायते कुतः ॥ 173
10.m: Indeed, dissolution into the principles is clearly observed in deep sleep; otherwise, how could a determinate dream-vision arise?

10.s:
sauṣuptamapi citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate /
asvāpsaṃ sukhamityādismṛtivaicitryadarśanāt // 174
10.d:
सौषुप्तमपि चित्रं च स्वच्छास्वच्छादि भासते ।
अस्वाप्सं सुखमित्यादिस्मृतिवैचित्र्यदर्शनात् ॥ 174
10.m: Deep sleep also shines variegated as clear, unclear, and so forth, because one observes a variety of memories such as 'I slept pleasantly.'

10.s:
yadaiva sa kṣaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nidrāyaiva prabuddhyate /
tadaiva smṛtireṣeti nārthajajñānajā smṛtiḥ // 175
10.d:
यदैव स क्षणं सूक्ष्मं निद्रायैव प्रबुद्ध्यते ।
तदैव स्मृतिरेषेति नार्थजज्ञानजा स्मृतिः ॥ 175
10.m: Precisely when one awakens after having slept for even a subtle moment, this memory arises at that very time; it is not a memory born of cognition arising from an external object.

10.s:
tena mūḍhairyaducyeta prabuddhasyāntarāntarā /
tūlikādisukhasparśasmṛtireṣeti tatkutaḥ // 176
10.d:
तेन मूढैर्यदुच्येत प्रबुद्धस्यान्तरान्तरा ।
तूलिकादिसुखस्पर्शस्मृतिरेषेति तत्कुतः ॥ 176
10.m: Therefore, when fools claim that this is the awakened person's memory of the pleasant contact with a mattress and the like at various intervals, how could that be so?

10.s:
māhākarmasamullāsasaṃmiśritamalābilāḥ /
dharādhirohiṇo jñeyāḥ sakalā iha pudgalāḥ // 177
10.d:
माहाकर्मसमुल्लाससंमिश्रितमलाबिलाः ।
धराधिरोहिणो ज्ञेयाः सकला इह पुद्गलाः ॥ 177
10.m: Those who are soiled by impurity intermingled with the surging of great karma, ascending the earth-[principle], are to be known here as the sakala embodied souls.

10.s:
asyaiva saptakasya svasvavyāpāraprakalpane /
prakṣobho yastadevoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ sphuṭam // 178
10.d:
अस्यैव सप्तकस्य स्वस्वव्यापारप्रकल्पने ।
प्रक्षोभो यस्तदेवोक्तं शक्तीनां सप्तकं स्फुटम् ॥ 178
10.m: When this very heptad is deployed in its respective operations, the agitation that occurs is clearly declared to be the heptad of powers.

10.s:
śivo hyacyutacidrūpastisrastacchaktayastu yāḥ /
tāḥ svātantryavaśopāttagrahītrākāratāvaśāt // 179
10.d:
शिवो ह्यच्युतचिद्रूपस्तिस्रस्तच्छक्तयस्तु याः ।
ताः स्वातन्त्र्यवशोपात्तग्रहीत्राकारतावशात् ॥ 179
10.m: For Śiva's nature is imperishable consciousness; but his three powers, by virtue of assuming the form of the cognizer through his absolute autonomy,

10.s:
tridhā mantrāvasānāḥ syurudāsīnā iva sthitāḥ /
grāhyākāroparāgāttu grahītrākāratāvaśāt // 180
10.d:
त्रिधा मन्त्रावसानाः स्युरुदासीना इव स्थिताः ।
ग्राह्याकारोपरागात्तु ग्रहीत्राकारतावशात् ॥ 180
10.m: would be threefold down to the Mantras, resting as if indifferent. But from the coloring by the form of the knowable, by virtue of the form of the cognizer,

10.s:
sakalāntāstu tāstisra icchājñānakriyā matāḥ /
saptadhetthaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ tatkṣobho mānatā tathā // 181
10.d:
सकलान्तास्तु तास्तिस्र इच्छाज्ञानक्रिया मताः ।
सप्तधेत्थं प्रमातृत्वं तत्क्षोभो मानता तथा ॥ 181
10.m: those three down to the sakalas are considered to be will, knowledge, and action. Thus cognizership is sevenfold, and its agitation is the means of knowledge;

10.s:
yattu grahītṛtārūpasaṃvitsaṃsparśavarjitam /
śuddhaṃ jaḍaṃ tatsvarūpamitthaṃ viśvaṃ trikātmakam // 182
10.d:
यत्तु ग्रहीतृतारूपसंवित्संस्पर्शवर्जितम् ।
शुद्धं जडं तत्स्वरूपमित्थं विश्वं त्रिकात्मकम् ॥ 182
10.m: whereas that which is devoid of the touch of consciousness in the form of a cognizer is pure, insentient objectivity. In this way the universe consists of the Trika.

10.s:
evaṃ jalādyapi vadedbhedairbhinnaṃ mahāmatiḥ /
anayā tu diśā prāyaḥ sarvabhedeṣu vidyate // 183
10.d:
एवं जलाद्यपि वदेद्भेदैर्भिन्नं महामतिः ।
अनया तु दिशा प्रायः सर्वभेदेषु विद्यते ॥ 183
10.m: In this manner, a person of great intellect should speak of water and the other principles as divided by distinctions. Along this direction, virtually in all distinctions,

10.s:
bhedo mantramaheśānteṣveṣa pañcadaśātmakaḥ /
tathāpi sphuṭatābhāvātsannapyeṣa na carcitaḥ // 184
10.d:
भेदो मन्त्रमहेशान्तेष्वेष पञ्चदशात्मकः ।
तथापि स्फुटताभावात्सन्नप्येष न चर्चितः ॥ 184
10.m: this fifteenfold division exists ending with the Mantramaheśas; nevertheless, because of its lack of obviousness, even though existing, it has not been discussed [at length].

10.s:
etacca sūtritaṃ dhātrā śrīpūrve yadbravīti hi /
savyāpārādhipatvenetyādinā jāgradāditām // 185
10.d:
एतच्च सूत्रितं धात्रा श्रीपूर्वे यद्ब्रवीति हि ।
सव्यापाराधिपत्वेनेत्यादिना जाग्रदादिताम् ॥ 185
10.m: And this has been aphorized by the creator in the venerable Pūrva-śāstra, which indeed teaches the waking state and the others with the words: 'By possessing agency with its operations', etc.

10.s:
abhinne'pi śive'ntaḥsthasūkṣmabodhānusārataḥ /
adhunā prāṇaśaktisthe tattvajāle vivicyate // 186
10.d:
अभिन्नेऽपि शिवेऽन्तःस्थसूक्ष्मबोधानुसारतः ।
अधुना प्राणशक्तिस्थे तत्त्वजाले विविच्यते ॥ 186
10.m: Even though Śiva is undivided, the web of principles resting in the vital power is now distinguished according to the subtle inner awareness,

10.s:
bhedo'yaṃ pāñcadaśyādiryathā śrīśaṃbhurādiśat /
samaste'rthe'tra nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ // 187
10.d:
भेदोऽयं पाञ्चदश्यादिर्यथा श्रीशंभुरादिशत् ।
समस्तेऽर्थेऽत्र निर्ग्राह्ये तुटयः षोडश क्षणाः ॥ 187
10.m: just as the venerable Śambhu taught this fifteenfold and other division: in every object to be grasped here, there are sixteen moments called tuṭis,

10.s:
ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule cāre sāṃśadvyaṅgulakalpitāḥ /
tatrādyaḥ paramādvaito nirvibhāgarasātmakaḥ // 188
10.d:
षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुले चारे सांशद्व्यङ्गुलकल्पिताः ।
तत्राद्यः परमाद्वैतो निर्विभागरसात्मकः ॥ 188
10.m: reckoned as parts of two digits in a movement of thirty-six digits. Among them, the first is supreme non-duality, whose essence is undivided relish;

10.s:
dvitīyo grāhakollāsarūpaḥ prativibhāvyate /
antyastu grāhyatādātmyātsvarūpībhāvamāgataḥ // 189
10.d:
द्वितीयो ग्राहकोल्लासरूपः प्रतिविभाव्यते ।
अन्त्यस्तु ग्राह्यतादात्म्यात्स्वरूपीभावमागतः ॥ 189
10.m: the second is discerned as having the nature of the surging forth of the grasper. But the last, through identity with the object to be grasped, has attained its own form;

10.s:
pravibhāvyo na hi pṛthagupāntyo grāhakaḥ kṣaṇaḥ /
tṛtīyaṃ kṣaṇamārabhya kṣaṇaṣaṭkaṃ tu yatsthitam // 190
10.d:
प्रविभाव्यो न हि पृथगुपान्त्यो ग्राहकः क्षणः ।
तृतीयं क्षणमारभ्य क्षणषट्कं तु यत्स्थितम् ॥ 190
10.m: the penultimate moment is the grasper, not to be discerned separately. The six moments, however, which exist beginning with the third moment,

10.s:
tannirvikalpaṃ prodgacchadvikalpācchādanātmakam /
tadeva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ // 191
10.d:
तन्निर्विकल्पं प्रोद्गच्छद्विकल्पाच्छादनात्मकम् ।
तदेव शिवरूपं हि परशक्त्यात्मकं विदुः ॥ 191
10.m: are non-conceptual, having the nature of veiling the emerging conceptual constructs; they know that to be the nature of Śiva, consisting of the supreme power.

10.s:
dvitīyaṃ madhyamaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ parāparapadātmakam /
vikalparūḍhirapyeṣā kramātprasphuṭatāṃ gatā // 192
10.d:
द्वितीयं मध्यमं षट्कं परापरपदात्मकम् ।
विकल्परूढिरप्येषा क्रमात्प्रस्फुटतां गता ॥ 192
10.m: The second, middle hexad has the nature of the intermediate level; this firm establishment of conceptual constructs also gradually attains clear manifestation.

10.s:
ṣaṭke'tra prathame devyastisraḥ pronmeṣavṛttitām /
nimeṣavṛttitāṃ cāśu spṛśantyaḥ ṣaṭkatāṃ gatāḥ // 193
10.d:
षट्केऽत्र प्रथमे देव्यस्तिस्रः प्रोन्मेषवृत्तिताम् ।
निमेषवृत्तितां चाशु स्पृशन्त्यः षट्कतां गताः ॥ 193
10.m: In this first hexad, the three goddesses become a hexad by swiftly touching the activity of opening and the activity of closing.

10.s:
evaṃ dvitīyaṣaṭke'pi kiṃ tvatra grāhyavartmanā /
uparāgapadaṃ prāpya parāparatayā sthitāḥ // 194
10.d:
एवं द्वितीयषट्केऽपि किं त्वत्र ग्राह्यवर्त्मना ।
उपरागपदं प्राप्य परापरतया स्थिताः ॥ 194
10.m: The same is true in the second hexad; but here, by following the path of the knowable and attaining the status of coloring, they stand as intermediate.

10.s:
ādye'tra ṣaṭke tā devyaḥ svātantryollāsamātrataḥ /
jighṛkṣite'pyupādhau syuḥ pararūpādavicyutāḥ // 195
10.d:
आद्येऽत्र षट्के ता देव्यः स्वातन्त्र्योल्लासमात्रतः ।
जिघृक्षितेऽप्युपाधौ स्युः पररूपादविच्युताः ॥ 195
10.m: In this first hexad, those goddesses, through the mere surging of absolute autonomy, even when an adjunct is sought to be grasped, remain undeviated from the supreme form.

10.s:
asti cātiśayaḥ kaścittāsāmapyuttarottaram /
yo vivekadhanairdhīraiḥ sphuṭīkṛtyāpi darśyate // 196
10.d:
अस्ति चातिशयः कश्चित्तासामप्युत्तरोत्तरम् ।
यो विवेकधनैर्धीरैः स्फुटीकृत्यापि दर्श्यते ॥ 196
10.m: And there is a certain progressive excellence among them as well, which is revealed and demonstrated by the wise whose wealth is discernment.

10.s:
kecittvekāṃ tuṭiṃ grāhye caikāmapi grahītari /
tādātmyena vinikṣipya saptakaṃ saptakaṃ viduḥ // 197
10.d:
केचित्त्वेकां तुटिं ग्राह्ये चैकामपि ग्रहीतरि ।
तादात्म्येन विनिक्षिप्य सप्तकं सप्तकं विदुः ॥ 197
10.m: Some, however, by consigning one tuṭi to the knowable and one to the knower through identity, recognize a heptad and a heptad.

10.s:
tadasyāṃ sūkṣmasaṃvittau kalanāya samudyatāḥ /
saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vāgvikatthanaiḥ // 198
10.d:
तदस्यां सूक्ष्मसंवित्तौ कलनाय समुद्यताः ।
संवेदयन्ते यद्रूपं तत्र किं वाग्विकत्थनैः ॥ 198
10.m: Therefore, what is the use of verbal boasting concerning the form which those who are intent on measuring experience in this subtle consciousness?

10.s:
evaṃ dharādimūlāntaṃ prakriyā prāṇagāminī /
guruparvakramātproktā bhede pañcadaśātmake // 199
10.d:
एवं धरादिमूलान्तं प्रक्रिया प्राणगामिनी ।
गुरुपर्वक्रमात्प्रोक्ता भेदे पञ्चदशात्मके ॥ 199
10.m: In this manner, the process extending to vital breath from the earth up to the root principle has been taught according to the lineage of gurus in its fifteenfold distinction.

10.s:
kramāttu bhedanyūnatve nyūnatā syāttuṭiṣvapi /
tasyāṃ hrāso vikalpasya sphuṭatā cāvikalpinaḥ // 200
10.d:
क्रमात्तु भेदन्यूनत्वे न्यूनता स्यात्तुटिष्वपि ।
तस्यां ह्रासो विकल्पस्य स्फुटता चाविकल्पिनः ॥ 200
10.m: When the distinction decreases gradually, there is a decrease in the tuṭis as well; in that [decrease], there is the waning of conceptual constructs and the clarity of the non-conceptual.

10.s:
yathā hi ciraduḥkhārtaḥ paścādāttasukhasthitiḥ /
vismaratyeva tadduḥkhaṃ sukhaviśrāntivartmanā // 201
10.d:
यथा हि चिरदुःखार्तः पश्चादात्तसुखस्थितिः ।
विस्मरत्येव तद्दुःखं सुखविश्रान्तिवर्त्मना ॥ 201
10.m: Just as someone long afflicted by sorrow, having subsequently attained a state of pleasure, completely forgets that sorrow by way of resting in pleasure,

10.s:
tathā gatavikalpe'pi rūḍhāḥ saṃvedane janāḥ /
vikalpaviśrāntibalāttāṃ sattāṃ nābhimanvate // 202
10.d:
तथा गतविकल्पेऽपि रूढाः संवेदने जनाः ।
विकल्पविश्रान्तिबलात्तां सत्तां नाभिमन्वते ॥ 202
10.m: even so people who have become firmly established in consciousness wherein conceptual constructs have ceased, do not conceive of that [objective] existence by the force of the resting of conceptual constructs.

10.s:
vikalpanirhrāsavaśena yāti vikalpavandhyā paramārthasatyā /
saṃvitsvarūpaprakaṭatvamitthaṃ tatrāvadhāne yatatāṃ subuddhiḥ // 203
10.d:
विकल्पनिर्ह्रासवशेन याति विकल्पवन्ध्या परमार्थसत्या ।
संवित्स्वरूपप्रकटत्वमित्थं तत्रावधाने यततां सुबुद्धिः ॥ 203
10.m: By virtue of the waning of conceptual constructs, consciousness, devoid of conceptual constructs and true in the highest sense, comes to reveal its essential nature; thus let one of good intellect strive with attentiveness towards it.

10.s:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittau saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā /
iyaṃ sā tatra tatroktā sarvakāmadughā yataḥ // 204
10.d:
ग्राह्यग्राहकसंवित्तौ संबन्धे सावधानता ।
इयं सा तत्र तत्रोक्ता सर्वकामदुघा यतः ॥ 204
10.m: Attentiveness to the relationship in the consciousness of knower and known is that which is taught in various contexts, because it grants all desires.

10.s:
evaṃ dvayaṃ dvayaṃ yāvannyūnībhavati bhedagam /
tāvattuṭidvayaṃ yāti nyūnatāṃ kramaśaḥ sphuṭam // 205
10.d:
एवं द्वयं द्वयं यावन्न्यूनीभवति भेदगम् ।
तावत्तुटिद्वयं याति न्यूनतां क्रमशः स्फुटम् ॥ 205
10.m: In this way, as long as each pair belonging to the distinction diminishes, so long clearly does the pair of tuṭis diminish by degrees.

10.s:
ata eva śivāveśe dvituṭiḥ parigīyate /
ekā tu sā tuṭistatra pūrṇā śuddhaiva kevalam // 206
10.d:
अत एव शिवावेशे द्वितुटिः परिगीयते ।
एका तु सा तुटिस्तत्र पूर्णा शुद्धैव केवलम् ॥ 206
10.m:
For this very reason, in absorption into Śiva, a two-tuṭi [state] is proclaimed;
and among these, one tuṭi is completely full and purely alone. // 206

10.s:
dvitīyā śiva(śakti)rūpaiva sarvajñānakriyātmikā /
tasyāmavahito yogī kiṃ na vetti karoti vā // 207
10.d:
द्वितीया शिव(शक्ति)रूपैव सर्वज्ञानक्रियात्मिका ।
तस्यामवहितो योगी किं न वेत्ति करोति वा ॥ 207
10.m:
The second is of the nature of Śiva's power itself, consisting of all-knowledge and all-action;
attentive to this, what does the yogin not know or do? // 207

10.s:
tathā coktaṃ kallaṭena śrīmatā tuṭipātagaḥ /
lābhaḥ sarvajñakartṛtve tuṭeḥ pāto'parā tuṭiḥ // 208
10.d:
तथा चोक्तं कल्लटेन श्रीमता तुटिपातगः ।
लाभः सर्वज्ञकर्तृत्वे तुटेः पातोऽपरा तुटिः ॥ 208
10.m:
And thus it was declared by the illustrious Kallaṭa: "The acquisition consisting in all-knowing and all-doing [arises] when one is situated at the fall of a tuṭi;
the fall of a tuṭi is the other tuṭi." // 208

10.s:
ādyāyāṃ tu tuṭau sarvaṃ sarvataḥ pūrṇamekatām /
gataṃ kiṃ tatra vedyaṃ vā kāryaṃ vā vyapadeśabhāk // 209
10.d:
आद्यायां तु तुटौ सर्वं सर्वतः पूर्णमेकताम् ।
गतं किं तत्र वेद्यं वा कार्यं वा व्यपदेशभाक् ॥ 209
10.m:
In the first tuṭi, however, everything, completely full in every way, has merged into unity;
what could be an object of cognition there, or what effect could receive a designation? // 209

10.s:
ato bhedasamullāsakalāṃ prāthamikīṃ budhāḥ /
cinvanti pratibhāṃ devīṃ sarvajñatvādisiddhaye // 210
10.d:
अतो भेदसमुल्लासकलां प्राथमिकीं बुधाः ।
चिन्वन्ति प्रतिभां देवीं सर्वज्ञत्वादिसिद्धये ॥ 210
10.m:
Therefore, the wise cultivate the goddess of intuitive flash, the initial fraction of the manifestation of difference,
for the attainment of omniscience and the rest. // 210

10.s:
saiva śaktiḥ śivasyoktā tṛtīyādituṭiṣvatha /
mantrādi(dhi)nāthatacchaktimantreśādyāḥ kramoditāḥ // 211
10.d:
सैव शक्तिः शिवस्योक्ता तृतीयादितुटिष्वथ ।
मन्त्रादि(धि)नाथतच्छक्तिमन्त्रेशाद्याः क्रमोदिताः ॥ 211
10.m:
That very [intuition] is declared to be the power of Śiva. Then, in the third and subsequent tuṭis,
the lords of mantras and their powers, the Mantreśvaras, and the like, are taught in succession. // 211

10.s:
tāsu saṃdadhataścittamavadhānaikadharmakam /
tattatsiddhisamāveśaḥ svayamevopajāyate // 212
10.d:
तासु संदधतश्चित्तमवधानैकधर्मकम् ।
तत्तत्सिद्धिसमावेशः स्वयमेवोपजायते ॥ 212
10.m:
For one who fixes the mind, whose sole characteristic is attentiveness, on them,
absorption into those respective spiritual accomplishments arises spontaneously. // 212

10.s:
ata eva yathā bhedabahutvaṃ dūratā tathā /
saṃvittau tuṭibāhulyādakṣārthāsaṃnikarṣavat // 213
10.d:
अत एव यथा भेदबहुत्वं दूरता तथा ।
संवित्तौ तुटिबाहुल्यादक्षार्थासंनिकर्षवत् ॥ 213
10.m:
For this very reason, just as there is a multiplicity of difference, so there is distance
in consciousness due to the abundance of tuṭis, like the lack of contact between a sense organ and its object. // 213

10.s:
yathā yathā hi nyūnatvaṃ tuṭīnāṃ hrāsato bhidaḥ /
tathā tathātinaikaṭyaṃ saṃvidaḥ syācchivāvadhi // 214
10.d:
यथा यथा हि न्यूनत्वं तुटीनां ह्रासतो भिदः ।
तथा तथातिनैकट्यं संविदः स्याच्छिवावधि ॥ 214
10.m:
For to the extent that there is a diminution of the tuṭis due to the decrease of difference,
to that extent there is an extreme proximity of consciousness, up to Śiva. // 214

10.s:
śivatattvamataḥ proktamantikaṃ sarvato'mutaḥ /
ata eva prayatno'yaṃ tatpraveśe na vidyate // 215
10.d:
शिवतत्त्वमतः प्रोक्तमन्तिकं सर्वतोऽमुतः ।
अत एव प्रयत्नोऽयं तत्प्रवेशे न विद्यते ॥ 215
10.m:
Hence, the Śiva principle is declared to be closer than everything [else];
for this reason, no effort exists for entry into it. // 215

10.s:
yathā yathā hi dūratvaṃ yatnayogastathā tathā /
bhāvanākaraṇādīnāṃ śive niravakāśatām // 216
10.d:
यथा यथा हि दूरत्वं यत्नयोगस्तथा तथा ।
भावनाकरणादीनां शिवे निरवकाशताम् ॥ 216
10.m:
For to the extent that there is distance, to that extent there is the application of effort;
people rich in oral tradition consider meditation, ritual instruments, and the like // 216

10.s:
ata eva hi manyante saṃpradāyadhanā janāḥ /
tathā hi dṛśyatāṃ loko ghaṭādervedane yathā // 217
10.d:
अत एव हि मन्यन्ते संप्रदायधना जनाः ।
तथा हि दृश्यतां लोको घटादेर्वेदने यथा ॥ 217
10.m:
to have no scope in Śiva for this very reason.
For let ordinary experience be observed: just as in knowing a pot or the like // 217

10.s:
prayatnavānivābhāti tathā kiṃ sukhavedane /
āntaratvamidaṃ prāhuḥ saṃvinnaikaṭyaśālitām // 218
10.d:
प्रयत्नवानिवाभाति तथा किं सुखवेदने ।
आन्तरत्वमिदं प्राहुः संविन्नैकट्यशालिताम् ॥ 218
10.m:
one appears as if making an effort, does one do so in the cognition of pleasure?
They call this internality, possessing proximity to consciousness, // 218

10.s:
tāṃ ca cidrūpatonmeṣaṃ bāhyatvaṃ tannimeṣatām /
bhavināṃ tvantiko'pyevaṃ na bhātītyatidūratā // 219
10.d:
तां च चिद्रूपतोन्मेषं बाह्यत्वं तन्निमेषताम् ।
भविनां त्वन्तिकोऽप्येवं न भातीत्यतिदूरता ॥ 219
10.m:
and that [internality is] the opening of the nature of consciousness, while externality is its closing.
Yet even though it is so close, it does not appear to worldly beings; hence it is extremely distant. // 219

10.s:
dūre'pi hyantikībhūte bhānaṃ syāttvatra tatkatham /
na ca bījāṅkuralatādalapuṣpaphalādivat // 220
10.d:
दूरेऽपि ह्यन्तिकीभूते भानं स्यात्त्वत्र तत्कथम् ।
न च बीजाङ्कुरलतादलपुष्पफलादिवत् ॥ 220
10.m:
For even what is distant appears when it becomes near, but how could that be so here?
Nor does this consciousness become sequential // 220

10.s:
kramikeyaṃ bhavetsaṃvitsūtastatra kilāṅkuraḥ /
bījāllatā tvaṅkurānno bījādiha sarvataḥ // 221
10.d:
क्रमिकेयं भवेत्संवित्सूतस्तत्र किलाङ्कुरः ।
बीजाल्लता त्वङ्कुरान्नो बीजादिह सर्वतः ॥ 221
10.m:
like seed, sprout, creeper, leaf, flower, fruit, and so on.
There, indeed, the sprout is produced from the seed, and the creeper from the sprout, but not here from the seed in all respects. // 221

10.s:
saṃvittattvaṃ bhāsamānaṃ paripūrṇaṃ hi sarvataḥ /
sarvasya kāraṇaṃ proktaṃ sarvatraivoditaṃ yataḥ // 222
10.d:
संवित्तत्त्वं भासमानं परिपूर्णं हि सर्वतः ।
सर्वस्य कारणं प्रोक्तं सर्वत्रैवोदितं यतः ॥ 222
10.m:
For the principle of consciousness, shining forth completely full on all sides,
is declared to be the cause of everything, because it arises everywhere. // 222

10.s:
tata eva ghaṭe'pyeṣā prāṇavṛttiryadi sphuret /
viśrāmyeccāśu tatraiva śivabīje layaṃ vrajet // 223
10.d:
तत एव घटेऽप्येषा प्राणवृत्तिर्यदि स्फुरेत् ।
विश्राम्येच्चाशु तत्रैव शिवबीजे लयं व्रजेत् ॥ 223
10.m:
Therefore, even in the case of a pot, if this movement of the vital breath pulses forth,
it should quickly come to rest right there, and dissolve into the seed of Śiva. // 223

10.s:
na tu kramikatā kācicchivātmatve kadācana /
anyanmantrādi(dhi)nāthādi kāraṇaṃ tattu saṃnidheḥ // 224
10.d:
न तु क्रमिकता काचिच्छिवात्मत्वे कदाचन ।
अन्यन्मन्त्रादि(धि)नाथादि कारणं तत्तु संनिधेः ॥ 224
10.m:
Never, however, is there any sequentiality in being the essence of Śiva;
what is other—the lords of mantras and the rest—is a cause because of proximity // 224

10.s:
śivābhedācca kiṃ cātha dvaite naikaṭyavedanāt /
anayā ca diśā sarva sarvadā pravivecayan // 225
10.d:
शिवाभेदाच्च किं चाथ द्वैते नैकट्यवेदनात् ।
अनया च दिशा सर्व सर्वदा प्रविवेचयन् ॥ 225
10.m:
and non-difference from Śiva, or further, in duality, because of the cognition of nearness.
And by examining everything at all times in this manner, // 225

10.s:
bhairavāyata eva drāk ciccakreśvaratāṃ gataḥ /
sa itthaṃ prāṇago bhedaḥ khecarīcakragopitaḥ // 226
10.d:
भैरवायत एव द्राक् चिच्चक्रेश्वरतां गतः ।
स इत्थं प्राणगो भेदः खेचरीचक्रगोपितः ॥ 226
10.m:
one swiftly acts like Bhairava, having attained the sovereignty of the wheel of consciousness.
Thus this division residing in the vital breath, concealed by the wheel of khecarīs, // 226

10.s:
mayā prakaṭitaḥ śrīmacchāmbhavājñānuvartinā /
atraivādhvani vedyatvaṃ prāpte yā saṃvidudbhavet // 227
10.d:
मया प्रकटितः श्रीमच्छाम्भवाज्ञानुवर्तिना ।
अत्रैवाध्वनि वेद्यत्वं प्राप्ते या संविदुद्भवेत् ॥ 227
10.m:
has been revealed by me, following the command of the illustrious Śaṃbhu.
When this very path attains the status of an object of cognition, the consciousness that arises // 227

10.s:
tasyāḥ svakaṃ yadvaicitryaṃ tadavasthāpadābhidham /
jāgratsvapnaḥ suṣuptaṃ ca turyaṃ ca tadatītakam // 228
10.d:
तस्याः स्वकं यद्वैचित्र्यं तदवस्थापदाभिधम् ।
जाग्रत्स्वप्नः सुषुप्तं च तुर्यं च तदतीतकम् ॥ 228
10.m:
has a diversity of its own that is named the states or planes:
waking, dreaming, deep sleep, the fourth, and that which transcends it. // 228

10.s:
iti pañca padānyāhurekasminvedake sati /
tatra yaiṣā dharātattvācchivāntā tattvapaddhatiḥ // 229
10.d:
इति पञ्च पदान्याहुरेकस्मिन्वेदके सति ।
तत्र यैषा धरातत्त्वाच्छिवान्ता तत्त्वपद्धतिः ॥ 229
10.m:
Thus they speak of five planes, while the knower remains one.
There, that series of principles extending from the earth principle to Śiva, // 229

10.s:
tasyāmekaḥ pramātā cedavaśyaṃ jāgradādikam /
taddarśyate śaṃbhunāthaprasādādviditaṃ mayā // 230
10.d:
तस्यामेकः प्रमाता चेदवश्यं जाग्रदादिकम् ।
तद्दर्श्यते शंभुनाथप्रसादाद्विदितं मया ॥ 230
10.m:
if there is a single knower in it, inevitably [exhibits] waking and the rest;
that is now demonstrated by me, known through the grace of Śaṃbhunātha. // 230

10.s:
yadadhiṣṭheyameveha nādhiṣṭhātṛ kadācana /
saṃvedanagataṃ vedyaṃ tajjāgratsamudāhṛtam // 231
10.d:
यदधिष्ठेयमेवेह नाधिष्ठातृ कदाचन ।
संवेदनगतं वेद्यं तज्जाग्रत्समुदाहृतम् ॥ 231
10.m:
That which is strictly an object governed, never a governing subject,
being an object of cognition within awareness, is called the waking state. // 231

10.s:
caitramaitrādibhūtāni tattvāni ca dharāditaḥ /
abhidhākaraṇībhūtāḥ śabdāḥ kiṃ cābhidhā pramā // 232
10.d:
चैत्रमैत्रादिभूतानि तत्त्वानि च धरादितः ।
अभिधाकरणीभूताः शब्दाः किं चाभिधा प्रमा ॥ 232
10.m:
The entities such as Caitra and Maitra, the principles beginning with earth,
the words serving as instruments of naming, and also naming, cognition, // 232

10.s:
pramātṛmeyatanmānapramārūpaṃ catuṣṭayam /
viśvametadadhiṣṭheyaṃ yadā jāgrattadā smṛtam // 233
10.d:
प्रमातृमेयतन्मानप्रमारूपं चतुष्टयम् ।
विश्वमेतदधिष्ठेयं यदा जाग्रत्तदा स्मृतम् ॥ 233
10.m:
the tetrad consisting of the knower, the object of knowledge, its means of cognition, and cognition—
when all this universe is an object governed, then it is remembered as waking. // 233

10.s:
tathā hi bhāsate yattannīlamantaḥ pravedane /
saṃkalparūpe bāhyasya tadadhiṣṭhātṛ bodhakam // 234
10.d:
तथा हि भासते यत्तन्नीलमन्तः प्रवेदने ।
संकल्परूपे बाह्यस्य तदधिष्ठातृ बोधकम् ॥ 234
10.m:
To explain: that blue object which appears in internal cognition
of a conceptual nature is the governing, revealing agent of the external [object]. // 234

10.s:
yattu bāhyatayā nīlaṃ cakāstyasya na vidyate /
kathaṃcidapyadhiṣṭhātṛbhāvastajjāgraducyate // 235
10.d:
यत्तु बाह्यतया नीलं चकास्त्यस्य न विद्यते ।
कथंचिदप्यधिष्ठातृभावस्तज्जाग्रदुच्यते ॥ 235
10.m:
However, that blue object which shines as external has no
governing nature whatsoever; that is called waking. // 235

10.s:
tatra caitre bhāsamāne yo dehāṃśaḥ sa kathyate /
abuddho yastu mānāṃśaḥ sa buddho mitikārakaḥ // 236
10.d:
तत्र चैत्रे भासमाने यो देहांशः स कथ्यते ।
अबुद्धो यस्तु मानांशः स बुद्धो मितिकारकः ॥ 236
10.m:
There, when Caitra appears, the bodily portion is declared to be
the unawakened; the portion consisting of the means of knowledge, producing cognition, is the awakened; // 236

10.s:
prabuddhaḥ suprabuddhaśca pramāmātreti ca kramaḥ /
cāturvidhyaṃ hi piṇḍasthanāmni jāgrati kīrtitam // 237
10.d:
प्रबुद्धः सुप्रबुद्धश्च प्रमामात्रेति च क्रमः ।
चातुर्विध्यं हि पिण्डस्थनाम्नि जाग्रति कीर्तितम् ॥ 237
10.m:
the well-awakened, and the fully awakened, and sheer cognition—such is the sequence.
For a fourfold division is proclaimed in the waking state called "residing in the body." // 237

10.s:
jāgradādi catuṣkaṃ hi pratyekamiha vidyate /
jāgrajjāgradabuddhaṃ tajjāgratsvapnastu buddhatā // 238
10.d:
जाग्रदादि चतुष्कं हि प्रत्येकमिह विद्यते ।
जाग्रज्जाग्रदबुद्धं तज्जाग्रत्स्वप्नस्तु बुद्धता ॥ 238
10.m:
For the tetrad beginning with waking is found individually here:
waking within waking is the unawakened, while dreaming within waking is the state of being awakened, // 238

10.s:
ityādi turyātītaṃ tu sarvagatvātpṛthakkutaḥ /
uktaṃ ca piṇḍagaṃ jāgradabuddhaṃ buddhameva ca // 239
10.d:
इत्यादि तुर्यातीतं तु सर्वगत्वात्पृथक्कुतः ।
उक्तं च पिण्डगं जाग्रदबुद्धं बुद्धमेव च ॥ 239
10.m:
and so on. But the transcendent fourth, because it is omnipresent, how could it be separate?
And it is stated: "Residing in the body is the waking state; unawakened, and awakened, // 239

10.s:
prabuddhaṃ suprabuddhaṃ ca caturvidhamidaṃ smṛtam /
meyabhūmiriyaṃ mukhyā jāgradākhyānyadantarā // 240
10.d:
प्रबुद्धं सुप्रबुद्धं च चतुर्विधमिदं स्मृतम् ।
मेयभूमिरियं मुख्या जाग्रदाख्यान्यदन्तरा ॥ 240
10.m:
and well-awakened, and fully awakened—this is remembered as fourfold."
This principal level of the object of knowledge is named waking; between the others, // 240

10.s:
bhūtatattvābhidhānānāṃ yo'ṃśo'dhiṣṭheya ucyate /
piṇḍasthamiti taṃ prāhuriti śrīmālinīmate // 241
10.d:
भूततत्त्वाभिधानानां योऽंशोऽधिष्ठेय उच्यते ।
पिण्डस्थमिति तं प्राहुरिति श्रीमालिनीमते ॥ 241
10.m:
that portion of the elements, principles, and names which is said to be the object governed
they call "residing in the body," according to the tradition of the illustrious Mālinī. // 241

10.s:
laukikī jāgradityeṣā saṃjñā piṇḍasthamityapi /
yogināṃ yogasiddhyarthaṃ saṃjñeyaṃ paribhāṣyate // 242
10.d:
लौकिकी जाग्रदित्येषा संज्ञा पिण्डस्थमित्यपि ।
योगिनां योगसिद्ध्यर्थं संज्ञेयं परिभाष्यते ॥ 242
10.m:
This designation "waking" is conventional, and "residing in the body"
is defined as a technical term for yogins for the sake of yogic accomplishment. // 242

10.s:
adhiṣṭheyasamāpattimadhyāsīnasya yoginaḥ /
tādātmyaṃ kila piṇḍasthaṃ mitaṃ piṇḍaṃ hi piṇḍitam // 243
10.d:
अधिष्ठेयसमापत्तिमध्यासीनस्य योगिनः ।
तादात्म्यं किल पिण्डस्थं मितं पिण्डं हि पिण्डितम् ॥ 243
10.m:
For the yogin who is seated in attunement to what is governed,
identity is indeed "residing in the body," for a body is limited, gathered together. // 243

10.s:
prasaṃkhyānaikarūḍhānāṃ jñānināṃ tu taducyate /
sarvatobhadramāpūrṇaṃ sarvato vedyasattayā // 244
10.d:
प्रसंख्यानैकरूढानां ज्ञानिनां तु तदुच्यते ।
सर्वतोभद्रमापूर्णं सर्वतो वेद्यसत्तया ॥ 244
10.m:
For the knowers who are firmly rooted solely in philosophical discernment, however, that is called
"auspicious on all sides," completely filled on all sides by the existence of the knowable. // 244

10.s:
sarvasattāsamāpūrṇa viśvaṃ paśyedyato yataḥ /
jñānī tatastataḥ saṃvittatvamasya prakāśate // 245
10.d:
सर्वसत्तासमापूर्ण विश्वं पश्येद्यतो यतः ।
ज्ञानी ततस्ततः संवित्तत्वमस्य प्रकाशते ॥ 245
10.m:
From whatever [aspect] the knower sees the universe completely filled with the reality of everything,
from that very [aspect] the principle of consciousness shines forth to him. // 245

10.s:
lokayogaprasaṃkhyānatrairūpyavaśataḥ kila /
nāmāni trīṇi bhaṇyante svapnādiṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ // 246
10.d:
लोकयोगप्रसंख्यानत्रैरूप्यवशतः किल ।
नामानि त्रीणि भण्यन्ते स्वप्नादिष्वप्ययं विधिः ॥ 246
10.m:
Indeed, on account of the threefold nature consisting of common worldly usage, yoga, and philosophical discernment,
three names are spoken; this rule applies to dreaming and the rest as well. // 246

10.s:
yattvadhiṣṭhānakaraṇabhāvamadhyāsya vartate /
vedyaṃ satpūrvakathitaṃ bhūtatattvābhidhāmayam // 247
10.d:
यत्त्वधिष्ठानकरणभावमध्यास्य वर्तते ।
वेद्यं सत्पूर्वकथितं भूततत्त्वाभिधामयम् ॥ 247
10.m:
However, that which exists having entered the condition of being an instrument of governance,
being an object of cognition previously described as consisting of the elements, principles, and names, // 247

10.s:
tatsvapno mukhyato jñeyaṃ tacca vaikalpike pathi /
vaikalpikapathārūḍhavedyasāmyāvabhāsanāt // 248
10.d:
तत्स्वप्नो मुख्यतो ज्ञेयं तच्च वैकल्पिके पथि ।
वैकल्पिकपथारूढवेद्यसाम्यावभासनात् ॥ 248
10.m:
that is primarily to be known as dreaming, and that is on the conceptual path,
because it manifests a resemblance to an object of knowledge situated on the conceptual path. // 248

10.s:
lokarūḍho'pyasau svapnaḥ sāmyaṃ cābāhyarūpatā /
utprekṣāsvapnasaṃkalpasmṛtyunmādādidṛṣṭiṣu // 249
10.d:
लोकरूढोऽप्यसौ स्वप्नः साम्यं चाबाह्यरूपता ।
उत्प्रेक्षास्वप्नसंकल्पस्मृत्युन्मादादिदृष्टिषु ॥ 249
10.m:
This dreaming is also well-known in worldly usage, and the resemblance is the non-external nature
in visions of imagination, dreaming, intention, memory, madness, and the like. // 249

10.s:
vispaṣṭaṃ yadvedyajātaṃ jāgranmukhyatayaiva tat /
yattu tatrāpyavispaṣṭaṃ spaṣṭādhiṣṭhātṛ bhāsate // 250
10.d:
विस्पष्टं यद्वेद्यजातं जाग्रन्मुख्यतयैव तत् ।
यत्तु तत्राप्यविस्पष्टं स्पष्टाधिष्ठातृ भासते ॥ 250
10.m:
Whatever aggregate of knowables is clear, that is primarily waking;
but that which, even in that case, is unclear, while its governing subject appears clearly, // 250

10.s:
vikalpāntaragaṃ vedyaṃ tatsvapnapadamucyate /
tadaiva tasya vettyeva svayameva hyabāhyatām // 251
10.d:
विकल्पान्तरगं वेद्यं तत्स्वप्नपदमुच्यते ।
तदैव तस्य वेत्त्येव स्वयमेव ह्यबाह्यताम् ॥ 251
10.m: An object of knowledge that falls within another conceptual construct is called the sphere of dream; / for at that very moment, the knower himself indeed knows its non-external nature // 251

10.s:
pramātrantarasādhārabhāvahānyasthirātmate /
tatrāpi cāturvidhyaṃ tat prāgdiśaiva prakalpayet // 252
10.d:
प्रमात्रन्तरसाधारभावहान्यस्थिरात्मते ।
तत्रापि चातुर्विध्यं तत् प्राग्दिशैव प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 252
10.m: Because of its lack of commonality with other knowers and its unstable nature. / There too, one should conceiving of that fourfold division just according to the previous manner: // 252

10.s:
gatāgataṃ suvikṣiptaṃ saṃgataṃ susamāhitam /
atrāpi pūrvavannāma laukikaṃ svapna ityadaḥ // 253
10.d:
गतागतं सुविक्षिप्तं संगतं सुसमाहितम् ।
अत्रापि पूर्ववन्नाम लौकिकं स्वप्न इत्यदः ॥ 253
10.m: ‘Gone and come back’, ‘well dispersed’, ‘collected’, and ‘well concentrated’. / Here too, as before, this is the conventional worldly designation: ‘dream’. // 253

10.s:
bāhyābhimatabhāvānāṃ svāpo hyagrahaṇaṃ matam /
sarvādhvanaḥ padaṃ prāṇaḥ saṃkalpo'vagamātmakaḥ // 254
10.d:
बाह्याभिमतभावानां स्वापो ह्यग्रहणं मतम् ।
सर्वाध्वनः पदं प्राणः संकल्पोऽवगमात्मकः ॥ 254
10.m: For ‘sleep’ is considered the non-grasping of entities regarded as external. / The sphere of the entire path is vital breath; conceptualization consists in comprehension. // 254

10.s:
padaṃ ca tatsamāpatti padasthaṃ yogino viduḥ /
vedyasattāṃ bahirbhūtāmanapekṣyaiva sarvataḥ // 255
10.d:
पदं च तत्समापत्ति पदस्थं योगिनो विदुः ।
वेद्यसत्तां बहिर्भूतामनपेक्ष्यैव सर्वतः ॥ 255
10.m: And that sphere is meditative absorption; yogins know it as ‘abiding in the sphere’ (padastha). / Completely disregarding the reality of objects of knowledge as existing outside, // 255

10.s:
vedye svātantryabhāg jñānaṃ svapnaṃ vyāptitayā bhajet /
mānabhūmiriyaṃ mukhyā svapno hyāmarśanātmakaḥ // 256
10.d:
वेद्ये स्वातन्त्र्यभाग् ज्ञानं स्वप्नं व्याप्तितया भजेत् ।
मानभूमिरियं मुख्या स्वप्नो ह्यामर्शनात्मकः ॥ 256
10.m: Knowledge sharing in absolute autonomy over the object of knowledge resorts to dream as a pervading state. / This is the primary level of the means of knowledge, for dream consists of reflective appraisal. // 256

10.s:
vedyacchāyo'vabhāso hi meye'dhiṣṭhānamucyate /
yattvadhiṣṭhātṛbhūtādeḥ pūrvoktasya vapurdhruvam // 257
10.d:
वेद्यच्छायोऽवभासो हि मेयेऽधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।
यत्त्वधिष्ठातृभूतादेः पूर्वोक्तस्य वपुर्ध्रुवम् ॥ 257
10.m: The manifestation bearing the shadow of the object of knowledge is indeed called the ‘basis’ regarding the object. / But that unchanging nature of the previously mentioned conscious controller of the elements and so forth, // 257

10.s:
bījaṃ viśvasya tattūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ sauṣuptamucyate /
anubhūtau vikalpe ca yo'sau draṣṭā sa eva hi // 258
10.d:
बीजं विश्वस्य तत्तूष्णींभूतं सौषुप्तमुच्यते ।
अनुभूतौ विकल्पे च योऽसौ द्रष्टा स एव हि ॥ 258
10.m: Which is the seed of the universe and has become silent, is called deep sleep. / For he who is the witness in direct experience and in conceptualization is the very same [one]. // 258

10.s:
na bhāvagrahaṇaṃ tena suṣṭhu suptatvamucyate /
tatsāmyāllaukikīṃ nidrāṃ suṣuptaṃ manvate budhāḥ // 259
10.d:
न भावग्रहणं तेन सुष्ठु सुप्तत्वमुच्यते ।
तत्साम्याल्लौकिकीं निद्रां सुषुप्तं मन्वते बुधाः ॥ 259
10.m: Therefore, there is no grasping of entities; this is called being ‘soundly asleep’. / By analogy with this, the wise consider conventional slumber to be deep sleep. // 259

10.s:
bījabhāvo'thāgrahaṇaṃ sāmyaṃ tūṣṇīṃsvabhāvatā /
mukhyā mātṛdaśā seyaṃ suṣuptākhyā nigadyate // 260
10.d:
बीजभावोऽथाग्रहणं साम्यं तूष्णींस्वभावता ।
मुख्या मातृदशा सेयं सुषुप्ताख्या निगद्यते ॥ 260
10.m: The condition of being the seed, non-grasping, equality, and having a silent nature— / this is said to be that primary state of the subject, designated as deep sleep. // 260

10.s:
rūpakatvācca rūpaṃ tattādātmyaṃ yoginaḥ punaḥ /
rūpasthaṃ tatsamāpattyaudāsīnyaṃ rūpiṇāṃ viduḥ // 261
10.d:
रूपकत्वाच्च रूपं तत्तादात्म्यं योगिनः पुनः ।
रूपस्थं तत्समापत्त्यौदासीन्यं रूपिणां विदुः ॥ 261
10.m: And because it is an agent of differentiation, it is ‘form’ (rūpa); yogins know identity with it / as ‘abiding in form’ (rūpastha), which, through absorption in it, is indifference regarding differentiated entities. // 261

10.s:
prasaṃkhyānavataḥ kāpi vedyasaṃkocanātra yat /
nāsti tena mahāvyāptiriyaṃ tadanusārataḥ // 262
10.d:
प्रसंख्यानवतः कापि वेद्यसंकोचनात्र यत् ।
नास्ति तेन महाव्याप्तिरियं तदनुसारतः ॥ 262
10.m: Because for one possessing higher contemplation there is here no limitation whatever by objects of knowledge, / this is therefore the ‘great pervasion’ in accordance with that. // 262

10.s:
udāsīnasya tasyāpi vedyaṃ yena caturvidham /
bhūtādi tadupādhyutthamatra bhedacatuṣṭayam // 263
10.d:
उदासीनस्य तस्यापि वेद्यं येन चतुर्विधम् ।
भूतादि तदुपाध्युत्थमत्र भेदचतुष्टयम् ॥ 263
10.m: Because the object of knowledge even for that indifferent one is fourfold, / the fourfold distinction here arises from its conditioning adjuncts such as the elements: // 263

10.s:
uditaṃ vipulaṃ śāntaṃ suprasannamathāparam /
yattu pramātmakaṃ rūpaṃ pramāturupari sthitam // 264
10.d:
उदितं विपुलं शान्तं सुप्रसन्नमथापरम् ।
यत्तु प्रमात्मकं रूपं प्रमातुरुपरि स्थितम् ॥ 264
10.m: The arisen, the extensive, the quiescent, and then the exceedingly serene. / But the form that consists of the means of knowledge, standing above the knower, // 264

10.s:
pūrṇatāgamanaunmukhyamaudāsīnyātparicyutiḥ /
tatturyamucyate śaktisamāveśo hyasau mataḥ // 265
10.d:
पूर्णतागमनौन्मुख्यमौदासीन्यात्परिच्युतिः ।
तत्तुर्यमुच्यते शक्तिसमावेशो ह्यसौ मतः ॥ 265
10.m: Turning toward the attainment of fullness, slipping away from indifference— / that is called the fourth [state, turya]; for it is considered absorption in power. // 265

10.s:
sā saṃvitsvaprakāśā tu kaiściduktā prameyataḥ /
mānānmātuśca bhinnaiva tadarthaṃ tritayaṃ yataḥ // 266
10.d:
सा संवित्स्वप्रकाशा तु कैश्चिदुक्ता प्रमेयतः ।
मानान्मातुश्च भिन्नैव तदर्थं त्रितयं यतः ॥ 266
10.m: That consciousness, however, is self-luminous, though stated by some to be distinct from the object of knowledge, / from the means of knowledge, and from the knower, since the triad exists for its sake. // 266

10.s:
meyaṃ māne mātari tat so'pi tasyāṃ mitau sphuṭam /
viśrāmyatīti saivaiṣā devī viśvaikajīvitam // 267
10.d:
मेयं माने मातरि तत् सोऽपि तस्यां मितौ स्फुटम् ।
विश्राम्यतीति सैवैषा देवी विश्वैकजीवितम् ॥ 267
10.m: The object rests in the means of knowledge, that in the knower, and he rests clearly in that cognition. / Thus, this very Goddess is the sole life of the universe. // 267

10.s:
rūpaṃ dṛśāhamityaṃśatrayamuttīrya vartate /
dvāramātrāśritopāyā paśyāmītyanupāyikā // 268
10.d:
रूपं दृशाहमित्यंशत्रयमुत्तीर्य वर्तते ।
द्वारमात्राश्रितोपाया पश्यामीत्यनुपायिका ॥ 268
10.m: Transcending the threefold portion of ‘object of sight’, ‘seeing’, and ‘I’, she endures; / having a means based solely on a gateway, she is without means in the sense of ‘I see’. // 268

10.s:
pramātṛtā svatantratvarūpā seyaṃ prakāśate /
saṃvitturīyarūpaivaṃ prakāśātmā svayaṃ ca sā // 269
10.d:
प्रमातृता स्वतन्त्रत्वरूपा सेयं प्रकाशते ।
संवित्तुरीयरूपैवं प्रकाशात्मा स्वयं च सा ॥ 269
10.m: This subjectivity shines forth consisting of absolute autonomy; / in this way, consciousness is the fourth form, and it is itself luminous by nature. // 269

10.s:
tatsamāveśatādātmye mātṛtvaṃ bhavati sphuṭam /
tatsamāveśoparāgānmānatvaṃ meyatā punaḥ // 270
10.d:
तत्समावेशतादात्म्ये मातृत्वं भवति स्फुटम् ।
तत्समावेशोपरागान्मानत्वं मेयता पुनः ॥ 270
10.m: In identity with absorption into it, subjectivity becomes manifest; / from the coloring of absorption into it comes the status of means of knowledge, and the status of object of knowledge, moreover, // 270

10.s:
tatsamāveśanaikaṭyāttrayaṃ tattadanugrahāt /
vedyādibhedagalanāduktā seyamanāmayā // 271
10.d:
तत्समावेशनैकट्यात्त्रयं तत्तदनुग्रहात् ।
वेद्यादिभेदगलनादुक्ता सेयमनामया ॥ 271
10.m: Arises from proximity to absorption into it; that triad exists by its grace. / Because the differentiation of object of knowledge and so forth dissolves, this [state] is called untainted. // 271

10.s:
mātrādyanugrahādā(dhā)nātsavyāpāreti bhaṇyate /
jāgradādyapi devasya śaktitvena vyavasthitam // 272
10.d:
मात्राद्यनुग्रहादा(धा)नात्सव्यापारेति भण्यते ।
जाग्रदाद्यपि देवस्य शक्तित्वेन व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 272
10.m: It is said to be ‘active’ because it bestows grace upon the knower and the rest. / Even the waking state and the rest are established as powers of the Lord. // 272

10.s:
aparaṃ parāparaṃ ca dvidhā tatsā parā tviyam /
rūpakatvādudāsīnāccyuteyaṃ pūrṇatonmukhī // 273
10.d:
अपरं परापरं च द्विधा तत्सा परा त्वियम् ।
रूपकत्वादुदासीनाच्च्युतेयं पूर्णतोन्मुखी ॥ 273
10.m: They are of two kinds: lower and intermediate; but this [fourth] is the supreme [power]. / Having fallen away from the indifferent [state] because it is differentiating, and turning toward fullness, // 273

10.s:
daśā tasyāṃ samāpattī rūpātītaṃ tu yoginaḥ /
pūrṇataunmukhyayogitvādviśvaṃ paśyati tanmayaḥ // 274
10.d:
दशा तस्यां समापत्ती रूपातीतं तु योगिनः ।
पूर्णतौन्मुख्ययोगित्वाद्विश्वं पश्यति तन्मयः ॥ 274
10.m: When absorption occurs in that state, yogins call it ‘transcending form’ (rūpātīta). / Because he is joined with turning toward fullness, he who is identified with it perceives the universe. // 274

10.s:
prasaṃkhyātā pracayatasteneyaṃ pracayo matā /
naitasyāmaparā turyadaśā saṃbhāvyate kila // 275
10.d:
प्रसंख्याता प्रचयतस्तेनेयं प्रचयो मता ।
नैतस्यामपरा तुर्यदशा संभाव्यते किल ॥ 275
10.m: It is gathered up by the contemplator, and therefore this is considered ‘accumulation’ (pracaya). / Indeed, in this state no other fourth state can be conceived. // 275

10.s:
saṃvinna kila vedyā sā vittvenaiva hi bhāsate /
jāgradādyāstu saṃbhāvyāstisro'syāḥ prāgdaśā yataḥ // 276
10.d:
संविन्न किल वेद्या सा वित्त्वेनैव हि भासते ।
जाग्रदाद्यास्तु संभाव्यास्तिस्रोऽस्याः प्राग्दशा यतः ॥ 276
10.m: For consciousness is certainly not an object of knowledge; it shines forth only as cognition. / The three states, however, beginning with waking, may be conceived, since they precede it. // 276

10.s:
tritayānugrahātseyaṃ tenoktā trikaśāsane /
manonmanamanantaṃ ca sarvārthamiti bhedataḥ // 277
10.d:
त्रितयानुग्रहात्सेयं तेनोक्ता त्रिकशासने ।
मनोन्मनमनन्तं च सर्वार्थमिति भेदतः ॥ 277
10.m: Therefore, through grace upon the triad, it is taught in the Trika tradition / according to its divisions as ‘supra-mental’ (manonmana), ‘infinite’ (ananta), and ‘all-objective’ (sarvārtha). // 277

10.s:
yattu pūrṇānavacchinnavapurānandanirbharam /
turyātītaṃ tu tatprāhustadeva paramaṃ padam // 278
10.d:
यत्तु पूर्णानवच्छिन्नवपुरानन्दनिर्भरम् ।
तुर्यातीतं तु तत्प्राहुस्तदेव परमं पदम् ॥ 278
10.m: That, however, whose form is full, undivided, and filled with bliss, / they call ‘beyond the fourth’ (turyātīta); that alone is the supreme abode. // 278

10.s:
nātra yogasya sadbhāvo bhāvanāderabhāvataḥ /
aprameye'paricchinne svatantre bhāvyatā kutaḥ // 279
10.d:
नात्र योगस्य सद्भावो भावनादेरभावतः ।
अप्रमेयेऽपरिच्छिन्ने स्वतन्त्रे भाव्यता कुतः ॥ 279
10.m: Here there is no existence of yoga, because of the absence of contemplative cultivation and the like. / In the unmeasurable, undivided, and autonomous, how could there be an object of contemplation? // 279

10.s:
yogādyabhāvatastena nāmāsminnādiśadvibhuḥ /
prasaṃkhyānabalāttvetadrūpaṃ pūrṇatvayogataḥ // 280
10.d:
योगाद्यभावतस्तेन नामास्मिन्नादिशद्विभुः ।
प्रसंख्यानबलात्त्वेतद्रूपं पूर्णत्वयोगतः ॥ 280
10.m: Therefore, because of the absence of yoga and the like, the All-pervading Lord assigned no name to it. / Yet by the power of higher contemplation, this form, through its connection with fullness, // 280

10.s:
anuttarādiha proktaṃ mahāpracayasaṃjñitam /
pūrṇatvādeva bhedānāmasyāṃ saṃbhāvanā na hi // 281
10.d:
अनुत्तरादिह प्रोक्तं महाप्रचयसंज्ञितम् ।
पूर्णत्वादेव भेदानामस्यां संभावना न हि ॥ 281
10.m: Is taught here beginning with the unexcelled, named the ‘great accumulation’ (mahāpracaya). / Precisely because of fullness, no distinctions can be conceived within it. // 281

10.s:
tannirāsāya naitasyāṃ bheda ukto viśeṣaṇam /
satatoditamityetatsarvavyāpitvasūcakam // 282
10.d:
तन्निरासाय नैतस्यां भेद उक्तो विशेषणम् ।
सततोदितमित्येतत्सर्वव्यापित्वसूचकम् ॥ 282
10.m: To refute them, no distinguishing qualification is spoken of in it. / The expression ‘ever-arisen’ indicates its all-pervasiveness. // 282

10.s:
na hyeka eva bhavati bhedaḥ kvacana kaścana /
turyātīte bheda ekaḥ satatodita ityayam // 283
10.d:
न ह्येक एव भवति भेदः क्वचन कश्चन ।
तुर्यातीते भेद एकः सततोदित इत्ययम् ॥ 283
10.m: For not even a single distinction exists anywhere at all. / To say that in the state beyond the fourth there is one distinction, namely ‘ever-arisen’, // 283

10.s:
mūḍhavādastena siddhamavibheditvamasya tu /
śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ padasthamaparaṃ viduḥ // 284
10.d:
मूढवादस्तेन सिद्धमविभेदित्वमस्य तु ।
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तेनोक्तं पदस्थमपरं विदुः ॥ 284
10.m: Is the assertion of fools; therefore, its lack of distinction is established. / Hence in the Śrīpūrva treatise it is said: ‘They know the inferior as abiding in the sphere; // 284

10.s:
mantrāstatpatayaḥ seśā rūpasthamiti kīrtyate /
rūpātītaṃ parā śaktiḥ savyāpārāpyanāmayā // 285
10.d:
मन्त्रास्तत्पतयः सेशा रूपस्थमिति कीर्त्यते ।
रूपातीतं परा शक्तिः सव्यापाराप्यनामया ॥ 285
10.m: The mantras and their lords along with the rulers are proclaimed as abiding in form; / transcending form is the supreme power, which is active though untainted; // 285

10.s:
niṣprapañco nirābhāsaḥ śuddhaḥ svātmanyavasthitaḥ /
sarvātītaḥ śivo jñeyo yaṃ viditvā vimucyate // 286
10.d:
निष्प्रपञ्चो निराभासः शुद्धः स्वात्मन्यवस्थितः ।
सर्वातीतः शिवो ज्ञेयो यं विदित्वा विमुच्यते ॥ 286
10.m: Free from worldly manifoldness, devoid of appearance, pure, resting in his own self, / transcending all, Śiva should be known, by knowing whom one is liberated.’ // 286

10.s:
iti śrīsumatiprajñācandrikāśāntatāmasaḥ /
śrīśaṃbhunāthaḥ sadbhāvaṃ jāgradādau nyarūpayat // 287
10.d:
इति श्रीसुमतिप्रज्ञाचन्द्रिकाशान्ततामसः ।
श्रीशंभुनाथः सद्भावं जाग्रदादौ न्यरूपयत् ॥ 287
10.m: Thus Śrī Śambhunātha, whose darkness was pacified by the moonlight of the wisdom of the venerable Sumati, / expounded the true reality in the waking state and the rest. // 287

10.s:
anye tu kathayantyeṣāṃ bhaṅgīmanyādṛśīṃ śritāḥ /
yadrūpaṃ jāgradādīnāṃ tadidānīṃ nirūpyate // 288
10.d:
अन्ये तु कथयन्त्येषां भङ्गीमन्यादृशीं श्रिताः ।
यद्रूपं जाग्रदादीनां तदिदानीं निरूप्यते ॥ 288
10.m: Others, however, explain this by adopting a different manner. / That form of the waking state and the others is now expounded. // 288

10.s:
tatrākṣavṛttimāśritya bāhyākāragraho hi yaḥ /
tajjāgratsphuṭamāsīnamanubandhi punaḥ punaḥ // 289
10.d:
तत्राक्षवृत्तिमाश्रित्य बाह्याकारग्रहो हि यः ।
तज्जाग्रत्स्फुटमासीनमनुबन्धि पुनः पुनः ॥ 289
10.m: There, that which is the grasping of external forms by relying on the operation of the sense organs / is the waking state, clearly seated, recurring again and again. // 289

10.s:
ātmasaṃkalpanirmāṇaṃ svapno jāgradviparyayaḥ /
layākalasya bhogo'sau malakarmavaśānnatu // 290
10.d:
आत्मसंकल्पनिर्माणं स्वप्नो जाग्रद्विपर्ययः ।
लयाकलस्य भोगोऽसौ मलकर्मवशान्नतु ॥ 290
10.m: Dream is the construction of one's own imagination, the reverse of waking. / That is the experience of the soul dissolved in subtle matter (layākala) through the force of impurity and karma, but // 290

10.s:
sthirībhavenniśābhāvātsuptaṃ saukhyādyavedane /
jñānākalasya malataḥ kevalādbhogamātrataḥ // 291
10.d:
स्थिरीभवेन्निशाभावात्सुप्तं सौख्याद्यवेदने ।
ज्ञानाकलस्य मलतः केवलाद्भोगमात्रतः ॥ 291
10.m: It cannot become stable due to the absence of night; deep sleep is the non-cognition of pleasure and the like / for the knower free of instruments (jñānākala), arising solely from impurity, consisting of pure experience. // 291

10.s:
bhedavantaḥ svato'bhinnāścikīrṣyante jaḍājaḍāḥ /
turye tatra sthitā mantratannāthādhīśvarāstrayaḥ // 292
10.d:
भेदवन्तः स्वतोऽभिन्नाश्चिकीर्ष्यन्ते जडाजडाः ।
तुर्ये तत्र स्थिता मन्त्रतन्नाथाधीश्वरास्त्रयः ॥ 292
10.m: Differentiated yet inherently non-different, both insentient and sentient, are sought to be created; / the three—mantras, their masters, and sovereign lords—are situated there in the fourth [state], // 292

10.s:
yāvadbhairavabodhāntaḥpraveśanasahiṣṇavaḥ /
bhāvā vigaladātmīyasārāḥ svayamabhedinaḥ // 293
10.d:
यावद्भैरवबोधान्तःप्रवेशनसहिष्णवः ।
भावा विगलदात्मीयसाराः स्वयमभेदिनः ॥ 293
10.m: Until the entities, capable of entering within the consciousness of Bhairava, / their own essence dissolving away, and themselves devoid of differentiation, // 293

10.s:
turyātītapade saṃsyuriti pañcadaśātmake /
yasya yadyatsphuṭaṃ rūpaṃ tajjāgraditi manyatām // 294
10.d:
तुर्यातीतपदे संस्युरिति पञ्चदशात्मके ।
यस्य यद्यत्स्फुटं रूपं तज्जाग्रदिति मन्यताम् ॥ 294
10.m: Are unified in the state beyond the fourth. Thus, within that which consists of fifteen aspects, / whatever clear form belongs to whatever state, that should be considered waking; // 294

10.s:
yadevāsthiramābhāti sapūrvaṃ svapna īdṛśaḥ /
asphuṭaṃ tu yadābhāti suptaṃ tattatpuro'pi yat // 295
10.d:
यदेवास्थिरमाभाति सपूर्वं स्वप्न ईदृशः ।
अस्फुटं तु यदाभाति सुप्तं तत्तत्पुरोऽपि यत् ॥ 295
10.m: Whatever shines forth as unstable, accompanied by what preceded it, is dream of such a kind; / but that which shines forth unmanifest, whatever was prior to it, is deep sleep; // 295

10.s:
trayasyāsyānusaṃdhistu yadvaśādupajāyate /
sraksūtrakalpaṃ tatturyaṃ sarvabhedeṣu gṛhyatām // 296
10.d:
त्रयस्यास्यानुसंधिस्तु यद्वशादुपजायते ।
स्रक्सूत्रकल्पं तत्तुर्यं सर्वभेदेषु गृह्यताम् ॥ 296
10.m: Whereas that by virtue of which the synthesis of this triad arises, / comparable to the string of a garland, should be understood as the fourth [state] among all distinctions. // 296

10.s:
yattvadvaitabharollāsadrāvitāśeṣabhedakam /
turyātītaṃ tu tatprāhuritthaṃ sarvatra yojayet // 297
10.d:
यत्त्वद्वैतभरोल्लासद्राविताशेषभेदकम् ।
तुर्यातीतं तु तत्प्राहुरित्थं सर्वत्र योजयेत् ॥ 297
10.m: But that which dissolves all differentiation through the brilliance of the weight of non-duality, / they call the beyond-the-fourth; thus one should apply it everywhere. // 297

10.s:
layākale tu svaṃ rūpaṃ jāgrattatpūrvavṛtti tu /
svapnādīti kramaṃ sarvaṃ sarvatrānusaredbudhaḥ // 298
10.d:
लयाकले तु स्वं रूपं जाग्रत्तत्पूर्ववृत्ति तु ।
स्वप्नादीति क्रमं सर्वं सर्वत्रानुसरेद्बुधः ॥ 298
10.m: In the case of the knower dissolved in voidness, one's own form is waking, while the state prior to that / is dreaming and the rest; in this way the wise person should trace the entire order everywhere. // 298

10.s:
ekatrāpi prabhau pūrṇe citturyātītamucyate /
ānandasturyamicchaiva bījabhūmiḥ suṣuptatā // 299
10.d:
एकत्रापि प्रभौ पूर्णे चित्तुर्यातीतमुच्यते ।
आनन्दस्तुर्यमिच्छैव बीजभूमिः सुषुप्तता ॥ 299
10.m: Even in the single, full Lord, consciousness is called beyond-the-fourth, / bliss is the fourth, will itself is the ground of the seed, [namely] deep sleep, // 299

10.s:
jñānaśaktiḥ svapna uktaḥ kriyāśaktistu jāgṛtiḥ /
na caivamupacāraḥ syātsarvaṃ tatraiva vastutaḥ // 300
10.d:
ज्ञानशक्तिः स्वप्न उक्तः क्रियाशक्तिस्तु जागृतिः ।
न चैवमुपचारः स्यात्सर्वं तत्रैव वस्तुतः ॥ 300
10.m: the power of knowledge is said to be dreaming, and the power of action is waking. / Nor is this a mere metaphor; in reality everything resides right there. // 300

10.s:
na cenna kvāpi mukhyatvaṃ nopacāro'pi tatkvacit /
etacchrīpūrvaśāstre ca sphuṭamuktaṃ maheśinā // 301
10.d:
न चेन्न क्वापि मुख्यत्वं नोपचारोऽपि तत्क्वचित् ।
एतच्छ्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे च स्फुटमुक्तं महेशिना ॥ 301
10.m: If not, there would be no primary meaning anywhere, nor any metaphor anywhere either; / and this was stated clearly by the Great Lord in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra. // 301

10.s:
tatra svarūpaṃ śaktiśca sakalaśceti tattrayam /
iti jāgradavastheyaṃ bhede pañcadaśātmake // 302
10.d:
तत्र स्वरूपं शक्तिश्च सकलश्चेति तत्त्रयम् ।
इति जाग्रदवस्थेयं भेदे पञ्चदशात्मके ॥ 302
10.m: There, one's own form, the power, and the embodied soul constitute that triad: / this is the waking state in the fifteenfold division. // 302

10.s:
akalau svapnasauṣupte turyaṃ mantrādivargabhāk /
turyātītaṃ śaktiśaṃbhū trayodaśābhidhe punaḥ // 303
10.d:
अकलौ स्वप्नसौषुप्ते तुर्यं मन्त्रादिवर्गभाक् ।
तुर्यातीतं शक्तिशंभू त्रयोदशाभिधे पुनः ॥ 303
10.m: The two instrumentless knowers are dreaming and deep sleep; the fourth belongs to the class of Mantras and the rest; / beyond-the-fourth is Śakti and Śambhu. But in the thirteenfold division, // 303

10.s:
svarūpaṃ jāgradanyattu prāgvatpralayakevale /
svaṃ jāgratsvapnasupte dve turyādyatra ca pūrvavat // 304
10.d:
स्वरूपं जाग्रदन्यत्तु प्राग्वत्प्रलयकेवले ।
स्वं जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुप्ते द्वे तुर्याद्यत्र च पूर्ववत् ॥ 304
10.m: one's own form is waking, and the rest is as before. In the knower isolated in cosmic dissolution, / one's own form is waking, the two are dreaming and deep sleep, and the fourth and beyond are here as before. // 304

10.s:
vijñānākalabhede'pi svaṃ mantrā mantranāyakāḥ /
tadīśāḥ śaktiśaṃbhvitthaṃ pañca syurjāgradādayaḥ // 305
10.d:
विज्ञानाकलभेदेऽपि स्वं मन्त्रा मन्त्रनायकाः ।
तदीशाः शक्तिशंभ्वित्थं पञ्च स्युर्जाग्रदादयः ॥ 305
10.m: In the division of the knower free of instruments as well, one's own form, Mantras, the lords of Mantras, / their rulers, and Śakti-Śambhu—thus waking and the others would be five. // 305

10.s:
saptabhede tu mantrākhye svaṃ mantreśā maheśvarāḥ /
śaktiḥ śaṃbhuśca pañcoktā avasthā jāgradādayaḥ // 306
10.d:
सप्तभेदे तु मन्त्राख्ये स्वं मन्त्रेशा महेश्वराः ।
शक्तिः शंभुश्च पञ्चोक्ता अवस्था जाग्रदादयः ॥ 306
10.m: In the sevenfold division designated as Mantra, one's own form, the lords of Mantras, the great lords, / Śakti, and Śambhu are stated to be the five states, waking and the rest. // 306

10.s:
svarūpaṃ mantramāheśī śaktirmantramaheśvaraḥ /
śaktiḥ śaṃbhurimāḥ pañca mantreśe pañcabhedake // 307
10.d:
स्वरूपं मन्त्रमाहेशी शक्तिर्मन्त्रमहेश्वरः ।
शक्तिः शंभुरिमाः पञ्च मन्त्रेशे पञ्चभेदके ॥ 307
10.m: One's own form, the great lordly power of Mantra, the great lord of Mantra, / Śakti, and Śambhu—these are the five in the fivefold lord of Mantra. // 307

10.s:
svaṃ kriyā jñānamicchā ca śaṃbhuratra ca pañcamī /
maheśabhede trividhe jāgradādi nirūpitam // 308
10.d:
स्वं क्रिया ज्ञानमिच्छा च शंभुरत्र च पञ्चमी ।
महेशभेदे त्रिविधे जाग्रदादि निरूपितम् ॥ 308
10.m: One's own form, action, knowledge, will, and Śambhu as fifth here: / waking and the rest have been explained in the threefold division of the great Lord. // 308

10.s:
vyāpārādādhipatyācca taddhānyā prerakatvataḥ /
icchānivṛtteḥ svasthatvācchiva eko'pi pañcadhā // 309
ityeṣa darśito'smābhistattvādhvā vistarādatha /
10.d:
व्यापारादाधिपत्याच्च तद्धान्या प्रेरकत्वतः ।
इच्छानिवृत्तेः स्वस्थत्वाच्छिव एकोऽपि पञ्चधा ॥ 309
इत्येष दर्शितोऽस्माभिस्तत्त्वाध्वा विस्तरादथ ।
10.m:
Through activity, through lordship, through the cessation thereof, through impelling, / through the cessation of will, and through resting in oneself, Śiva, though single, is fivefold. // 309
Thus this path of principles has been shown by us at length. Now:
